		Foreword
		______________________________
		SCENE
			It is autumn, 2015. The world stands on the brink - undone by events decades in the making.

			In 1908, President Theodore Roosevelt made the monumental decision to seek a third term. He won that election in a landslide - his Second Square Deal reforms streamlined the American government, empowering the executive. Satisfied, he stood down at the 1912 election, and Woodrow Wilson took the reins of power.
			That same year, the Tunguska Event terrified locals. None yet knew of the true horrors to come.

			Then, in 1914, a Serbian man shot an Austrian archduke. Almost as soon as German boots crossed into Liege, the British government announced its declaration of war. American businessmen grinned unanimously, making a fortune selling guns and munitions to the Entente.
			1917 was a tumultuous year. Russia had fallen, with fighting between Socialist forces and reactionary remnants.	Yet at the same time, the Ottoman Empire fell to the Arab revolt. American soldiers landed in the trenches of Saint-Mihel, and began to turn the tide against the German juggernaut.

			By 1918, an exhausted continent signed the Treaty of Versailles.
			A wise man once said "The only fair deal is one where no-one is happy."
			A much wiser man once said "This is not a peace. It is an armistice for 20 years."

			Imperialism carried on as if nothing had happened - as if it didn't just result in an entire generation being fed into the meat-grinders.
			In Ireland, hopeful revolutionaries who had been fighting since Easter, 1916 - and 800 years before then - believed they were going to win. Their hopes were dashed by chance - a string of unlikely British victories, along with the assassination of IRA leadership, ended in a smouldering Eire with the Union Jack still flying over the ashes of Dublin.
			The Imperial Boomerang was in full effect - the Empire's totalitarianism abroad fostered totalitarianism at home. Strikes were outlawed, the nascent Labour Party was disbanded, and the British State - and its disgustingly wealthy owners - reigned supreme.
			Across the Empire, things were no different. Egypt faced a brutal crackdown and was forced under direct rule from London; Canada had prison camps built specifically for the internment of Quebecois nationalists; the colonies of Oceania were reforged into the Commonwealth of Australasia, whose first Act of Parliament was the "White Australasia Policy" and the 'pacification' of indigenous rebels; the combined Dominion of South Africa absorbed Namibia and Rhodesia, with criminals across the Empire being deported to the 'frontier' - the goal being the elimination of the Black Native as a sovereign force.
			Perhaps most dystopian of all, for the peoples of the Raj, nothing changed at all.
			In fact, the only Imperialist quagmire avoided was in Arabia. Focus on consolidation of its existing Empire meant the British had no interest in Sykes-Picot - instead viewing a unified Hashemite kingdom as a valuable proxy state. The "Hashemite Kingdom of Arabia," stretching from Palestine to Baghdad and Damascus to Sana'a, had as much independence as you could want - aside from every major corporation in the kingdom being a British, American, or French subsidiary.

			And yet, as the British Empire tightened its grip on its quicksilver colonies, and as the French struggled to reconcile Liberté, Egalité, and Fraternité with Autorité, Iniquité, and Vanité, the Russian Empire was consigned to the history books. The Russian Civil War ended in a victory for the Soviet Red Army - a coaltion force of Bolsheviks, Mensheviks, Orthodox Marxists, Radical Socialists, Liberals and Anarchists who had had a Damascene conversion, and more - all eventually coagulating into the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.
			Then, in a mansion in Gorki in 1924, Vladimir Lenin breathed his last. He was succeeded by a troika of Nikolai Bukharin, Leon Trotsky, and Grigory Zinoviev. Josef Stalin, and his Bonapartist clique, were ousted after his disastrous performance in the Polish-Soviet war - but his cronies began the work of infiltrating the state apparatus.
			The war had brought Eurasia to its knees. But thankfully, careful industrialisation, organised collectivisation, the New Economic Policies, and decentralised leadership managed to prevent a food shortage in Ukraine and Kazakhstan from becoming a full-fledged famine.

			The Great Depression shattered the American spirit, but from the ashes, Senator Huey Long built a national machine with his "Share Our Wealth" program.
			President Franklin D. Roosevelt responded with his own New Deal, but the political landscape was fractured. In 1934, the shadowy "Business Plot" to overthrow the government was exposed and thwarted by the heroic testimony of General Smedley Butler, revealing the rot at the heart of American capital.
			In 1935, a son of a judge shot Long in the chest - hitting his pocketbook. Long's bodyguard immediately slew the assassin, but the Kingfish's paranoia and megalomania only grew. Convinced of a vast right-wing conspiracy out to get him - not entirely without merit, it must be said - he knew exactly what to do. The 1936 elections were looming, and he approached FDR with a choice - Give me power, or I'll run as a spoiler.

			The Democratic Party wanted nothing to do with Long's populist policies, but Roosevelt knew he couldn't win with Long in the running - so he approached him, covertly. He expected an egomaniac who would demand the Vice Presidency for himself - but instead, he fell into the traps of a shrewd political operator.
			Long demanded appointment as head of the WPA, the key agency of the New Deal - and demanded that said appointment be made a cabinet position. He also demanded General Butler be made Secretary of War.
			Roosevelt was surprised, but agreed hastily to the terms, leading to the resignation of his Vice President, Garner. In response, Long made one additional demand - appoint Henry Wallace as VP.
			The 1936 election was won by the new administration in a landslide. America experienced a shift in politics not seen since the Reconstruction era, with increasing civil rights, redistribution of wealth, and the ascent of radical new figures.
			As the Share Our Wealth platform overtook the New Deal, America began a parallel process - economic justice, and a growing patronage network, with the Kingfish at the top.

		Roosevelt to Roosevelt
		______________________________
		SCENE
			But while the USA saw exposure of fascist plots, and the USSR saw a new age of democratic socialism, the European Continent went rabid.
			In Italy, the home of the word 'Empire,' Benito Mussolini's Blackshirts marched on Rome, forging a fascist model others were eager to follow. Their brutal conquest of Ethiopia, their genocidal actions in Libya, their annexation of Albania, and their puppeteering of Greece, made them seem like the kings of the New Order in Europe.
			That is, until another king entered the castle. In Germany, the Nazi Party rose to power on a tide of resentment, its growth fueled by a brutal campaign of street violence and a new, escalating terror campaign by the radicalized KPD. 
			Hitler was well aware of the growing resentment to capitalism, and so he used an ancient trick to Empire - blame someone else. Every rich pig in German high society was quick to blame all the problems of their robber-baronism on a secret, Jewish cabal. Antisemitism was the greatest tool of German capital - an imaginary group of devious financiers, obscuring the very real group of devious financiers, all swearing fealty to the Fuhrer.

			The Soviet Union, seeing full well the growing fascist movements, did not sit idly by like the isolationists in Washington. It provided arms and advisors to communist proxies in the Chinese Civil War and watched Poland closely, forging a pact with France in the face of British indifference to the inevitable war.
			The eruption of civil war in Spain doused Europe in gasoline. The Republican forces saw support from France and the USSR, along with tepid aid from America; meanwhile the goons of General Franco saw aid from Germany and Italy, along with similarly tepid support from Britain. At the same time, the great Polish Peasant Strike of 1937 devolved into a fratricidal free-for-all, with populist militias fighting the Sanationist regime, and infighting between the rebel forces; some gleefully accepting Moscow's support, others chafing under Soviet direction. The battle lines were drawn.
			In 1938, those lines were crossed, and the spark was lit; German forces swept into Czechoslovakia and Poland, citing border incidents with Soviet clients. That same year, the Nazi regime quietly initiated Aktion T4 - the murder of the disabled, and Phase 1 of the coming nightmares.

			Britain, under Chamberlain and fearing a resurgent USSR more than Hitler, declared neutrality. Backbencher Winston Churchill failed to mobilise a pro-war movement - none of his Tory peers wanted to fight and die for Russian Communists, and his own imperialist demagoguery made him no friends among the proscribed socialists.

			Isolated, Paris fell within months, a puppet regime installed at Vichy. Madrid followed, with direct intervention from Wehrmacht troops crushing the remaining Republican forces.
			America, under an increasingly frail FDR and a secretly-dying Butler, extended Lend-Lease to the desperate Soviets, despite the protestation of the isolationist Long. In response, German U-boats began sinking Atlantic convoys, which only enraged the American public and further wounded the Isolationist movement.
			If the Kingfish wanted to keep his crown, he needed to adapt.

			In the Pacific, Japan's hunger for empire only grew. Its proxy war in China, coupled with total humiliation in Khalkin Gol, led to the sidelining of the Army, with the immense Zaibatsu corporations backing the Imperial Navy's ambitions for Pacific dominance. The army was instead ordered to focus on China, while the 'real war' would be fought at sea. Plans were drawn up for operations to begin in Feburary, 1940.
			The resentment, along with extremist racism endemic to the army, lead to horrific atrocities across China. From sickening experiments in Manchuria that would make Frankenstein pale, to unspeakable brutality in Nanjing - if an alien force was looking at Eurasia, they'd see two increasingly disgusting genocides, spreading like wildfire.
			While the IJA committed crime after crime, the IJN struck across the pacific - first, seizing French territories in Indochina; then, taking Indonesia from the occupied Dutch; and last, attacking British and American holdings - culminating in its occupation of the Phillipines and a sponsored uprising of Hindu nationalists in the Raj - and at the same time, a shocking invasion of Hawaii.

			A vengeful Congress, shepherded by Butler, declared war on the Axis - against a U-Boat campaign in the Atlantic, and a mass-expansion in the Pacific. Long knew he couldn't fight for isolation anymore - so he, ever the masterful spin doctor, got to work re-framing the war as a continuation of his campaign against Wall Street - a fight against fat cats, at home and abroad, who would dare to threaten the American people.
			The crowds went wild. The Kingfish had done it again.
			And then, in June of 1940, Smedley Butler went to the doctor with complaints of stomach pains. It was cancer. He resigned from the administration, and spent his last few weeks at home with his family, praying that his work would be done.
			The stresses of war, a hostile underling, and rage from Wall Street, took their toll on Roosevelt. First a small stroke, then a major one, and like Wilson before him, the President was bedbound.
			Long knew the administration would be paralysed as long as FDR's heart was still beating. And so, to ensure his now-puppet Wallace could ascend to the highest office, the unthinkable was ordered. Rumours say it was Long himself who smothered the old man - but there was never any proof of foul play.

			On the Eastern Front, the full might of the Wehrmacht plunged deep into Soviet territory. The conflict became one of annihilation, and the Nazi regime's genocidal ambitions escalated into the industrialised horror of the Holocaust. 6 million Jewish people, 1.5 million Roma and Sinti, hundreds of thousands of dissidents - all burned in the charnel houses of Europe. In parallel, Generalplan Ost, and Organisation Todt, depopulated Eastern and Central Europe, as hunger policies caused famine to rip through the Bread Basket, while forced labour claimed millions of lives to feed the German war machine.
			Fascist forced mobbed outside of Leningrad, Moscow, and 'Fortress Crimea', but the Red Army, ever defiant, made the invaders pay for every inch. The German advance was finally, and decisively, broken in the ruins of Volgograd.

			The American war machine, now ruthlessly organizsd by Long's shadow network, awoke. Its first great victory was the bloody liberation of occupied Hawaii. For London, however, the Raj slowly slipping from its grasp sent a message across the Empire - "They can be beaten."
			A wave of mass strikes and demonstrations in Canada was the first sign of the British Empire's death rattle. The Governer-General authorised a crackdown on any revolutionary impulse within the country, leading to masses of refugees arriving in the Northern USA.
			The de-facto Long administration, made up of isolationists-turned-hawks, smelled blood. The American people were largely sympathetic to their northern neighbours, and so, the unthinkable happened - the execution of War Plan Crimson. American invasion of Canada.

			The invasion was swift - the US Army was welcomed into Ottawa with only token resistance. To the Canadians' horror, however, the Americans decided that independence was not their destiny - instead, the Provinces of Canada became incorporated as States. The anti-Empire movement was split - some supporting American statehood, with most demanding total independence - and a not-insignificant Loyalist minority only added further fuel to the fire.
			Losing Canada and the Raj sent a clear message across the Empire - Australasia was next, declaring unilateral independence; while South Africa threw out the British, and welcomed the Germans - becoming a non-belligerent Axis pact member. The African colonies broke free in near-unison, while the Caribbean saw American occupation replace British dominance. Ireland tried once again to break free, but the British, now no longer needing to station forces away from the Isles, had another idea.
			Driven mad by the unstoppable collapse of its Empire, and fueled by rabid hatred towards the birthplace of anti-Imperial action, the punishment of Ireland made the failed Independence War seem tame in its bloodshed. Having taken out its frustrations on the Emerald Isle, Britain sued for peace with the American juggernaut.
			Come the 1944 elections, President Long swore his oath of office to crowds of cheering supporters. Vice President Wallace stood beside him, secretly hating his puppeteering ways.

			Back in Europe, the Nazi forces floundered against the Soviet walls. Pushed back to Berlin, with uprisings across Western Europe and a looming American invasion, the Soviets decided to end this war with flair. Twice in a century, they'd faced German aggression - this time, with the crime of crimes being committed against their citizens. They were determined that the German people would never again threaten them.
			Thousands of theoretical physicists had escaped the Reich and its proxies. While a few went to America or Britain, both countries' deepening authoritarianism made a different destination appeal - Moscow.
			Codenamed the "Chelyabinsk Project," a new type of weapon was designed. It was clear that, as long as Berlin stood, the Axis stood with it. The Soviet army had lost millions in the war, and taking Berlin would only bleed them dry - and they needed troops to secure the fracturing Reich, let alone their Eastern flank.
			On the 18th of May, 1946, a single plane flew above Berlin. All anti-air defences in the city were destroyed by successive bombing campaigns - a reverse-Blitz of epic proportion. The plane flew as high as it could, and dropped a single bomb, targeted at the Reich chancellery building, and the Fuhrerbunker beneath.
			In an instant, a light beyond light engulfed the square, blinding for miles all who dared to look at it. A massive fireball swirled out, and a mushroom cloud formed above the centre of the Reich. Shockwaves ripped up the ground beneath, with famous monuments being reduced to ash, rubble, and memories.
			Not since the Thirty Years' War had Berlin seen such devastation.
			Hundreds of thousands of civilians were vaporised alongside the Reich. Demoralised and terrified, the remaining holdouts surrendered immediately. The leadership of the Nazi Party, who had merely 4 years prior been the kings of Europe, were missing, presumed dust.
			Across Eurasia, Japan failed to fight a two-front war. With Soviet troops now free to cross into Manchuria, their army folded, as the Red Flag flew above Beijing and Seoul. Terrified of Soviet occupation, the Imperial government surrendered to the Americans.

			In Washinton, the end of the war with a planet-cracking bullet point led to panic among the new elite of Long's network. Wallace's clique believed that the USSR were potential allies, and that they should secure the future of the world by formalising this alliance. Meanwhile, General Douglas MacArthur, who had grown in power and influence throughout the war, wanted to steal the secret superweapon that had melted Berlin, and use it again - on Moscow.
			Long, tired, pained, and jaded, couldn't hope to reconcile the two bitter foes. Realising his pursuit of high office was all for nothing, and his dirty tricks had only enabled the same hawkish technocrats to take the reins, the President wrote a note, placed it in his desk, and went for a walk into the woods, alone. He was never found.

			Wallace's ascent was marked by instability, with MacArthur's clique accusing him of murdering Long. Wallace managed to organise the post-war order of Europe, and stepped down at the 1948 elections, placing the keys to the Oval Office into the hands of President MacArthur, and Vice President Robert Taft. The New Deal, the Share Our Wealth project, the age of Every Man a King, was gone. In its place was the beginning of a new war.

			A very, very... Cold one.

		The Second World War
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Backed by the resentful oligarchy, America began its divine mission: to contain a socialist bloc that stretched from Madrid to Seoul.
			Europe fractured: France, Iberia, and much of the East aligned with Moscow, while Britain built a rival coalition of anti-communist states in northern Europe - the European "Democratic" Union.

			In 1962, the Hashemite Kingdom of Arabia fell to Ba'athist revolutionaries. Religious and ethnic tensions still smouldered underneath, suppressed by the watchful eye of the Party.
			China, guided by the orthodox Wang Ming after Mao's quiet ouster, threw its lot in with the Soviets. Nixon never went to China, and as it industrialised, the Soviet bloc seemed unstoppable. Even India and Arabia quietly bowed to the communist juggernauts.

			Ireland remained under British rule. Another, slighly more successful revolt, led to devolution for Connaught, Leinster, and Munster - collectively known as the Autonomy. Ulster, however, was still ruled straight from London, with gerrymandering allowing the Protestant minority to hold a majority of power.
			The Troubles never ended. The Catholic provinces had substantial Loyalist minorities, imported over by the Brits after its brutal depopulation strategy of 1944. No Irish state could be born without mass-terrorism from its Loyalist subjects - a fifth column, and a hallmark of British imperial strategy: Divide and Rule.

			Surprisingly, the two superpowers managed to avoid a nuclear arms race. Wallace had hobbled the early efforts of the so-called "Manhattan" project, while the Soviets had no interest in building superweapons instead of train lines. While both powers continued research into peaceful nuclear power, and secretly maintained a tiny arsenal of weaponry, neither openly pointed global annihilation at the other.

			Elsewhere in the nascent anti-communist bloc, the capitalist nations pursued reactionary politics to divide their working class. Apartheid carried on alive and well in South Africa. Australasia became a brutal police state, propping up puppet states in Papua and Indonesia. In the States, the Civil Rights Act of 1947 was still on the books, but was swiftly undermined by crypto-racist policies that restored segregation in all but name.

			Come 1994, Chairman Mikhail Gorbachev was ousted in a soft coup by Marshal Dimitry Kruglov. At long last, Stalin's progeny had taken the throne. The simmering rot in the Soviet state had reached its top, and Kruglov's cronies soon enriched themselves, becoming no different to the oligarchs of America they decried.
			The rest of the Soviet Bloc embraced this change, and Bonapartist leaders took power across Eurasia. In Poland, General Jaruzelski declared martial law, outlawing strikes and crushing dissent. In the Balkans, leaders like Milosevic and Boban took power in regional republics, claiming ethnic loyalty over class solidarity.
			Socialists across the globe were horrified at this shift, while separatist movements and religious extremists chafed under centralised rule.

			In 2002, mass uprisings in Derry escalated into the brutal "Bogside War." Loyalist paramilitaries, openly backed by the British state, bombed schools and massacred civilians. Britain's authoritarian grip only tightened in the aftermath - an inevitability of colonialism coming home to roost.
			Ulster Catholics decided their time was up. They emigrated - either southwards to the Autonomy, or further out to Iberia. Many ended up using their experience in seperatist warfare to aid regional paramilitaries like the ETA.

			And then, in 2009, Eurasia fell into anarchy. Continued instability, growing nationalist movements, and the assassination of Kruglov by rebels caused the mighty USSR to collapse. Its satellites followed suit - Poland came under a fundamentalist Catholic Junta, the Balkan Federation collapsed into a practical race war, and China fell into a familiar era of warlord cliques - Xinjiang, Tibet, Manchuria, Qinghai, and a weakened central remnant.

			By 2015, Britain and the United States stand as hollowed-out powers - right-wing kleptocracies where democracy is theatre, wealth is power, and resistance is futile.
			
			The world is on the verge of a new, horrifying order.
			Earth is a land of decaying empires and failed states, rotten to the core.

			The old world is dying. The new world struggles to be born.

			Now is the time of monsters.

		Time of Monsters

VOLUME - Wolves Among Sheep
	______________________________
	EPISODE - Beginnings
		______________________________
		SCENE
			The morning sun dragged itself up from the horizon, shining softly over Geneva. Cold autumnal winds swept through the World City, scattering orange leaves like glitter on a child's drawing. Zeppelins floated through the skies, while jetplanes crisscrossed above them. Down below, the people moved like ants.
			Zhao looked both ways at the small road, and crossed quickly. He pulled his coat's hem, trying to keep some warmth.
			He felt like someone was watching him. But then, he always did.
			Ahead, a large, gleaming building of glass and steel - the World Health Organisation's headquarters. Or, as he knew it: work.
			"Good morning, Eva." he nodded as he entered.
			"Good morning, Dr. Zhao!"
			The barrier slid open, and he passed through, glancing over his shoulder.
			From the outside, a noise bled in - some kind of engine running, or an abnormal wind effect. Before he could place it, a voice called out.
			"Morning, Zhao." an older, stern-faced man in a sharp suit nodded.
			"Ah, Dr. Ibekwe. Did you get those reports I sent you?"
			"I did. I must say... I thought the xeno-grehlin would've worked."
			A quiet sigh, before Ibekwe spoke again. "Back to the drawing board, I suppose."
			"I'll talk to the Director. Maybe we can--"
			"NOBODY FUCKIN' MOVE!"
			Gunshots. Lots of them.
			Shattering glass. Screaming.
			"RUN!" Zhao roared. Ibekwe froze, in blind panic.
			Zhao yanked open a door, and shoved Ibekwe through. He went to follow--
			*BANG!*
			At first, it didn't hurt. His heartbeat quickened as his eyes shot downwards. The bullet slammed into his knee, buckling it.
			Then, the pain hit. A scream ripped out of his throat, as he forced himself to see his assailant.
			"Please, I'm begging you--"
			He was answered by a rifle's stock crashing into his temple. His eyes rolled back as his conscious mind lulled.
			"Him, too." his attacker barked.
			The rough hands of another gunman wrapped around Ibekwe's wrists.
			They dragged their prizes out to the front - where a black helicopter hovered lowly.
			Captives were thrown aboard, as Zhao was hauled in.
			As the chopper took off, the lead gunman put his fingers to his ear.
			"Command, this is Delta Five-One. Package secure."
			The engines screamed as their afterburners kicked in, and the chopper tore on through the skies.

			The room was dark. An imposing man, with greying hair and a cropped beard, was illuminated by a blue screen that flickered into white. Ink-black veins jutted and tore down his cheeks, like running mascara. A nexus of these clustered around his eyes, whose steel irises glimmered in the shadows.
			"Gentlemen." he began. He spoke with a Virginian accent - and at once sounded like honey and sulphur. "Thank you for attending."
			"Commandant." an implacable voice growled from the speakers. "You have a lot of nerve."
			"Enough. What's done is done." cut in a second voice. An older, upper-class accent was palpable, even through the modulation. "I have spoken with our friends in Geneva - no further action will be taken."
			"The operation was a success." the Commandant protested.
			"Oh it was, was it?" the first voice scowled.
			"To an extent." the second added. "The... erratic nature of the attack can be worked to our advantage. Federal Police will butt heads with UN Security, and Interpol will be completely ineffective. Switzerland's tradition of direct democracy has always limited our influence... By provoking public fear, we can herd the sheep into our pens."
			"And the WHO?"
			"Placated. We've pinned the attack on the Romand Citizen's Army. What matters now is that we have Dr. Zhao again. Now he must be reminded of his... obligations."
			"Oh, he will be reminded alright... I can *assure* you of that, sir." the Commandant scowled.
			"Good. Now... continue your report."
			"Gladly, sir." the Commandant nodded. "Operations in the East have progressed smoothly. The Reds are on the back foot."
			"Excellent." the first voice audibly grinned. "Our associates in America should be pleased. Lord Oxford, how fare our proxies in the third world?"
			"Quite well, quite well." the aristocrat replied. "Western backing of the Somali coup has opened up the nation's oil reserves to our backers, and by extension, us. How about on your front, Claus?"
			"I've been keeping an eye on Renard, as requested. He's been in contact with Neumann."
			"Damn fool. You almost have to admire the balls on him." Oxford audibly grinned.
			"And how about your group, Commandant?"
			"We work ever closer to the Final Victory, sir."
			"Indeed, indeed." Claus said dismissively.
			"Don't forget who pays your wages, Commandant." Oxford added hastily. "Your... 'ideological inflexibilities' had better not impair our operations."
			"Of course not, sir." the Commandant nodded, his lip curling silently.
			"Commandant?" Claus chimed in. A hint of glee cut through the modulation.
			"Yes, sir?"
			"You are hereby ordered to cease all activities regarding the Progeny investigation. Just bring Zhao back to Drackhill, and restart production. The 'children' are off-limits."
			"Agreed." Oxford added. "The last thing we need is to provoke Neumann even further. Geneva was bad enough..."
			"...Sir." the Commandant reluctantly growled. He cut off the call, and dialed a second number.
			"Commandant!" a jovial voice exclaimed. "How did the meeting with the Board go, sir?"
			"Need-to-know basis, Morland."
			"That badly, eh?"
			The Commandant didn't reply. Instead, he called another number.
			"Commandant, sir. Mr. Morland, sir."
			"Five-One." the Commandant began. "Is everything in place?"
			"Yes, sir." the soldier audibly nodded. "Drackhill ETA is 45 Mikes. My men on the ground have moved into the field lab."
			The Commandant stroked the hairs on his chin, before taking a deep breath.
			"And the boy?"
			"We're ready to grab him, sir."
			The Commandant grinned savagely. "I'll do it. I'll meet you at the Fenrir site."
			"As you wish, sir."
			"Morland - you have your orders." he continued. "Damn the board to hell, Progeny will be mine. And soon, you shall have more supply than you can dream of."
			"Excellent, sir." Morland gleefully replied. "Hail Victory."
			"Hail Victory, sir."
			"Hail Victory." the Commandant nodded. He switched off his computer, and lit a cigar. He took a long drag, and smiled devilishly.

		Need to Know
		______________________________
		SCENE
			It was the 25th of September, 2015. A crisp, cold Friday morning.
			The sun shone in through the curtainless window, illuminating a 2-bed apartment. In one room laid a young man, with scruffy, dark-blonde hair. Strands fell across his forehead in no particular order, as though sleep itself had styled them, while a faint ginger stubble shadowed his jaw.
			Connor Barrett.
			His phone, plugged into a charger on the floor and resting on the bedside table, began to hum a pleasant-sounding tune.
			Connor groaned, and sat up, pulling the blanket off of him. He turned off the alarm, looked down at his pillow, and seriously considered saying "Fuck it," and staying home.
			Nevertheless, he forced himself to rise. He stretched out, and it felt like every joint in his body clicked at once. In truth, just his shoulders and knees.

			What?
			What?!
			WHAT?!

			The man stumbled backwards, as blood and brain shot out of the top of his head, punctuated by shards of skull. His hands reached towards his newly-folded neck for a split second, before he fell down to the ground. Gory paste rained down behind him.
			For a moment, Connor stood frozen, unable to process what he'd just done. Then, the act hit him like a wave of nausea.
			His stomach turned, and bile rose up his throat as he stared at the lifeless body. His hands trembled, slick with blood, and he felt a cold dread seep into his bones.
			He stumbled into alleyway, vomiting bright yellow.

			"Fuck..." he groaned, feeling pressure mounting under his skin - like something was going to burst out of it.
			His vision blurred and twisted. He looked back into the water, and saw the world go greyscale. And his eyes - they were almost glowing.
			Not almost. Bright enough to cast streaks across the water, like a lens flare. And the veins around his eyes - normally imperceptible - turned ink-black.
			"Gah..." he spat, blood and bile launching from his mouth. He clutched his head, and groaned in agony.
			The pressure was unbearable. It was like something inside him was trying to break free. His pulse quickened as the sensation intensified. He couldn't breathe, couldn't think - he only felt the agony of his own body betraying him.
			"Fuck... FUUUCK!" he screamed.
			For a moment, every nerve in his body seared in agony. But then... a black, tarry gel forced itself out from his skin, encasing him in it. And then it hardened, forming an exoskeletal bodysuit that covered him from head to toe. It hadened, then calfified, becoming a chitinous exoskeleton. Claws cut out from his hands, as he fell down to his knees.
			He looked back into the water, and under the exoskeleton, went even paler than before. His eyes blazed crimson.
			He felt a pounding in his chest.
			No.
			Not *a* pounding. *Two* poundings.
			He felt his chest, and quickly confirmed - two heartbeats. Twin hearts.
			He tried to pant - the way one does in such a panic attack.
			He wasn't panting. To his horror - as one lung filled, the other emptied.
			And so did the other. And so did the other.
			Four lungs. Two windpipes, even.
			As quickly as it had formed, the chitin liquefied once more, and forced itself back down through his pores.
			What was left on his skin quickly shifted and turned, slithering around him like worms on a corpse.
			He looked back into the water, and saw that he was wearing the same outfit from when he...
			When he died.
			Even the motorbike helmet had been perfectly imitated. He felt his stomach heave once more, and he desperately tore at it until it dissolved.
			That wasn't him, no. *He* wasn't *him.*
			Can't be.
			He was dreaming, of course.
			Humans don't have two hearts. Humans don't have four lungs.
			Humans aren't strong enough to kill like that.
			And he was human, right?
			Right?
			Finally, mercifully, he collapsed.

		SCENE
			Connor grunted as his conscious mind flickered like a faulty light.
			His ears pricked up, and he forced himself to his feet.
			A low, mechanical humming noise whispered above him. His eyes crept upwards, and he saw it.

			Its light moved away from the headless corpse across the street, and fell on him.
			He looked into the light, his hearts quickening.

			"TAKE AIM!"
			"Nonono, w-w--wait, wait wait..." Connor frantically gasped, holding up his hands.
			"FIRE!"
			Connor screamed in agony. The bullets slammed into his hide, and he felt his skin perforate.
			He fell down, blood pouring from his chest.
			He was dead.
			Right?
			Living people don't lie there like that, in a pool of their own blood, do they?
			So why... why in God's name were his twin hearts still beating?
			"GRRAAAAGH!" he roared, his eyes aflame. "WHAT DID YOU PEOPLE DO TO ME?!"
			The squadron ceased fire, and their eye-veins pulsed as they looked at him in horror.
			He looked around quickly, and spotted a wireframe fence further down the alleyway.
			Were he in his right mind, he'd know full well any attempt to scale it would be futile.
			But this had been a very strange evening, after all.
			He turned, and ran. He planted his foot on the wall opposite the fence, and pushed himself off. The wall cracked as he launched like a bullet, firing over it and rolling as he hit the ground.
			"Target's on the move! Go! Go! Go!" one gunman barked.
			"Sh-shit." he spat. He took a breath - through both pairs of lungs - before sprinting as fast as he could.

			Amy fumbled at the flat door's lock, before drunkenly stumbling in.
			She took a deep breath, sitting down at the sofa. Then, another breath, before she pulled out her phone.
			Trembling, she pressed call.
			"Hey, this is Connor. Sorry I missed your call. Leave a... actually, just text me, I never listen to these things." he said, audibly grinning.
			*Beep!*

			She started sobbing, choking the word again and again.
			Please.

			"Status report! Status report!" a voice barked over the radio.
			The black-veined gunman in the front seat of the car looked out, his lip curling.
			Ahead was Connor, sprinting away. They reached a crossroads, and he turned - catching himself by his hand as he skidded by a corner. The black, armoured SUV made an audible screech as it struggled to follow. Behind them, a similar car roared through.
			"Subject was able to survive the inital strike." he reported. "We are currently in pursuit. Bravo team have arrived to provide backup."
			"Received. What is the subject's vehicle?"
			"It, um... the subject is running on foot, sir."
			The radio went silent for a moment.
			"Alpha team, new orders. Run the target down."
			"Copy that."

			Connor ran as fast as he could, feeling the air roar past him. His hood fluttered in the wind, and he took a moment to dare to look down.
			"Holy fuck..." he whispered through one breath, as another came in.
			He was running about as fast as his motorbike could drive.
			He felt the air beside him distort, and turned his head.
			"Oh SHIT!" he gasped, as the black SUV slammed into him.
			Instinctively, he stomped his foot down hard, cracking into the road. Then, he swung his arm out, crashing it into the bonnet. He felt the metal bend, as the speeding car swept him off his feet.
			The men in the car frantically gripped as they made impact - it was less like hitting a human, and more like hitting a reinforced concrete wall.
			Airbags inflated. Seatbelts locked hard enough to choke. Glass shattered, and fixings snapped.
			Connor heaved as blood dripped from him - but without any conscious thought, he turned mid-air. His foot hooked under the bumper, denting it as his kick launched it upwards.
			"Control, this is Bravo One!" the other car's driver barked in horror, as he slammed on the breaks. "Alpha vehicle down!"
			"Go! Go! Go!" Bravo team's leader roared, as the men poured out.
			The car, and its quarry, flipped forwards. It smashed down into the ground, cracking its roof. It carried on tumbling, snapping its passenger's bones. Finally, it shot down, scraped along the road, and... it didn't fall. It stayed hoisted at an angle.
			"LIGHT IT UP!"
			"But sir, our men are still in there!" one gunman protested.
			"I SAID OPEN FIRE!"
			Bravo team stopped hesitating, and their muzzles blazed.
			And then, the car raised in the air.
			Connor's eyes burned crimson, as he screamed in animalistic fury. Sparks from the gunfire fell by his side, and searing petrol glowed in preparation.
			"OH FUCK!" Bravo One gasped. "HIT THE DECK!"
			Connor pushed the car in the air, spinning it, and grabbed the back axel, before launching it forward.
			"NO!" another gunman howled, as the car landed atop his.
			*FF-BOOM!*
			The concussive force of the explosion knocked Connor back. He slammed the back of his head against the road, leaving another pothole in the gravel.
			His ears rang. Every cell ached.
			He forced himself to roll onto his front, and looked.
			Burning men screamed, as they desperately rolled on the ground, trying hard to not die.
			Still, they did.
			Clinging onto the waking world like a man on a cliff, Connor slipped. The world went black once more.

		Car toss

		SCENE
			It had been a long night.
			But nights still end, and give way to dawn. The Earth didn't stop spinning, even if it felt like it had.
			Back in Belson, a man in a creased trenchcoat stood at the scene, rubbing tired eyes beneath short, receding brown hair. He had a detective's badge, a beer belly under his shirt, and stubble from too many late nights. He looked up, and let a spatter of rain fall onto his face. He closed his eyes, sighed, and looked back at the scene.
			"DI Henry Naismith, Serious Crime." he introduced himself. He wasn't a local - he spoke with a tame, but definitive Leeds accent. "What's the story?"
			"We're still not sure, sir." the FI shrugged. "Catastrophic trauma at the base of the skull. At first glance, it looks like a contact shotgun blast under the jaw, the kind where gases blow the skull apart, but..."
			"But?"
			"There's nothing. No pellets, no casing, no gunpowder residue, not even soot. The pattern of fractures and tissue disruption doesn't quite match a firearm, either. Honestly... it's more consistent with massive blunt-force trauma. Almost as if..." he hesitated, glancing back at the corpse. "As if someone punched him."
			"Punched? No, that's not possible." Naismith shook his head incredulously.
			A young south-asian woman in a PC uniform approached the pair.
			"Sorry to bother you, sirs." she said. "PC Nina Chowdhury."
			"Not at all." Naismith smiled. "DI Naismith."

			"From the state of the head, we've done a bloody good job identifying him as human." the FI snarked. "If your super's giving you grief, tell him to take it up with the FC."
			She nervously nodded.

			"Yes, sir. Just finished a placement in Mispers, now I'm on Serious Crime."
			"And as per usual, no one on SC was informed?" he raised an eyebrow.
			"Certainly seems that way, sir." she smiled.

			"As you can see, sir - no soot, no thermal damage. Not a firearm." the FI began.
			"Any connection to the gangs here?" Naismith tilted his head.
			"None that we can see. We haven't stripped him down yet - once we do, we'll check for tattoos."
			"No need." Naismith cut in. "Look here."

			"So?" the FI asked, confused.
			"1488 is a Nazi number." Naismith said nonchalantly.
			"Nazi number?" the FI pulled his head back. "How?"
			"14 for the Fourteen Words - a racist slogan. And the 8th letter of the alphabet is H. 88 - HH. Heil Hitler."
			"The Skulls do have a lot of outright neo-fascist members - especially Stoker's faction." the FI nodded. "We found a knuckleduster on his person too. We're checking for prints, see if we can ID this guy."

			She pointed delicately with a gloved hand. "These fractures - see how they radiate from under the chin? There are four clear breaks, evenly spaced. Almost the same distance as knuckles."
			For a moment the tent was silent, rain pattering on the canvas above.
			"Sorry..." she said shyly. "Looking at the numbering on his knuckles... made me notice the similarity."
			"Well spotted." Naismith nodded, kneeling closer.
			"That's why we thought it was a gunshot at first." he realised. "Fragments of jawbone broke off at such a high velocity, they cut through the brain like bullets. That's why the exit wounds look unusual."
			The FI sighed. "It makes no sense. You can't just punch someone's head off."
			Naismith didn't answer right away. He rubbed at the stubble on his chin, eyes narrowing, running the thought through. "No." he said at last. "But we've yet to find another explanation that fits."
			"Okay... so the suspect is, what, Heracles?" the FI joked.
			"Obviously not." Naismith shook his head. "No, there... there's gotta be an explanation."
			"I can go through previous case files, if you like, sir?" Nina asked. "See if there's any parallels?"
			"Good idea." Naismith nodded, before turning to the FI. "Once you find an ID, send it through. I'll see if the Hoods have anything to say about this."

			"It's our only lead." he shrugged.

			"A fist." he whispered to himself. "Fuckin' Christ..."

			His chest heaved, and he let himself look down. Beneath, a skip full of rubbish bags.

			He saw himself killing men.

			He saw blood all over his hands.

			No one was in. It was the same state he'd left it in.

			He wiped his mouth, feeling sustained somewhat. It was new to him, but it made sense. How else would he be strong enough to...

			To raise men by one hand? To regrow his skin in mere hours?
			To raise a car above his head, and launch it?
			He banished the thoughts. Regardless of what was happening to him, there were bodies out there.
			He went into his bedroom. It had clearly been slept in since he'd been gone - he always made his bed in the mornings. Instead, the bed was unkempt, with one of his pillows nested in the side. He kneeled down, and could smell Amy's perfume.
			She'd been sleeping in his bed. Cudddling his pillow.
			"God..." he whispered, a tear rolling down his face. "I'm... I'm sorry..."
			He reached for his laptop, unlocked it, and checked the date. It had been just over a week since he was taken.
			He took a deep breath, and allowed himself a smile. His sense of time was still disoriented - but the world hadn't moved on too far without him.
			He checked the news, and some headlines stood out to him.
			"MAN FOUND DEAD IN BELSON." "FIRE IN BLACKMARSH." "SERIOUS CAR CRASH IN REDBRIDGE."
			He pulled up his red hood, and headed to the Singing Horse.

		SCENE
			Back home, Connor was in his bathroom, freshening up. He looked at his reflection. He gently, gingerly placed his hand on the mirror, and sighed deeply.

			He looked back in the mirror, and confirmed they'd returned to their previous steel-grey, and the veins had faded back into his skin.
			Eager to explore this strange new perception, he closed his eyes. He focused his listening - picking up even the smallest sounds. His own heartbeats. The sound of pipes throughout his tenement block. People talking, walking, arguing, or even snoring in their own homes. Noises a human couldn't ever hear. And they were deafening. His ears would put a bat to shame.
			He covered his ears, and the sound died down. Then, another idea.
			He applied this same 'tuning' to his vision, instead. His vision had gotten better since his rebirth, but now it was stronger than even that. He could see tiny micro-fractures in the mirror. The imperceptible ridges within the ceramic sink. He looked down at his hand, and saw the fingerprints and follicles and pores with complete precision. His eyes would put a falcon to shame.
			Then, he shifted from his eyes to his nose and mouth. He sniffed the air like a dog, and instinctively, he could recognise chemical signals he'd never even perceived. The toothpaste in the tube on his sink was at least 4 months old. As for the water in the plughole, he could tell it was soft. There was a stagnant stench coming from down the pipes.
			He'd done a remarkable job of cleaning away the biley vomit and blood in the bathroom, but the lingering micro-stains railed into his nostrils. He closed his eyes, and instinctively was able to tap where the stains were, simply locating them within his mental map by the proximity of their stink. His nose would put a wolf to shame.
			Finally, he closed his eyes and ran his fingers over a piece of paper. He could feel the faint impressions of ink - and he could read it.
			Tunable senses. Useless, though, if activating them would just overwhelm him.
			That's when it hit him.
			He re-activated the synesthetic 'super-vision,' and tuned his hearing back up. The noise was strong in his ears, but... bearable.
			Why wouldn't it be? He didn't need to 'hear' the sounds - now he could just 'see' them. Auditory input data was now being handled by optical processors. Like a load-balancing server.
			He looked around. Where he had heard the noises before, now he could see them. His hearing was strong enough that he could even see the heartbeats of the people on his floor.
			He looked at one heartbeat in particular - chosen at random - and focused his attention on it. Colour returned, but only on the rippling waves he could now see. They were bright red, like his eyes were now. He looked away, and looked back - the colour was still there, calling him.
			Now, he closed his eyes. Despite the thick skin covering his irises, he could still see rather clearly. 
			At first, he assumed he was simply seeing through the skin, such was the power of his vision. But it was more than that - despite his eyes being closed, his other super-senses were defined enough to help him visualise his surroundings in lieu of sight. Even if you gouged out his eyes, the feeling of air disturbances on his skin; the tiny sounds of microscopic insects in his ears; the scent tags of chemicals in his nose. He could 'see' it all.
			The perfect hunting system.
			He shook his head, turning it all off.
			"Hunting system?" he whispered aloud. "What the fuck am I thinking?"

His super-vision activated automatically, and he saw the vibrations of his terrified prey. The heartbeat was, like before, highlighted in a blood-red glow, matching his demonic eyes.

			Inhumanity.

And I'm very proud of the man you've become. Anyway, I... I gotta go, these phones are dogshite. But still... I hope I can see you soon, lad."
			Connor's eyes teared up at the message.
			He leant back and sighed, wiping his face. He looked at his phone again, and saved the message.
			He hesitated, and then put on a pair of headphones. He played a compilation of screaming babies. The noise was deeply irritating. He got to work disassembling the clock.
			While disassembling, his irritation peaked. He struggled to loosen a fastening, and nearly broke it in his haste. He leant back, and took deep breaths.
			"Stay in control... Stay in control..." he muttered to himself. He finished disassembling the clock, and then reassembled it from memory.
			Pain. Discomfort. Overwhelming frustration. And he didn't break a fragile clock.
			Maybe... maybe he wouldn't break a fragile human, either.
			Hopeful, he turned off the noise, and called Tommy.
			"Connor?" Tommy asked, answering the phone.
			"I'll do it." Connor said firmly. He hung up. He hesitated, and headed back out.

			It was getting dark now, as Connor made it to the city cemetery.
			There were two graves he would be seeing tonight.
			The first was a wooden cross, with a hastily-made plaque on it.
			"Reece Tomlinson," it read.
			The image of Connor's punch sending shards of jaw through his brain flashed, like a fire.
			Presumably, there was no need for further forensic examination. After all, cause of death was pretty obvious.
			He stood for a momnt, as the sound of the gunshot racked into his ears.
			Soon, Steve Fletcher would be buried in a grave not too different. A local authority's wooden plaque would be all the evidence that they'd ever lived at all.
			The 'Commandant' who haunted his dreams had taken Connor away from himself - and now, the creature he had become did the same to others.
			Two humans dead at his hands.
			The others, the mutants, those freakish, black-veined spooks - he had no choice. Kill or be killed.
			But these... they didn't have to die.
			Yet, they did. Connor did that. He killed them.
			How many more?
			He walked along a little further, and came across one grave he knew all too well.
			
			LAURA SINEAD BARRETT
			4/11/1975 - 10/10/1996
			COME UNTO ME, ALL WHO LABOUR AND ARE HEAVY LADEN, AND I WILL GIVE YOU REST.
			
			19 years, to the day.
			He sat down at the grave.
			"Hey, mum." he began. "Sorry, no Vince this year... my fault."
			He cleared his throat.
			"Something happened to me, mum. Something big, something bad... And I need to know what."
			He covered his face, and had a small cry.
			Amy crouched down next to him, startling him slightly.
			"Thought you'd be here." she said softly.
			"Hey..." he whispered.
			She put her arms around him, and squeezed.
			"Sometimes..." he began, "Sometimes I wonder if..."
			"If what?" she pressed.
			"If Vince would have been happier if she never died, if... If I was never born." he said, choking back tears.
			"Don't be stupid..." Amy shook her head. "You know he adores you."
			Connor sighed. "Did I ever tell you how this tradition started?"
			She tilted her head, gesturing for him to elaborate.
			"It was on my 9th birthday - the first one I had since we moved in with him." he began. "We'd had that wee party - I'd never really had a proper birthday celebration 'til then."
			"I remember." she nodded. "Bless you, you got so confused why we were singing." she chuckled nostalgically.
			He let out a chuckle, too. "Anyway, that night, I... I caught him sneaking out. You were fast asleep, so I snuck out after him. And I found him here, just sitting at this very grave, telling her how I was getting on. He told her about how you had come along into the family, said you reminded him of her at your age... and I just walked over, like you did just now, and sat down with him. He jumped out of his skin, before explaining what he was doing. That's why... That's why every year, he always seemed like he was putting on a smile for my birthday. 'Cause, it's the same day I killed her."
			"You didn't kill her." Amy countered. "You were just... born, Connor. What happened along with that... it wasn't your fault."
			"My grandad didn't think so." Connor shrugged.
			"Yeah, well, he was a prick, from what you told me." she smirked.
			Connor chuckled. "Yeah, he really was."
			She squeezed him again. "You know, I've been here a few times, trying to see if my own mum was buried here. See if I could find out anything about her. You have Vince to tell you about yours - I ain't really got a clue where I came from."
			Connor nodded. "I'm sorry. My self-pity party could be worse, I suppose."
			"I think Trey's probably spoken to his mum's grave, and all." Amy nodded. "I wonder if we'll ever learn what really happened back then."
			"Did you hear that one guy's theory that it was some experimental drug?" Connor tilted his head. "That the big biotech company in Belson had something to do with it?"
			"Eh, it's all just rumours." she shrugged. "I heard one nutter say it was actually the Fae, trying to swap out all the fetuses for changelings."
			"Better avoid any cold iron, just to be safe."
			She chuckled. "Come on, it's getting dark. Let's go back home, and we'll have a glass of whiskey. For Vince."
			Connor hesitated, but let out a small smile. "Yeah. Let's do it."
			The pair rose, and left.

			At the same time, a man with black receding hair and a thick beard sat down on a bench outside a cafe. An older man with a cane sat next to him.
			"Mr. Sokolov." the older man nodded in a Russian accent.
			"Morozov." he replied.
			"[Have you received the correct information?]"
			"Da." Sokolov nodded. "[The trap has been laid.]"
			"[Excellent.]" Morozov smiled. Sokolov rose.
			"[Long live the Soviet Union.]" Morozov raised his fist.
			"[On with the Red Dawn.]" Sokolov nodded, before saluting back.

		SCENE
			It would have been some time in autumn 2007. Connor was ten years old, going-on-11. He was running through the fields, and a small grey Staffy ran by his heels.
			"Come on, Stella!" Connor cheered. Stella barked back happily.
			The two leapt over a stream, and continued sprinting.
			Then, Connor was an adult again, in a kevlar bodysuit, running, with a great black wolf at his side.
			"WE'RE GETTING OUT OF HERE!" Connor roared to the wolf.
			"THEY'RE GAINING ON US!" the wolf shouted back, in perfect English.
			A group of men were chasing them. Connor looked around, confused, before he found himself back with Stella all those years ago.
			"Stella?"
			She tilted her head at Connor, wagging her little tail at him.
			Connor looked around, bewildered, and he shifted back again.
			The men chasing him had caught up. They launched bolas at Connor and the wolf, knocking both down.
			"Targets secure!" the leader proclaimed proudly. His voice, his face... The Commandant. That was the name Connor's subconsciousness roared in homicidal fury.
			The wolf slipped out of his netting, as did Connor. The wolf launched at the men, mauling them.
			"GO!" the wolf shouted.
			"NO! I'M NOT LEAVING YOU!" Connor barked back, before a bullet buried itself into his abdomen.
			The two were overpowered, and dragged away.
			Suddenly, Connor woke up from this in a cold sweat. Blood dripped from his nose, and he clutched his blanket.
			"What the fuck happened to me..." he whispered to himself.
			His brow creased with determination, as he reached into his drawer. He pulled out his gun, and took a deep breath. Then he stashed it in his backpack, and headed off to the garage.

			It was still early. Connor's new 'job' along with Jake's impromptu resignation meant that the shop could only be open when Trey was free. Still, Connor had his key - and he let himself into the workshop section.
			Within, he saw the bike he'd taken from the Skulls. He hadn't got a good look at it before, but it was a pretty decent ride.
			Whereas his old bike was your typical cruiser, this one was a Japanese-style sports bike. It was sleek, and painted a shimmering black - but with thin red decals.
			He couldn't help but crack a grin - it definitely fitted *his* style better than a Skull.
			Part of him wanted to focus on that. The men he killed were scum - why mourn them?
			No.
			He shook his head, sighing.
			He pulled out the gun, and stared at it.
			The image of the Steve's perforated heart made his own two ache.
			"Never again..." he whispered.

			Across the river, a church sermon began. 11th of October, 2015 - a crisp Sunday morning.
			Father Declan began the Liturgy of the Word, turning to the book of Isaiah, as Connor got to work dismantling, pressing, smelting, and reforging the gun.

			"He shall judge between the nations," the priest said, as the gun's components were set aside.
			"And shall decide for many peoples," as electronic circuitboards were assembled and made ready.
			"And they shall beat their swords into ploughshares," as the hydraulic press flattened parts to be refolded and remade.
			"And their spears into pruning hooks," as Connor gripped hot metal with his bare hands, feeling the pain as penance.
			"Nation shall not lift up sword against nation," as he took the new parts and cobbled them together.
			"Neither shall they learn of war again," as he took a deep breath, and held his new contraption in his still-sore palms.

			A knock at the door shook him from his stupor.
			"Delivery for a Mr. Barrett?" the young man said.
			"Thank you." Connor nodded, taking the box and signing for it. He cut it open, and smiled.
			Haemostatic gel. A foam that could be sprayed over a wound, stopping someone from bleeding out. It would dissolve in hours - more than enough time to get them proper care. A lifesaver.
			He filled the device's cartridge, and held it aloft. Where he squeezed the red-hot metal, a perfect grip had formed. He pulled the trigger, and thick, orange foam hissed from the nozzle.
			He flicked a switch on the hilt, and a small needle began threading - the same way it would if it were to close a wound.
			A coagulator. A hand-portable coagulator.
			He took a deep breath. Where this metal once made holes in flesh, it would now close them. Where it brought death, it would now save life.
			His brow creased again. He was still the monster they made him. He would still have to kill, sometimes.
			But at least now, he could save too. Maybe one day, his ledger would be even again. Maybe he could leave the world with more lives saved than taken.
			Maybe, just maybe... he was still Connor. And nothing - and no-one - could take that away.

			As the church bells rang, he took a deep breath.
			It had been a while, but... well, if anyone could use some spiritual guidance, it was him.
			He headed across the bridge, and nervously entered the chapel.
			He pulled his red hood up, and kept his head down, before making his way to the confessional. He crossed himself as he passed the altar - old habits died hard.
			"Good morning, my child." Father Declan began. He had a kind voice about him.
			"Uh... morning, father." he nodded awkwardly. "Uh---forgive me, for I have sinned, or... something."
			"Heh, close enough. How long has it been since your last confession?"
			"Oof... 10 years, give or take?"
			"I see. Perhaps, then, there is something troubling you, to bring you back after so long?"
			"Something like that..." he sighed. "Listen, um... I wanna preface this by saying I don't believe in God, and I--I don't want to, either."
			"I understand." the priest said, audibly offering a reassuring smile. "The purpose of the confessional is not to make you conform to dogma - it is to help you unburden your spirit before God. Whether or not you believe in Him."
			Connor paused. "I... I'm not sure if I can say it out loud."
			"You don't have to." Declan began softly. "But I want you to understand, my job is not to sit in judgment. It is to help you on your journey of confession to God."
			he took a breath, finding the right words.
			"If it helps, don't think of Him as God, the personal Creator. Think of Him as a perfect concept - the ideal form of justice, compassion, mercy, and forgiveness."
			"Isn't that heretical?" Connor smirked.
			"So's being an atheist, but who's counting?" Declan chuckled back. Connor's shoulders loosened slightly.
			"If you believed you could talk to that form, what would you tell it?"
			He took a deep breath. "Can anyone else hear me? Besides, you know, God?"
			"No. These booths are soundproofed, and I promise you, not one word of this discussion will leave my lips. This is a sacred process, protected by the Seal of the Confessional."
			A gulp, and a long pause.
			"Perhaps it would be easier to work backwards?" he suggested. "Whatever it is you've done... how is it making you feel?"
			"Angry. Ashamed. Disgusted. I... I put a gun to my head last night."
			"A gun?" Declan half-gasped, before shaking his head. "I am sorry to hear that. What made you decide not to pull the trigger?"
			Connor cleared his throat. "I, uh... I did. By accident. I mean, I tried pulling it on purpose, but I couldn't go through with it. But then my sister called, and I..."
			Declan took a moment. "I assume, given we're speaking right now, that the gun wasn't loaded?"
			"Maybe I'm a ghost." Connor snarked, before breathing deeply.
			"Are you still thinking about taking your own life?"
			"I don't know. Not actively."
			"I understand." he smiled softly. "Why didn't you pull it on purpose?"
			"...too cowardly, I guess."
			"A coward wouldn't be sat in this booth, talking to a stranger so candidly." Declan countered.
			Connor took a moment, before the words left his mouth like a choke.
			"I... killed people."
			"...I see." Declan said after a short while. "How, um... how many?"
			"12." he sheepishly admitted. "And I'm gonna... I'm gonna have to kill more. Maybe even tonight."
			"I... why? Why did you kill them? And why do you plan to kill again?"
			"They... it was complicated." he whispered. "A few of them, it was an accident, I... I didn't mean to. I was too strong, or--or I panicked. I didn't want it to happen."
			"And the others?"
			"They..." he shuddered. "They took me away. They did... something to me. And they want to do it again. I... I don't have a choice. I have to stop them, before they hurt me again, I..."
			"My child..." Declan shivered. "This is a very serious matter. I will not tell a soul, but... you mustn't take another life. Murder is a grave sin - one of the gravest."
			"It's not--It's not 'murder.'" Connor shook his head. "They *have* to die, they--"
			"Only God can decide who deserves to die." Declan sighed. "If you believed what you did was righteous, you would not have come to this booth, correct?"
			Connor wiped his eyes, leaning back.
			"Exactly. Part of you - call it your soul, or your conscience, or the Holy Spirit, it doesn't matter - part of you knows this is wrong. My child - if these men truly seek to harm you again, then you must speak to the police. Be brave, and admit what you have done. And bring them to justice through the light - rather than damning yourself."
			"I... I don't have a choice." Connor cried. "They've twisted me up inside... made me into a freak. They're not human, I--I can't fight them without killing 'em. If they were human, if--if *I* was still human, I--"
			"My child..." Declan said sadly. "I can provide you with spiritual help, but... it sounds to me you may need psychological help, as well."
			"What?" Connor stammered. "I--I'm not crazy."
			"I never said you were. But a discussion with a professional may help you in this matter. I can happily recommend a therapist--"
			"I'M NOT *CRAZY!*" he roared, shooting his fist through the wall.
			It shattered on impact. Declan fell back, and looked up.
			Connor looked down on himself - the chitinous exoskeleton had once again erupted from his skin. Where his fist hung in the air, a pronged, claw-like gauntlet had formed over it.
			The monster within - the monster without.
			Declan's eyes were wide, and Connor heard - saw - his heart pounding.
			"Our father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name..." Declan began frantically, clasping his hands together.
			"Wait, I... I'm not gonna hurt you." Connor began. He tried to make it a soft whisper - instead, it was a savage growl.
			"Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on Earth as it is in heaven... give us this day our d-daily bread, and... and..."
			"Oh god, what is that thing?!" a woman screamed.
			"Monster! HELP!" another howled.
			"D-demon! It's a demon!"
			"Someone help!"
			"Please, God save us!"
			Connor's eyes flared in pain, and he ripped out of the chapel. He rushed through street after street, before making it to an alleyway - unobserved. Safe.
			He took a deep breath, and felt the chitin liquefy and reform into his clothes.
			He looked into a nearby window, staring at his face.
			Demon.
			Abomination.
			Monster.

			No.

			He ran his hands through his hair, and stabilised himself.
			They were still out there.
			They still needed to be stopped.
			And he could stop them.

	EPISODE - In Sheep's Clothing
		______________________________
		SCENE
			If you asked someone to draw a kindly professor, they would draw Isaac Lowenthal.
			He was an old man, probably in his late 60's - and clearly, one who enjoyed teaching enough to stick it out for this long.
			His hair was unkempt, like Einstein - and his glasses, slightly too big for his face, clashed in a funny way with his small bow-tie.
			Chloe smiled, tuning her hearing aids to the classroom soundfield system. Despite the groaning of a Monday morning, she was in her element.
			"So, class - H. I. V." he said, underlining each letter. "A true scourge of modern medicine. Our greatest weapon - the vaccine - powerless! Or, so we think."
			He smiled, and looked over the classroom.
			"I want you all to try and figure out how we could make a vaccine for HIV."
			Chloe looked up, confused. The rest of the class began writing away, or talking to each other. Chloe nervously walked over to Lowenthal, who had sat down at his desk - clearly happy to have stumped the class.
			"Um, excuse me, Professor Lowenthal?" she asked, sheepishly.
			"Yes, Miss Derrington?" he smiled warmly.
			"Um... Well, I'm a little confused - HIV is so dangerous because it targets the immune system itself - a vaccine wouldn't do anything - would it?"
			"Indeed!" he chuckled. "Don't worry, Miss Derrington - the point of this excercise is not to break biology itself. I just want to see how you all think!"
			Chloe smiled, and nodded. "Right, of course - sorry to bother you."
			"Not at all - it's what they pay me for!" he laughed. Chloe returned to her desk, and thought deeply - googling, writing notes, and chewing her pencil absentmindedly.
			After 30 minutes had passed, Lowenthal stood, and clapped his hands together, startling her.
			"Okay, class! Let's hear it. Who'd like to go first?"
			The room fell silent. Finally, one man stood up.
			"I've got an idea." he said.
			"Excellent!" Lowenthal smiled. "Let's hear it!"
			"Okay, so I think we just do what we did with cowpox and smallpox- introduce Simian Immunodeficiency Virus into the host, and get them to base their immunity off of that." he said confidently.
			Lowenthal smiled, trying to avoid looking patronising. "Well, Mr. Darvill, that's an interesting idea. Unfortunately, current understanding is that SIV-infected bushmeat was the initial cause of HIV. So, by implementing your idea, we may end up just making a new strain of HIV instead. But, A for effort!"
			He was trying hard to seem supportive. "Anyone else?"
			"Um, I have an idea!" one girl raised her hand.
			"Go ahead, Miss Ross!" Lowenthal smiled.
			"Well, how about we take HIV virions, and deactivate them, before injecting the dead virions?" she asked.
			"Ah..." Lowenthal pinched the bridge of his nose, trying his best to not seem rude. "Well Miss Ross, that is the standard way to induce immunity via vaccination. Unfortunately, HIV does not work with that method. HIV is unique because, unlike many other viruses, it requires a very specific interaction with immune cells - particularly T cells - to trigger an effective immune response. Simply using a dead virus may not stimulate a strong enough immune response, especially one that targets the virus effectively. And, live HIV is incredibly mutable. Anyone else?"
			Chloe's heart raced. She knew her answer was solid, but the thought of being wrong in front of everyone made her stomach churn. Still, she raised her hand.
			"Ah, yes, Miss Derrington?" Lowenthal asked, smiling.
			"Ah, well, sir... Um..." Chloe fumbled over her notes. She could hear quiet snickering in the background, but steeled herself.
			"I was thinking... HIV envelopes have specific conserved regions, yes? Regions that are unlikely to mutate without making the virus unviable?"
			"Go on?" Lowenthal asked, intrigued.
			"Well, those conserved regions would have antigens, right? And, well, antigens have antibodies matching them. I'm thinking, we introduce only those conserved region antigens, along with a bunch of matching monoclonal antibodies. Doing so, hopefully the body could learn to produce those antibodies. If that worked, you would only need to take ART maybe, only weekly or monthly? That'd be a godsend for people in more developing countries. Of course, the challenge would be isolating the conserved antigens and ensuring the monoclonal antibodies are broadly neutralising across HIV strains..." she continued.
			Darvill muttered under his breath "That's not a vaccine."
			Chloe paused, trembling.
			"Miss Derrington..." Lowenthal began, awestruck. "Absolutely brilliant!"
			Chloe breathed a deep sigh of relief, and allowed herself a smile.
			"Amazing!" he continued. "That is a very good idea. You not only provoke an immune response, but actively improve care outcomes for the people in most need."
			Chloe smiled, and returned to her seat. Once the lecture finished, she grabbed her bag and went to leave, along with everyone else.
			"Oh, Chloe?" Lowenthal asked.
			"Sir?"
			"Do you have a minute?"
			"Yes, of course." Chloe smiled, sitting down.
			"I've been giving it some thought - I think it's a waste having you in this classroom." he said.
			"I... Sorry, sir, I know the objective was to come up with a vaccine idea rather than treatment, but I just thought--" Chloe began.
			Lowenthal raised his hand. "Oh no, dear - your idea there was brilliant. No, I fear *you're* wasted in this lecture hall! You're far beyond the rest of the class."
			"Sir?" Chloe asked, still timid.
			"Have you ever heard of a company called 'Vitalis?'" Lowenthal asked. "They're a medical research company."
			"I... Yes, sir, I've heard of them. Their head office is in Belson, isn't it?"
			"I'm going to put in the good word, and see if we can get you a work placement there." Lowenthal smiled.
			"You will?" Chloe gasped. "Sir, I... Vitalis is such a big, successful company - are you sure I'd be any good there?"
			"Absolutely." Lowenthal nodded. "The placement would be for three days a week. Working there will count towards your academic credits here, as well. And, you'll get paid!"
			"Sir, I..." Chloe thought for a moment. "I'd be honoured." she smiled.
			"Excellent." Lowenthal smiled back. "Take care now, Miss Derrington."

			Disgusted with himself, he went outside. There, the bike sat ready for him. He'd modified it a little - tuning up the engine, taking off the reg plates - but most of all, when he hopped on and turned his keys in the ignition, the headlights - replaced with thin striplights that looked like squinting eyes - blazed red in the night.
			He took a deep breath, centring himself. His gloves rippled as the blood slipped away.

			His eyes turned crimson behind his tinted visor, and they shone through the plastic, like LEDs in a glass bulb. His jaw clenched, and the bike roared as he tore off.

			"No, nothing. Managed to find whatever he was pushing on 'em, though - some kind of syringe."
			"Probably the steroids Stoker was freaking about." Tommy shrugged. "How was the fight?"
			"Not as bad as last time." Connor began. "Only killed one person - he was enhanced, like me - but weaker. I didn't have much of a choice."
			"You had *no* choice. What about the others?"
			"They're hurt, but they'll live. I've, uh... I'm getting better at holding back."
			"That's good."
			"Yeah." Connor nodded. "Also, I took one of the syringes with me."

			As the morning sun rose over the valley, it gave only a sliver of light to the people below - for dark, rainy clouds had gathered, as if in jest.
			Despite the damp, Connor sat atop his block of flats. Legs crossed, eyes closed - almost meditating. Black veins raied over his eyelids and down to the top of his cheeks.

			Echolocation. He chuckled, and turned it off.

			"Kinda! Try it. Use your throat." Connor nodded encouragingly.

			Turns out, tracheotomies are easy enough if you can see every vein in a man's neck.
			The next breath was better. Not good, but better. Connor rose, and shuffled over to the bar.

			"Am I becoming one of them?"
			Connor shuddered, pulling up his mask to expose his mouth, and taking a long drink from his pint. The bitter taste did little to wash away the gnawing sense of guilt.
			Suddenly, the door crashed open. Police officers stormed into the pub, assault rifles raised.
			"For fuck's sake!" Connor growled under his breath, tossing the pint aside and diving out the window in one fluid motion. Glass shattered as he leapt, just as bullets tore through the air, filling the space he had just occupied.
			He landed in the alleyway below, but the officers were quick to follow. Connor sprinted, instinctively grabbing onto a nearby wall. His fingers latched onto it, and for a moment, he just stood there, eyes wide in realization.
			He looked down at his gloved hands. The costume had morphed a special adhesive, allowing him to scale the wall with ease. Without a second thought, he began to climb, moving up the building like a moth.
			As he reached the top, he took one last glance down, ensuring no one was close. He caught his breath, before sprinting across the rooftop, disappearing into the night.
