			Before another minute of victory could pass, the moment was killed.
			"ARMED POLICE! SHOW ME YOUR HANDS!" Naismith roared.
			"Oh, look! More pigs!" Connor quipped. His and Sparky's armours thickened, as they bull-rushed forwards, knocking the officers down.
			Naismith stumbled to his feet, frantically giving chase--no. They were already long gone.
			"Jesus Christ..." he spat, before heading back downstairs.
			"This... is a lot to process." Nina shuddered.
			"Hey, leave it to the NCA. They wanna deal with the paperwork here? Let 'em." he chuckled darkly.

			"Why didn't you kill him?" Sparky asked, as the two arrived in the city's outskirts.
			Connor paused for a moment. "Because people like that... they're not responsible for what they're doing, not really. Okay, he hurt a lot of people - but from his perspective, he was saving sentient beings that were being tortured and murdered. And he was ill."
			"We need to find out who changed his face." Sparky nodded. "That's the real criminal here."
			"Agreed." Connor nodded. "Now... we'd better go on patrol."
			"Ugh..." Sparky groaned.
			"Fair's fair."
			"You got all the cool fighting! I had to play sheepdog with a bunch of things that very much weren't sheep!"
			"How do you think I feel? It's gonna be a good week or so before I can stomach a bacon sarnie again."
			The two locked eyes, then burst into laughter.
			At the back of Connor's mind though, a gnawing feeling persisted.
			Why wasn't he horrified? Why wasn't he in shock?

			Why was this normal, now?

		Porky Pies
		______________________________
		SCENE
			The final notes of the organ faded into silence. Father Declan stood at the altar, watching the last few parishioners filter out into the cold night air.
			Danny, a boy of perhaps twelve, moved through the pews with practiced efficiency, collecting hymn books and straightening kneelers.
			"Come now, Danny." an older woman began. "I'm sure our dinners have already gotten cold."
			"Oh, I--" Danny stammered. "I offered to help Father Declan close up."
			"Did you, now?"
			"Yes." he smiled. "If I'm going to be a priest when I'm older, I'd better get used to this kind of work."
			"Well, the best priests always listen to the nuns." Declan smiled, approaching. "Don't worry, Mary - I shan't keep him long."
			She chuckled. "Well, I'm here anyway. I'll sort the collection money in the office."
			"You'd better not pocket any!" Danny grinned cheekily.
			"Wicked boy!" Mary gasped, before giggling. "A good priest never makes unsubstantiated accusations."
			"Also, don't think this gets you out of homework." Declan smirked.
			"Aww!" Danny groaned, before heading off to put out the candles.
			The church fell quiet. The only sound was the faint hum of the heating system and the soft squeak of Danny's shoes.
			"Father? Can I ask you something?"
			Declan hung his sermonal vestments on a hanger, before turning to the boy. "Clearly, you can. You just did."
			Danny rolled his eyes. "May I, then?"
			"Of course you may." Declan smiled.
			"The man in the confessional. The one who... you know."
			He gestured vaguely at the refurbished confessional booth.
			"Danny..."
			"Was it true? Was it really a monster in there?"
			"Daniel." Declan said firmly. "You know full well, anything that happened in that booth was between the penitent and God. And all of it is protected by the Seal of the Confessional."
			"I know..." Danny sighed. "But... does that happen often? When I become a priest, will it happen to me, too?"
			Declan took a breath, before kneeling down.
			"Listen... sometimes, people who are... deeply troubled, will come to the booth seeking help; from you, or from God. And sometimes, sadly, deeply troubled people can lash out. It's not for us to sit in judgement on that - only to help them, to the best of our ability."

			The door swung open.
			Declan looked up, expecting a latecomer. Instead, six figures in black tactical gear marched down the centre aisle. Their eyes were dark with pulsing veins.
			Declan's blood went cold.
			The leader pulled down his balaclava, and smiled savagely.
			"Father Declan. We need to talk."
			Two of his men grabbed Danny. Another dragged Sister Mary from the sacristy, her hands bound.
			"Take your hands off him!" she shouted.
			The leader ignored her. "The Werewolf came to you. He told you things. I want to know what."
			Declan gulped. "I---I can't. The Seal--"
			A stike to the face stopped the sentence from finishing.
			"I don't give a fuck about your rules, Chaplain." the leader barked. "Talk."
			"...you'll have to kill me." he defiantly scowled.
			"Okay. Okay." the leader nodded. "Number Four?"
			"Yes, sir?"
			"On the count of three, shoot the boy."
			"Sir."
			"NO! No, please don't!" Mary screamed, as Danny froze in terror.
			"Her next. One."
			"Please! Please don't do this."
			"Two."
			"ALRIGHT! I'll talk." Declan barked, ashamed.
			"Thank you." the leader grinned. "So?"
			"He... he told me he'd killed 12 men, and planned to kill more. He said people had taken him, and... twisted him inside. And that they were going to do it again."
			"Anything else?"
			"No, I swear."
			Number Four pulled the hammer on his gun.
			"As God is my witness, I swear."
			"Very well." the leader grinned. "Alright boys - take aim."
			"NO! Please, shoot me if you must, but let them go!" Declan roared.
			"Oh, lookie here! A good old fashoined matyr! There's comfier ways to sainthood, Chaplain."
			The leader drew his pistol, smirking devilishly.
			He pulled back the slide, loading the round.
			Declan closed his eyes.
			He fully expected that, when they reopened, he'd be in hell.
			But there was one "demon" that wasn't having that.

			*DING-DONG, DING-DONG. DING-DONG-DING-DONG!* the church bells rang, the noise ripping through the air.
			The Agents raised their weapons, flashlights on.
			"Come out!" the leader barked.
			A laughing noise - a guttural, demonic laughing noise cackled through the hall.
			Connor darted from rafter to rafter, his twinned windpipes flexing.
			One kept the laughing, while the other began to speak.
			"Deliver the poor and needy. Rid them out of the hand of the wicked." he recited.
			"So... you betrayed your true purpose, to become a preacher boy? Is that it?" the leader snarled.
			The laughter wouldn't stop. The other voice continued.
			"I will be merciless, and punish them in anger. And when I exact vengeance, they shall know that I am the Lord."
			The words boomed throughout the chapel, as the laughter grew more unhinged.
			"LIGHT HIM UP!" the leader roared.
			The Agents' guns erupted in a hail of fire, as bullet after bullet dug into the rafters and ceiling.
			"Cease fire! Cease fire!"
			The Agents frantically searched with their flashlights, looking for their prey.
			Declan had knee-walked over to the others - and, like true Catholics, it seemed he and Mary were competing for who would be the human shield.
			"Circle formation! Back to back! Don't let him get the drop on us!"
			The Agents quickly moved into position, searching through panicked breaths.
			In the middle of the circle, a large metal grate stood. Its purpose was to drain mopwater from the church floor, as well as provide easy maintenance access to the supply pipes.
			Humans weren't meant to fit in there. Indeed, the only real access point within the Werewolf's reach was another gutter on the upper floor, which connected to a chute that brought dirt and soap down into the wider drainage network.
			And yet... hypermobile joints, combined with a pain tolerance that thought nothing of dislocating one's shoulders...
			"The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance."
			At that, the grate burst open, and a red-eyed demon roared out.
			The Agents turned quickly.
			Not quickly enough.
			Connor's first strike disemboweled Number Four. The second took off Number Six's head. The third was a slice, then an impalement stab, over Number Two's chest.
			The Agent's guns roared for a split second, before uselessly clicking.
			"DAMN IT! RELOADI---" Number Five barked, before a wristblade turned his throat into set dressing.
			Connor turned quick, sending his blade upwards. It stabbed upside Number Three's head, poking out the top of his skull. A quick rip tore the head off surprisingly cleanly.
			Finally, the leader drew his machete.
			"Come get some, Traitor!"
			Connor's eyes blazed, as he charged.
			The leader's swipe slashed open his throat.
			Usually, that ends a fight.
			Oh, the fight ended, sure.
			The leader's shocked expression quickly went vacant, as Connor's blades drove into his ribcage. Then they swept out, and the gory paste that was once a Super-Agent fell to the floor.
			Connor huffed. Heaved. He pulled out his Coagulator, and quickly sprayed his neck with it.
			Then, he breathed properly again.
			"Are... are you..." Declan gasped, pale. "Are you alright?" he finally spluttered.
			"You mean, apart from the unwanted tracheotomy?" Connor would've quipped. Instead, he let out a rasp, before sighing - well, "sighing," and putting a thumb up.
			"I... I'm sorry, I... I'm so sorry." Declan cried.
			Connor put a gentle hand on Declan's shoulder, then patted it. He turned, and saw Mary and Danny looking up at him.
			Mary was pale as a sheet. All her knowledge of theology couldn't prepare her for this.
			Danny, however, looked up in awe.
			"Are you... Azrael?" he asked.
			Connor chuckled. The Angel of Death. Incidentally, not recognised as such by the Catholic church - Danny was a heretic in the making, it seemed.
			And yet, it was clear the child meant no harm by it. To Danny, his saviour was a monster - a holy, righteous monster.
			Connor heaved a bloody breath, stepping forwards.
			The wounds from Pig Head's wrath had reopened in the carnage. He was supposed to be dead.
			Indeed, he walked through the valley of the shadow of death.
			No one was with him. Neither rod nor staff comforted him.
			But as his crimson eyes dimmed, and he melted into the night, he feared no evil.

		Last Rites

		SCENE
			The afternoon sun fluttered through Connor's window - before a cloud choked it away.

			"Hi! Hello Chloe! I missed you!" Sparky said, rushing up to her.

The valley's bedrock is mostly clay and limestone, which is perfect for tunnelling. That's also why the inner city has so many high-rises - there's a surplus of building materials, and space comes at a premium the closer you get to Caldermouth. During the Great Depression, there was a public works scheme where they just built a shitload of tunnels for various purposes. Plenty of older houses' basements still join into them, and most major car parks are built underground. There were plans for a metro line in the 50s, but--"
			"Nerrrrd." Amy snarked. "Besides, he's underselling it. No one calls it 'the old tunnel network.' They call it..."

So they built this massive pipe network, taking fresh water straight from the Calder into a network of public fountains. But if a pipe sprung a leak, they would have to dig up the entire road to get to it - so they instead made these tunnels for easier maintenance access--"

They had tiny little lamps made of animal fat, and they had to crawl on their bellies. The smell of burning fat would attract packs of hungry, oversized rats..."

			"You guys have some very overactive imaginations." Bea grinned.

			"And the Sewer People were born." Trey shivered. "Their skin is so white, it's like chalk. Their eyes are all black, and bulging like fish. And their claws - perfectly evolved for digging - are sharper than swords."

The tunnels connect you to plenty of old underground structures and abandoned lower levels, and a lot of them just need a bit of jury-rigging to get power to them. For a lot of homeless people, it's better than sleeping on the street. Which says a lot about the state of this city, really."

			"Ugh, I get enough of those at uni." Bea groaned. The gang chuckled, and refilled their drinks.

	EPISODE - Crusades, Unending
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Autumnal evenings in Drackhill were often grim, and tonight's, it seemed, would be no different.
			The sky gods had clearly decided to add some variety to the valley's night - you could almost feel their laughter as hail crashed down from the heavens.
			Despite this, the city still needed its monstrous heroes. No rest for the virtuous, it seemed.

			"*DIE!*" Connor screamed, delivering his wristblade right into a battered Super-Agent's heart. At the same time, Sparky's jaws tore the head off another, while a satisfying *KK-BOOM!* noise punctuated Ivan's sniper fire.
			"Command, this is Zulu 7! We're pinned down here! Need reinforcements!" one Agent barked into his radio, just before the twin Werewolves pounced on him. In moments, they reduced him to paste.

			Just outside the city, in an armoured van, sat a radio operator, hearing the screams of his Agents. The black veins around his eyes darkened with mutant adrenaline.
			"HQ, this is Command Post 8-4. Request deployment of Crusader unit."
			"HQ copies. Crusader unit en-route."

			The bullet slammed right into Connor's head, making his ears ring as he stumbled backwards.
			The shooter grinned, but not for long - Ivan's return fire made his head pop like a grape.
			"Connor! Are you okay?" Sparky asked, rushing over.
			"I'm fine, buddy." Connor smiled, forcing himself to rise. "Looks like that's all of them."
			"Nice work, tovarishchi." Ivan praised over the radio.
			The hail came down heavier, now, as the ruins of the field post fell eerily quiet.
			"Come on, let's see what they've got." Connor beckoned, as the trio advanced into the site. Upon entering, they saw a host of crates.
			The two Werewolves sniffed the air, and nodded.
			"Serum." Connor noted. "Shitloads, too."
			"Enough to build an army." Ivan said grimly, stroking his beard. "I'd love to know where they get it from."
			"It's our blood." Connor shrugged. "Or at least, it smells like it. There are certain scents that normal blood doesn't have. The Agents have the same smells, just in a smaller amount. God knows where they're getting our blood from, though."
			"Fascinating..." Ivan cocked an eyebrow, before cracking a crate open. "But even aside from that... where are they getting the soldiers from? It's not like we're fighting Afrikaners - these aren't Paladin mercs, they're locals."
			"Two options, I guess." Connor began. "Either they're Skulls, or former British soldiers themselves."
			"God knows." Ivan sighed, before placing down some C4 charges. The trio cleared the room, and Ivan pulled his detonator.

			Immediately, the post went up in smoke, before the flames died down. The smell of burning mutant blood filled the air, and the two Werewolves grimaced.
			"Good work tonight, you two." Ivan smiled. "We'd better scram, before the police show--"
			Before he could finish, an ATV ripped into the site. Its rider - a Super-Agent encased in a metallic exoskeleton - hopped off.
			The three immediately re-assumed their fighting stances.
			"Who the hell are you?!" Connor barked.
			He was answered by the iron warrior raising his arm, pointing a wrist-mounted gun right at him. It fired something - too big to be a bullet - right at him. Connor dashed out of the way, avoiding a direct hit, only for the world to turn red and fiery.
			A grenade. Their attacker had a grenade launcher built into his arm.
			The blastwave rocked Connor's bones against his musculature, while Sparky dug his claws into the mud beneath and skided a pace away. Ivan hit the deck, before rolling down the hill and darting into cover.
			"Good evening, traitor." the Agent smirked under his helm.
			Connor coughed and spat blood, before rising. His suit rippled and tore, hardening into chitinous spiked armour, and claws. His eyes flashed red, ready for the kill.
			"Let's kill this guy already!" Sparky barked, likewise shapeshifting.
			"Couldn't agree more." Connor nodded, before the pair charged.
			The Agent snarled, and drew something from a sheathe on his hip - a blade. As Connor entered melee range, he swung.
			Connor's senses slowed to a crawl as the agony ripped into his arm. This wasn't a normal blade - its edge oscillated at ultrasonic frequency, sawing into his flesh. At the same time, an electric current coursed through it, which danced across his skin before jolting in, sending scorching pain straight into his neurons.
			Were Connor his usual self, he'd crack a joke about what kind of insanity must have driven the creation of this device - some bastard child of a chainsaw and a stun baton, squeezed into a machete - but instead, he howled in unimaginable fury. He delivered a strike to the Agent's chest - one whose movement through the air made an almost booming noise through sheer force - and it landed right on the Agent's breastplate. He felt his knucklebones crack, as they pushed hard enough to leave a noticable dent in the metal chestpiece. To his dismay, he watched the force radiate out through the metal and settle in the edges of the piece, leaving the Agent's ribcage - and heart - uninjured.
			The Agent skidded backwards from the force of the hit, and swung his blade down, flinging the chunk of flesh it had torn from Connor's arm to the ground. It made a sickening squelch as the red mush became one with the black mud. The blade hummed, almost hungry for more.
			A hail of gunfire slammed into the Agent's cerametallic carapace, each bullet either ricocheting or skimming off.
			"Yob tvoyu mat..." muttered Ivan, holding his SMG and scowling.
			Sparky howled in furor, and pounced at the Agent. He shoved him to the ground, and pinned him down with his paws.
			Connor rushed over, and delivered a stomp to the helmet. And another. And another.
			At the fourth stomp, the world went pitch black, and he felt his body betray him.
			From his vantage point, Ivan watched in horror as the electromagnetic pulse crackled through the air, and his comrades convulsed and collapsed.
			"Chyort!" he gasped, holstering the SMG and pulling his sawn-off shotgun from his rifle. He charged forward, and delivered both barrels into the Agent's centre mass. The Agent fell backwards, dazed but otherwise unharmed.
			The Werewolves struggled to their feet, beaten but not broken. Their eyes flashed a deep blood-red, and they caught their breath.
			At that, a convoy of ARVs pulled up at the site. Officers in tactical gear poured out.
			"Blyat..." Ivan cursed, pulling down his balaclava.
			"ARMED POLICE! DROP YOUR WEAPONS!" their leader roared.
			The Agent grinned sadistically under his helm, and aimed his grenade launcher at them.

			"Hm, I suppose you're right. Anyway, I'm way, *way* too sober right now." she grinned, opening up a cupboard full of alcohol. "Got these in case Bea and I were gonna have a girl's night one night. Fancy any vodka?"
			"Hah, yes please." he chuckled. "You prefer vodka, don't you?"
			"Vodka and cola is my go to." she grinned. "Not that I mind other spirits, that is..."
			The pair sat down on the sofa and began drinking. Sparky flopped down at their feet.
			"Haha, bless him." Chloe smiled warmly.
			"Out like a light." Connor chuckled.

			"Okay, let's play a game. It's called 'two truths and a lie'. I'll say 3 things, only one of them is false. You've gotta figure out which one's false."
			"Haha, okay, go for it. I'll warn you, I'm very good at picking out liars." Connor smirked.
			"We'll see." she replied, raising an eyebrow and smirking back. "Okay. I won the polo competition at my school, I've travelled to every continent bar Antarctica, and I'm type-1 diabetic."
			Connor thought for a moment. "Wait, aren't polos a mint?"
			Chloe burst out laughing. "It's an equestrian sport."
			"Oh, right..." Connor said, bashfully. He breathed in deep through his nose. "Okay, well... I'm still going to say the polo one is the lie."
			Chloe blinked, surprised. "Really? What makes you say that?"
			"Well, the continent one just seemed too unlikely to be a lie, your bag has a very, very faint smell of insulin coming from it, and, well, my school didn't have 'polo,' so..."

			"Not strongly. My nose is very sensitive anyway, and one of my foster-carers was diabetic - it's a distinctive smell, if you know it."
			"Hm." Chloe replied, deep in thought. "Well, you were right - I never did polo." she chuckled.
			"If it makes you feel better, neither did I. Pretty sure I've had Polio, though." he quipped. They both laughed.

			"USA, France, Brazil, Egypt, Japan, Australia." she checked off.

			He chuckled. "Wish I was as well-travelled."
			"Anyway, your turn. Two truths and a lie. Make it a good one!" she grinned, pouring a fresh drink.

			"Oooh..." Chloe thought aloud. "Well, the Ireland one is true."

			"It's okay. I was only little - as a kid, you think the whole world revolves around you. I mean to an extent, it does, doesn't it? Everyone waits on you, feeds you, clothes you, wants to care for you... well, not everyone."

			Connor nodded. "I get the whole 'family treating you differently' thing, by the way." he said quietly. "My grandad used to treat me like dirt when I was growing up. Especially because it took so long for me to start speaking - all the other kids would be singing along their choirs and prayers, and I'd just be sat there. Needless to say, in such a heavily Catholic community, that didn't go down well. Eventually, he just stopped bringing me."

I had a bad stutter growing up, but I went to a speech therapist to 'fix' it." she explained, putting 'fix' in scare-quotes. "You've probably noticed my lisp, as well. Ah, the joys of being hard-of-hearing."

			He grinned. "I learned it when I was little. When I'd get upset, I'd go mute - but for some reason, I could still sign. So, that's how I'd communicate. My uncle, bless him - he took a whole course just to become fluent for me."

		Day in the life

			Another Agent charged from the side, but he anticipated the attack, sidestepping and landing a crushing blow to the back of the man's skull. Fragments of bone tore through his brain, and he squirmed, then went still.

		Bats Out Of Hell
		______________________________
		SCENE
			The tunnel opened up into a wider chamber - an abandoned metro station that had clearly been reoccupied.
			One door in particular stood out - it was lit. A keypad stood next to it, providing a tiny shimmer of light within the pitch darkness.
			"Great. Any idea for the code?" Sparky grinned.
			Connor peered in, his eyes blood-red.
			"Yeah, actually. Four keys are more worn than the others."
			"Really?" Sparky grinned. "That works. Any idea what order they're in?"
			"Nah. But hey, there's only 24 possible combinations."
			"Boring!" Sparky chuckled, before slamming the door open with a strike.
			"...that works too." Connor laughed, as they entered.
			"Intruders!" a Super-Agent sentry barked. He readied his gun, and Connor responded with a quick-morphed crossbow bolt to the eye.
			His partner fared no better, as Sparky's claws cut into his abdomen. Connor decapitated his own prey, while Sparky took out his throat.
			"This is definitely the place." Connor nodded grimly.
			Inside, the lab was a converted maintenance space - pipes ran along the ceiling, and the walls were lined with medical equipment.
			Before they could take in the sights, however, they felt a thundering charge towards them.
			"Oh grand." Connor groaned. "Another monster."
			A nearby door gave way - as did the wall around it. The pair threw up their guards, but were launched back into the metro. As they rose, they saw their attacker, and shuddered.
			"Fee, fi, fo, fum." it chuckled menacingly. It was huge - at least 8 feet tall - and broad too. Its eyes were black-veined, and it wore a massive version of the standard Super-Agent getup.
			"What the fuck are you?" Connor gasped.
			The Giant didn't answer - instead, it charged again.
			The two Werewolves moved as one - Connor diving low, aiming for the Giant's knees, while Sparky launched high, claws extended toward its throat.
			The Giant's eyes tracked them both, and it moved.
			Connor's strike connected with the Giant's left knee - and it was like punching a concrete pillar. For the first time in a while now, his fist *hurt.*
			The Giant didn't even flinch. Instead, it grabbed Sparky mid-pounce, catching the wolf by the scruff and hurling him into the far wall. Sparky hit with a sickening crack.
			Connor roared, surging forward.
			He threw everything he had into a barrage of strikes - jabs to the gut, hooks to the ribs, a spinning elbow that caught the Giant across the jaw. His wristblades carved shallow trenches across its chest.
			Then, the behemoth sent a backhand that cracked the air.
			Connor felt the impact crash into his ribs, as they bent under the force. He sailed through the air, smacking into a concrete wall. He fell down to the ground, as pebbles followed him.
			The urge to kill grew. Connor slapped his ear, annoyed more than disagreeing.
			The Giant laughed - a wet, grinding sound.
			Connor forced himself to his knees, spitting blood. His eyes blazed red. Then, he pounced again.
			The Giant sent a haymaker that Connor barely dodged. His response was a slash to the gut - one that left a thin red line over the monster's abdomen.
			Not enough. Not nearly.
			The Giant grabbed him by the ankle, swinging him like a child's toy. Connor slammed into a metal cabinet, the impact rattling his bones. He bounced off, hit the floor, and rose again.
			"Sparky!" he barked. "Now!"
			Sparky rose, blood streaming from his muzzle, his eyes aflame. He launched himself at the Giant's legs, claws raking across its tendons.
			The Giant stumbled, roaring in fury. Connor pressed the advantage, driving his blade into its chest, carving toward the heart.
			It worked. His blade punched into the monster's heart.
			So *why the fuck didn't it die?!*
			Under the mask, Connor went pale. This thing had two hearts - just like him.
			The Giant grinned, spat blood, and caught him by the throat.
			Its grip was iron. Connor's windpipes buckled, his vision blurring at the edges. The Giant rose, lifting Connor off the ground, and twisted. The tendons in his neck screamed. Any second now, the vertebrae would start to snap.
			"Any last words?" the Giant sneered.
			Connor's jaw unhinged, as one windpipe sang. The other choked out three words.
			"Right behind you."
			Behind it, the tunnel filled with leathery wings and crackling blue light.
			The bat-creatures descended like a biblical plague.
			The Giant dropped Connor, and swatted a few away. More came. They latched on, taking chunks of red meat and globules of hot blood with each bite.
			Tasty, it seemed. Very nourishing.
			The Giant screamed as electric stinger-tails whipped at its hide. Connor dragged himself away, letting the swarm do the work.
			Sparky rose, his eyes blazing. He charged through the chaos, lunging at the Giant's exposed throat, claws extended.
			The wolf's jaws snapped around the Giant's throat. Then he twisted.
			The Giant's head came free with a wet, grinding sound - like a tree limb tearing from its trunk. It hit the floor with a wet thud, rolling to a stop at Connor's feet. The body stood frozen for a long moment, like it hadn't quite realized it was dead, before collapsing with a thunderous impact.
			Sparky landed beside the corpse, panting, his muzzle painted with black blood. He spat out a chunk of flesh and looked at Connor, his eyes still glowing.
			"I hate this job," he wheezed. "I really hate this job."
			Connor laughed - a ragged, desperate sound - and clapped his packmate on the shoulder. "Come on. The lab's just ahead."
			They left the Giant's body to the bat-creatures, who greedily devoured their well-earned meal.
			Connor ripped a flaslight from an Agent's corpse, and led the way.

			Deeper, now. The pair's red gazes came across their target - a cluster of heartbeats.
			A pit. The lab rats were being kept in a pit.
			"Please... no more..." one weakly groaned.
			"Don't hurt us... please..."
			"I'm sorry... I won't scream anymore..."
			"It's okay." Connor said softly, kneeling down. "Let me help you, please."
			"Another trick?" one whispered.
			"Don't... don't do it..."
			But one timidly approached. His eyes were pained by the light - as if he hadn't seen it in far too long. He was flithy, and scabbed, and emaciated - but alive. Gingerly, he took Connor's hand.
			"Come with me, please." Connor whispered. "I'm one of you, okay?"
			"How can we know that?" one asked.
			Connor paused, before dropping into the pit, and placing their hands on his chest - one on each heart.
			They gasped, before nodding. Then, one by one, they let themselves be carried out.

			Above the lab, on the street, three girls were wandering - aimlessly, drunkenly.
			"Wooo!" Bea cheered. "Who said Caldermouth didn't have any good pubs?!"
			"I did." Amy snarked. "Posh spice over here thinks that shithole was nice."
			"The cocktails were good!" Bea meekly protested. "Weren't they, Chlo?"
			"I wouldn't know - you drank the entire pitcher." Chloe quipped, before giggling. "I'm supposed to be the sensible one, and here I am, wasting my salary on the world's blandest vodka."
			"How come you always drink vodka, by the way?" Amy tilted her head.
			"It was my first drink." Chloe shrugged. "We, uh... we have a lot of Russian family."
			"Well, I'll drink to that." Amy grinned. "Come on - there's a nightclub over in Celt Square that does suicide shots."
			"*Now* you're talking." Bea laughed.
			"Wait a sec." Chloe cut in, stepping forward.
			"What? What's wrong?"
			"There. In the middle of the street." she pointed.
			A manhole cover - it was shuffling slightly, as if being pushed.
			"Uh oh, the Sewer People are coming for us." Bea grinned. "Probably just some maintenance worker."
			"No, maintenance workers would leave the cover open." Chloe shook her head. "We should go help!"
			Before they could move, however - a strike made the cover ring like a bell, as it knocked into the air and crashed back down. The girls gasped - and went pale, as they saw the creature emerge.
			"Come on!" Connor called out, as the first of the lab rats crawled out from the ladder. "Let's keep moving, guys!"
			"Oh my god." Chloe covered her mouth. "Is that--"
			Amy rushed over. "H-hey!" she stammered. "Can we help at all?"
			Connor froze, looking at her.
			"Shit." he thought. "Shit, shit, shit."
			"Uh... yeah." he nodded, masking his voice with both windpipes. "Call an ambulance - a lot of them. Tell them there's been a mass casualty event."
			"Got it." Amy nodded, pulling out her phone.
			"Sparky - I need you to sneak off. The others are here." Connor whispered - too quiet for a human to hear.
			"Got it. I'll start tonight's patrol." he audibly nodded, skulking away.

		Killer, Saviour
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Before long, a group of ambulances had arrived. The paramedics struggled to make sense of the situation, but managed to organise a transport operation. Firemen had come too - providing truck transport for those who didn't need immediate care. Ready now, the convoy began to drive.
			Sirens blasted, as they snaked through Drackhill's roads, making the long route back to the hospital.
			As they approached a crossroads, a pair of black SUVs pulled out in front of the lead vehicle.
			"CLEAR THE ROAD!" its driver roared, blaring his sirens. "NOW!"
			The doors swung open - and uniformed, masked men with guns alighted.
			"Fuck!" the driver gasped, before something else came - slamming into the ground behind the men.
			"HEY!" Connor roared. "WHY DON'T YOU PICK ON SOMEONE YOUR OWN SIZE?!"
			His wristblades ginted in the light, as he danced through the Agents. Blood hissed from each body, and heads rolled. He kicked the SUV's boot, denting it and shunting it to the side.
			"COME ON! I'LL PROTECT YOU!" he barked.
			The driver swallowed a gulp, and moved forward.

			Judi rushed down the steps of A&E, helping to carry the patients inside.
			Connor rushed in, carrying one who was bleeding.
			"Got an urgent one here! Let's go!" he barked, quickly spraying her with the Coagulator and rushing back out.
			There, he saw a squad of armed officers.
			"Armed police." Naismith said grimly. "Hands where I can see them."
			Connor scowled, his eyes flaring.
			"See all these people? They'd be dead if it weren't for me."
			"We're not here for the people you've helped. We're here for the ones you've killed." Naismith snapped back. "I don't care who or what you are - you are *not* above the law."
			Connor chuckled mirthlessly.
			"Oh, the law." he began. "The same law that made it so the people hurt by this couldn't speak without fear of state violence? The same law that had you forget about what was going on here to go after me instead? THE SAME LAW, THAT IGNORES *SCUM* LIKE THE SKULLS, WHILE POINTING GUNS AT ANYONE TRYING TO STOP THEM? *THAT LAW?!*"
			The officers trained their guns on him - and he readied his blades.
			"Wait! Please, stop this!" Judi barked, rushing in between them.
			"HOLD YOUR FIRE!" Naimsmith roared. "Judi, what are you doing? Get away from him!"
			"Henry, please! I know what he's done in the past... but he saved lives tonight. Please, I'm begging you, don't do this!"
			Connor snarled, before raising his crossbow, and firing.
			The bolt's head had been replaced - intstead of a sharp tip, it was some kind of globule. It hissed on impact, as black smoke sprayed into the air. The officers scrambled to get away, to try and see - but no. The Werewolf was gone.
			Naismith coughed, and stepped forward.
			"I should arrest you." he growled.
			"Then do it."
			He let out a sigh. "Alright, people, come on. That convoy was already attacked - let's make damn sure no one else dies tonight. I want a secure perimiter. No one approaches the hospital without us knowing about it. Nina, I want you liasing with hospital security for any weak spots. Simmons, go on overwatch in the north gate. Michaels, I want CT here to provide armed support. Kent, you go and..."

			It was the early hours, now. Judi took a deep breath, as she opened her flat's door.
			"Hey, doc." Connor waved.
			"Oh fuck!" she gasped, before chuckling.
			"Sorry - I just wanted to check in."
			"How do you know where I live?"
			"You approached Crane and asked for a meet. You think I didn't do a background check before showing up?"
			"Fair enough. Anyway, how can I help you?"
			He smiled. "I just wanted to make sure the patients were okay."
			"Much better, thanks to you." she smiled. "I... I know what people say about you, but... you're alright in my book."
			"Hah... thanks, doc." he nodded, before preparing to leave.
			"Wait." she cut in, before scribbling something on a notepad. "My number."
			"Shouldn't I at least by you a drink?" he quipped.
			She let out a laugh - the kind you make when you've just crawled out of hell, and can finally breathe again.
			"My guess is, someone in your... 'line of work,' could probably use access to someone in my line of work. Call that number any time, and I'll patch you up - discreetly, of course."
			"I can heal just fine without--"
			"You're still limping slightly. And there's enough of a wheeze in your voice to suggest lung damage."
			He chuckled. "Give it an hour, I'll be fine."
			"Well, maybe one day, someone you care about gets hurt. Someone who can't heal like that, and you can't go to hospital without them asking awkward questions. Call me, and I can help out."
			"What makes you think I have people I care about?"
			She smiled softly. "I saw the way you helped that woman out of the ambulance. The way you gently carried her. You can deny it all you like, but as long as there's one person in this city, there's someone you care about. *That's* who you are."
			"You're talking like I'm some kind of saviour, rather than a killer."
			"Maybe you're both." she shrugged.
			He hesitated, before taking the number, and bowing his head. She watched him leave, and smiled softly.

			"God *DAMN* IT!" the Commandant roared.
			"I'm sorry, sir. All livestock were lost." his aide bowed his head. "Unfortunately, we were unable to recover the remains of Project Jotunn, as well."
			The Commandant scowled.
			"Get Agent Weiss here. Now. Tell him to set the trap."
			"Yes, sir."

		Sorry, So Sorry

	
	______________________________
	EPISODE - Helping Hands
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Morning came, then afternoon, as Connor jogged through the high street. A voice caught his ear.
			"Oh, hey!" Bea called over. Connor slowed, turned, and smiled.
			"Hey, guys!" he waved. She and Chloe walked over.
			"Fancy seeing you here!" Bea smiled. "Out for a run?"
			"Yeah - honestly, I appreciate the break." he grinned.
			"Do you run a lot? You don't seem out of breath at all." she noted.
			"I train when I can." he shrugged.
			Chloe smiled. "We're just out for our lunch break. Do you wanna come along?"
			"Sure!"
			The group headed into the nearest bistro, and took their seats.
			"So, how's school?" he asked.
			"Yeah, pretty good." Bea smiled. "I've spent my whole morning studying the British constitution - or, lack thereof."
			"Fun stuff." Connor grinned.
			"We just finished a lab session." Chloe chimed in. "Dissections, this time."
			"Gross." Bea chuckled, putting down her food. Chloe let out a giggle.
			They finished their lunch, and headed out of the bistro. There, a man in military uniform with a bright red poppy held a collection box.
			He marched up to the group. "Poppy appeal. Donations, please."
			"Oh, uh..." Bea fumbled at her pockets. "Sorry, I'm out of change!"
			"We take card." he said firmly.
			"Right." Bea nodded awkwardly. She reached for her wallet.
			Connor looked the man up and down, and his pupils constricted slightly.
			"Guys, let's go." he said hurriedly.
			"What's wrong?" Chloe asked.
			"Nothing, just... let's go."
			"Wow." the soldier scowled. "You feel like a big man, disrespecting the Army like that?"
			"You feel like a big man, shooting little kids?" he snapped back.
			"Connor!" Bea gasped.
			"What the *fuck* did you just say to me?!" the soldier barked.
			Connor stood his ground, his jaw clenching. "I see the medal, you Tan fuck. Did you enjoy yourself--"
			"Come on, let's go." Chloe cut in, grabbing his arm. "Now."
			Connor took a deep breath, staring into the soldier's soul. He nodded, and they moved.
			"Real brave, kid!" the soldier jeered. "Mouthing off at real men who fought for your freedoms!"
			Connor's head snapped around, but Chloe jerked his arm.
			"Don't." she said firmly. He sighed, and carried on walking. The trio came to a halt and leaned against a wall.
			"Fuckin' Tan. Fought for my chains, more like!" he hissed.
			"Okay, what's going on?" Bea asked firmly.
			Connor raised an eyebrow.
			"I've not known you for long - but you've never seemed like the type to pick fights with strangers on the street." she pressed. "What's wrong?"
			He let out a deep breath. "Sorry... Sorry."
			Another deep breath, before he explained.
			"That guy's medals - one of them was the General Service Medal for Operation Flying Fox - the occupation of my hometown."
			"Oh..." Bea realised.
			He sighed. "Seeing a man in uniform cornering us isn't a happy memory even ignoring that. To me, a soldier is someone who kicks down your door, screams in your face, smashes your windows, and beats you in the chest. And he had the nerve... the fuckin' nerve to shake his little collection box in our faces and ask for money?"
			"It's the poppy appeal..." Chloe shrugged. "I mean, they do help people--"
			"They help *soldiers.*" he corrected. "Call me heartless, but they're not better than anyone else. They don't deserve their own special charity, some massive public campaign, or every single person wearing a special flower just for them."
			He let out a breath, and bowed his head. "Sorry - I don't mean to rant about it. I know you guys get it."
			"We do." Bea nodded softly. "Look, we've gotta get back to uni, but... are you gonna be okay?"
			"Yeah, why?" he tilted his head.
			"Connor... what you're describing, it... it sounds like PTSD." Chloe said gently.
			He looked away.
			"There's no shame in it." she added quietly.
			"I know." he nodded. "I don't think colonised people have a word for PTSD. I think we just call it 'normal.'"
			Bea let out a sad smile. "We'll stay out a little longer."
			"No, guys you--you have classes..." he meekly protested.
			"Doesn't matter." Chloe smiled warmly. "Come on, let's go for a walk down the park, and talk about random stuff."
			"Sounds like a plan." Bea nodded.
			Connor hesitated, but smiled back.

		Remembrance
		______________________________
		SCENE
			It had been a long, long day at the cafe. Too long. Unsurprisingly, Amy's face lit up as she saw Connor and Sparky waiting outside for her.
			"Oh my goodness!" she beamed, rushing straight over to Sparky. "Hey, buddy! How've you been all day? Did you miss me?"
			"Yeah! Today's been good. Connor's been teaching me how to read a little better!" he barked back.
			Oblivious, Amy smiled warmly. "Such a good boy..." she cooed.
			"Nice to see you too, dickhead." Connor quipped.
			"Next time, just send the dog." she snarked back. She stood, and pulled him in for a hug.

			Connor finished tinkering away at the now-fixed wristwatch on his bedroom desk, and came into the living room. There, Amy was making a fuss over Sparky, as usual.
			"Who's a good boy? Whosagoodboyyy?" she asked in a baby voice.
			"Me, so I've been told." Sparky grinned. "Can I have the bloody treat now, or what?"
			"Paw?" she asked.
			Sparky sighed, giving a very graceful paw-shake.
			"Beg?"
			He hopped up, planting his front legs on her forearm.
			"Roll over?"
			"This bacon twist better be worth it." he grumbled, obeying.
			"Good boy! Catch!" she cheered, throwing the treat in the air. He inhaled it.
			"Hmm... yeah, not bad. " he shrugged.
			She laughed. "He's so good."
			"Sure is." Connor chuckled, endeared. "It's nice, seeing yous two get on so well."
			"Yeah, well if you remember, *I* was always Stella's favourite." she grinned.
			He laughed heartily, as did she.
			"You know..." she began. "Ever since getting him, I've noticed you've been doing better and all."
			Connor smiled. "Yeah, well... perfect excuse to get out of the house, isn't he?"
			Sparky rolled back onto his back, and was immediately attended by Amy's belly rubs.
			"How was your day, by the way?" she asked.
			"Oh, *now* you ask!" he snarked.
			"Fuck off, I don't actually care." she grinned.
			He chuckled. "Yeah, not bad. Ran into Chloe and Bea earlier."
			"Ah, nice. How are they?"
			"They're good. We, uh... we got cornered by some poppy appeal guy."
			"Oh." Amy nodded sympathetically. "You okay?"
			"Yeah. They helped me get over it." he nodded.
			Before he could continue, his ears pricked up. His burner phone was ringing.
			"One sec." he said, rushing into his room. He answered it.
			"Hello?"
			"Hi, Connor." the other voice replied.
			"Commandant..." Connor snarled, his face going white.
			"Commandant?!" Sparky jumped up, barking and curling his lip.
			"What's wrong?" Amy asked, confused.
			"What do you want, you fucking cunt?!" Connor snapped. "Wanna show your face? Let me pay you back for what you did to me?!"
			"'Did to you?'" Amy tilted her head. "Wait..."
			"Yeah, that's not a half-bad idea." the Commandant audibly grinned. "Meet me in Belson. Marsh Road. Unit 4-7-81/P."
			"You're a dead man. You hear me?" Connor growled. "*DEAD!*"
			A drop of hot blood came from his nostrils, and the pain in his head intensified.
			"I'll tear your throat out!" Sparky added through a roar.
			"See you soon!" the Commandant laughed, cutting off the call.
			Connor turned to Sparky. "Let's go."
			"Whoa, whoa..." Amy cut in, standing in front of the door. "You're not going anywhere."
			"Amy..." Connor began, supressing himself. "Get out of my way."

			"Amy, wait!" he begged.
			"CONNOR!" Sparky barked, similarly encased in his battle-form. "We have to go!"

		Commandant Calls
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Across the city, Connor and Sparky perched atop an industrial unit. Sparky's fur flowed in the cold breeze, and their eyes flashed red as they scanned the fourth unit below.
			"Electromagnetic signals." Sparky noted. "Some electrical equipment in the walls."
			"Probably just wiring. Though, I'm not sure - that there looks like a radio receiver." Connor pointed.
			"Smells like WiFi." Sparky shrugged. "I doubt it's anything important. Can you get that plastic smell?"
			"Plastic? I thought it was oil." Connor tilted his head. "Well, this place is an industrial unit. Probably just old product."
			Sparky nodded, then his eyes darted. "See that?"
			"Yeah - cluster of heartbeats."
			He flexed his throat and unhinged his jaw, as did his packmate. They both let out an ethereal, alien song - one high-pitched enough that the bats in Wyrmrock went crazy.
			"Canines." he nodded. "A couple of them. A humanoid, too - must be the Commandant."
			"217 must be in there. She *has* to be. As for the other... they must be another sibling. More of my people."
			Connor gently stroked him between the ears.
			"This is the big moment. We get our revenge, and you get your sister back. After that... we hunt the rest of them down."
			"No time to dawdle, then." Sparky smiled. The two rose, and stretched their legs out.
			Connor closed his eyes, and focused. He flexed his thighs and calves, and felt his hot blood rush to them, saturating them with mutant power.
			Whatever the Commandant had done to him... it was going to be his undoing.
			The two rushed forward, and jumped. Their legs kicked into the roof's edge, smashing the metal downwards as they launched upwards. They landed on a skylight, crashing down.
			They landed on the ground, their arrival punctuated by raining shards of glass. 
			"COMMANDANT!" Connor roared. "SHOW YOURSELF!"
			His scream echoed in the cold, metal unit. He was answered by the sound of scraping, as a Super-Agent walked out from a storage crate, wielding twin machetes and clad in thick kevlar armour. 
			A television screen, which hanged from the wall, flashed to life. The Commandant's image flickered onto the screen.
			"Good evening, freaks." he grinned sadistically.
			"YOU FUCKING COWARD!" Connor howled. "SHOW YOUR FACE AND *DIE LIKE A MAN!*"
			"It's cute, honestly. You think you two little shits could kill me." he laughed. "And honestly, I think I may have tortured you a little too well. I tell you I'm somewhere, and mere minutes later you come running? You must miss me."
			"WHERE'S 217? WHERE'S MY SISTER?!" Sparky roared.
			"Oh, Six! Good to see you again." the Commandant smirked.
			At that, the Agent was joined by a pair of snarling, muscular mastiffs. It was barely visible past their fur, but the smell of their blood confirmed it - there was super-serum in their black veins.
			"She's not here, but don't worry - you have company. Project Fenrir wasn't a *complete* failure - that blood we harvested was given to these... mangy, rabid mutts."
			The twin Werewolves assumed a fighting stance.
			"You take the dogs - don't kill them." Connor whispered firmly, morphing blades from his wrists. "I'll fight the Agent."
			"Save some for me." Sparky snarled back, eyes burning red.
			"Sic 'em, boys!" The Commandant barked. "Agent Weiss - kill him."

			Connor wasn't here to fool around - he was here for blood. He spun forwards like a vengeful tornado, his wristblades ripping through the air. Weiss darted back, then knelt down and crossed his machetes, catching Connor's right.
			Under his mask, Connor grinned. His left blade burst forwards, aimed straight for Weiss's gut.
			Not fast enough. Weiss turned, twisting his blades so Connor's fell forward, and then he countered. Connor bent sideways into an L-shape, dodging the first mache. The second nicked his neck.
			First blood. Connor felt the wound close up in moments, and snarled viciously.
			He roared, charging forwards again.

			At first, Sparky's wolven form intimidated the lesser canids. But then both remembered what the Commandant would do if they failed, and their black-veined eyes darkened with furor.
			"Listen to me! I don't want to hurt you!" he pleaded, as he slammed the backside of his paw around the head of one. He was careful not to catch it with his claws.
			The other used the opening to sink his teeth into Sparky's back leg, tearing hot blood and red meat.
			He howled in shock and pain, before turning and beating that one down. It got back up in short order.
			Sparky turned his head, and saw Connor's fight. His pupils shrank as they caught the Commandant's image.

			"DIE!" Connor demanded, as the tip of his blade sank into Weiss's thigh.
			Most men - hell, most Super-Agents - would've been thrown off by that. Weiss simply used his proximity to drive his own blade through Connor's hand.
			Connor screamed in rage as the blade shunted in between his carpal bones, popping out of his palm. Weiss pulled the blade backwards, splitting his hand in two.
			He flipped, and clutched his hand tight, setting the bones back and morphing a bandage to bind them. His eyes flashed crimson, and he formed bucklers over his wristblades.
			"Ah, finally - you've figured out you're not invincible, eh?" the Commandant taunted. "In fact, I'd say you're quite vincible."
			"Fuck you." Connor spat, his armour thickening and calcifying. He raced forwards, and the two monsters - one in form, one in soul - clashed again.

			Sparky snarled as another chunk of flesh tore out from his hide. He turned, and bit the scruff of the one who did it. He raised up on his hind legs, and threw it across the unit.
			Breathing space. He pounced on the other forcing it to its back.
			For normal canines, that would be it. The loser would submit, accepting that the winner would have its throat otherwise.
			The super-mastiff went right for Sparky's throat, instead. Sparky darted back just in time.
			"Please! Stop fighting me! I'm on your side! I want to stop the Commandant!" he begged.
			No answer. This wasn't one of his people - just an animal. A raging, monstrous animal.
			Sparky closed his scarlet eyes for a second.
			"I'm sorry." he whispered, as he ripped out its throat.
			He turned, as the other was sprinting towards him. He bowed his head in shame, and went for the kill.

			Connor snarled as Weiss's machete was knocked backwards by his buckler. He saw his opening and pounced forwards, paying him back in kind with a slash across the chest.
			Weiss's armour was shredded and torn, and his skin was raked and bloody - but he wasn't beaten. Not yet.
			He brought his blades together, holding them side-by-side. He half-closed his eyes, and breathed out slowly.
			Connor charged, pointing his own blades forward. He was going to impale this son of a bitch.
			Weiss held position. He felt his heart beat with anticipation. Then, he struck.
			Connor was tired. Exhausted, even. So exhausted, his reflexes were a nanosecond too late.
			Weiss's blades swept in a horizontal motion, clashing into Connor's forearms. The bucklers absorbed the damage, bending and cracking as his arms swung outwards.
			Connor went to close the opening, to put his guard back up, to do *something.*
			Too late.
			Weiss twisted his blades to their sides, and drove them through a gap in Connor's ribs.
			They sank through his armour, then his upper lungs, and punched out through his back.
			Connor went to scream - instead, blood poured from his mouth and nose, as he gurgled in pain.
			Weiss gripped the hilts of his blades, and pushed Connor to his knees.
			"Hah..." the Commandant chuckled. "I expected more. Goodbye, Connor."
			Weiss placed his foot against Connor's sturnum, and pulled his blades free - slowly. Grinning.
			The blades glinted in the dim light, as he crossed them - holing them like shears ready to take the Werewolf's head.
			The blades tore through the air, sailing inward.
			Their impact sent a shock through the air, as they crashed into Connor's swiftly-raised forearms.
			"No..." he gurgled. "NO!"
			Weiss struggled, but couldn't break past the Werewolf's determined guard.
			Connor was a lot of things. A lot more, lately.
			He was not someone who knew when to die.
			"GRAAAAGH!" Sparky howled, slamming into Weiss's side. He skidded to a halt as Weiss crashed into a wall.
			Connor spat a globule of blood, and forced himself to rise.
			Weiss planted his blades in the ground, using their support to get back up. He looked at the dead mastiffs, and laughed cruelly.
			"Oh dear, Six. It's not the first time you've seen your misbegotten kind die, is it? First time you've killed them, though." the Commandant chimed in.
			"You killed them. We just put them out of their misery." Sparky snarled grimly.
			"And if you wanna see 'killing,' then we're happy to oblige." Connor added. He readied his blades, as his lungs scabbed over.
			Weiss gripped the hilts tightly, as his eyes frantically darted side to side.
			The Werewolves charged in.
			Sparky hit first. Weiss's blade cut across his muzzle, but the crimson-eyed beast was unfazed. His teeth sank into Weiss's side, ripping out chunks of hot meat.
			Connor, meanwhile, sent his own blades down - ripping off Weiss's right hand. He screamed in pain, but then Sparky's claws sank into his throat.
			Connor grabbed the fallen machete, and swept as hard as he could.
			Weiss's body fell to the ground. His head landed a few feet away.
			"Credit where it's due." the Commandant grinned. "The data we've gained from this encounter is... invaluable."
			Sparky's hackles rose.
			Connor didn't move. His blades stayed forward, tense. "We're coming for you. We're going to make you feel everything you did to us. But before we do - where's 217?"
			The Commandant tilted his head, as if considering it. "Still on that, huh?"
			A faint crackle ran through the walls.
			Connor noticed it first. Not heard - felt. A low, irregular pulse under the metal floor. His eyes narrowed.
			"Well, now." the Commandant grinned. "Isn't this a nice trip down memory lane?"
			Connor's stare tightened. "What did you do?"
			"Not the first time Six has watched his kind die because of me. And definitely not the first time you've been buried."
			Connor went still. He tilted his head, but then, his irises shrank to pinpoints. His twin heartbeats turned to hums of terror.
			"Ah... The penny drops."
			Sparky's red gaze darted to his packmate. "Connor...?"
			"RUN!" he screamed.
			"What?! Why?!"
			"PLASTIC! IN THE WALLS!"
			Too late.
			The sound came first: a deep, mechanical *thump* from inside the walls.
			Then heat.
			The world around him erupted into flame. A massive explosion shook the building, and down it came.

			Sparky pulled himself out of the wreckage first. He frantically started digging, cutting his paw pads apart on the shrapnel. Finally, he unearthed Connor, who took a sharp intake of breath.
			The ringing in his ears was deafening. His vision blurred as he came to, the world around him a hazy mess of rubble and smoke. He groaned, disoriented, but alive.
			"Connor! Come on, we've got to go! The police will be here soon!"
			The sound of sirens wailing in the distance cut through the haze. Connor tried to rise, but looked back in horror. His hand was pinned under an entire wall's worth of rubble.
			His hearts raced as panic set in. He tugged at the debris, his breath coming in sharp gasps, but his hand remained firmly caught.
			"No... no, no, no..." he stuttered.
			He shifted his weight, tried to use his enhanced strength, but it was useless. His hand was trapped, and couldn't leave unless he freed it.
			Sparky put all his might into shifting the mess, but he could barely budge it.
			"Connor, I... I'm not strong enough." he cried.
			A grim realisation dawned on him.
			He morphed a serrated dagger from his free hand. The blade's edge gleamed under the light. He gritted his teeth and pressed it into his trapped forearm.
			Squelch.
			*SHK!*
			The world slowed. The pain was like nothing he'd ever felt before - sharp, intense, and relentless.
			It coursed through him, amplifying every sensation, turning his vision dark at the edges.
			Squelch again.
			*SHK-SHK!*
			The flesh had been severed. Only bone left - too strong for even his knife to saw through.
			He grimaced, pale as a ghost, and his stomach heaved.
			*HAWK-ptoo!*
			The bone hissed as the acid bit through it. After a while, it was weak enough.
			*SHK-SHK!*
			*SHHK!*
			*SNAP.*
			With a final, brutal motion, he freed himself, his body recoiling from the sheer agony of it all. As he pulled free, the flesh ripped, and his wrist-joint popped.
			He rose to his feet, breathless, bloodied, and battered.
			The world slowed down to a standstill. If normal pain could sharpen a mind - what could this pain do?
			He tensed, squeezing his eyes shut. Despite his eyelids being closed, his irises glowed with such a bright, brilliant red, that they shone past the skin. The glow faded, and the bleeding finally stopped. A bark from Sparky shook him from his stupor, and the pair sprinted up a wall back to their overlook, just as police and fire engines poured onto the site.

		The Loss of a Hand
		______________________________
		SCENE
			It had been a hundred years. It had been a couple of seconds.
			Connor woke up on the roof. As he did, Sparky rushed over, and licked his face frantically.
			"Are you okay?" he asked, worried.
			"Hah... I'm fine. Just blacked out for a moment." he nodded, his head feeling both light and heavy.
			He morphed back down into his civilian clothes, and reached into his pocket. He pulled out a small pack of cigarettes.
			"Thank god these weren't squished back there." he chuckled, holding one in his mouth, and lighting it. The motion was tricky with one hand, but he managed.
			"Why do you burn those stinky sticks?" Sparky asked.
			"Honestly? Not much use to me these days. Downside of being a super-powered mutant is you can't get anything out of nicotine." he shrugged. "Still, the ritual of it... calms me down, I guess."
			Sparky nodded, and sat down with his packmate. "What happens now?" he asked.
			"Now? Now we see if I can grow back limbs." Connor laughed and coughed. "If I can't... we may need to rethink our operation."
			He leant back. "I've been putting off asking you... maybe because I'm scared about what you'll say. But... this whole thing with the Commandant..."
			"He was... he was right." Sparky said, nearly gagging on the words. "We thought we were better, but all it took was one phone call, and it's like we're back in the cages again."
			Connor looked away for a minute, before turning back.
			"My memories of it all... they're jumbled. I can't remember us escaping the first time. But... you remember, don't you?"
			Sparky thought for a moment.
			"All my life, I remember being in this cage. Being hurt by the bad men." he began. "And none of them ever cared. They just kept hurting me. Sometimes it was for fun, sometimes I think they were being curious, but it was always cruel. And..." he paused. "And then, one day, the bad men brought you in. You were hurt, badly - but alive. They chained you up. I wasn't in the room, but I could hear you screaming as they hurt you too."
			Connor leant forward, listening intently.
			"I kept hearing them talking about programming. I think they wanted to train you. They kept saying these specific words - 'Listen and Obey.'"
			Connor flinched at the words. Even hearing them telepathically from a wolf didn't soften their blow.
			"Every time they did, they hurt you." Sparky continued. "One day, your screaming was louder than ever before. I heard you thrashing and smashing about, and you burst out of the door they held you in. You came running out, and I knew you were different. You looked at me, and I didn't see cruelty, just sadness. I begged you to let me out, and you heard me, and you saved me."
			Connor rubbed his temples with his intact hand, processing. "So... We broke out, together?"
			"Yes. We ran for miles and miles." Sparky nodded. "But they caught up to us. They overwhelmed us, and dragged us away. They separated us - I never knew what happened to you afterwards."
			Connor looked downwards. "And... they brought you back to the place I found you?"
			"No. They brought me back to where we first met." Sparky explained. "But they were worried you might come back for me. So they moved me to the other place - the one where you and Ivan saved me."
			Connor leaned back. "Did, um... did you ever see me leave on my own? The Commandant... he pulled a trick on me."
			"No, never." Sparky shook his head.
			Connor stroked his chin. "Makes sense. We escape together, then after they bring us both back, the Commandant stages another escape to crush my hopes of leaving. They must've somehow wiped my memories of us getting out, too."
			Sparky looked away. "They were cruel. After meeting so many normal humans, I don't get it. Humans aren't so different to wolves. You're naturally decent. So what's wrong with them?"
			Connor sighed. "I don't know, bud. They're cruel. Evil. Monsters..."
			Sparky thought for a moment. "The word he used - Fenrir. That's what they called me, too."
			"Project Fenrir... That explains the super-dogs earlier." Connor nodded, visibly joining the dots. "Whatever made me and the Super-Agents, Fenrir made you and the dogs."
			"They're building an army." Sparky realised in horror.
			"Still... it doesn't explain why we're different. I mean, you couldn't hear the dogs talking, could you?"
			"No, nothing." Sparky shook his head. "This weird connection we have... I think it's just us."

			Connor paused. He closed his eyes, hesitated, and reached out. He placed his hand on Sparky's head, and their minds touched.
			Fear. Pain. Rage. All swirling through his mind, like he was pulling the depths of the ocean to the surface. He reached inwards, and Sparky let him in.
			This 'mind-bond' they had was utterly alien to both. The flashes, the shared dreams... and now this. Connor stretched his mind's eye into Sparky's subconsciousness, and watched. He saw himself, bursting out of a steel door, drenched in blood and howling in pain. He felt Sparky's memories, his emotions, his senses... the link grew stronger. Sparky saw through Connor's eyes, and Connor through Sparky's. The line where one ended and the other began had blurred into oblivion.
			Connor saw the torment Sparky had faced. Horrific surgeries. Agonising tests. He watched as the rest of Sparky's litter died, until only he was left.
			Sparky saw Connor's own pain. The torments. And others, too. He saw the moment Vince was arrested. He saw the days in the Bogside where Connor's grandfather beat him. He saw a blazing inferno in a car, with his grandmother's burning corpse hanging out. And deeper still, he watched through Connor's eyes as drove a fire poker through an older man's head.
			It was too much. The two pulled back, and rubbed their skulls, regaining their senses of self. After a short while, they both opened their eyes, and looked down - as though visibly checking which one they were.
			"You okay?" Connor asked.
			"Yeah, I... I'm Sparky, right?" he replied.
			"Yeah. Which means I'm Connor... Alright, I'm okay now."
			"Me and 217 did that once. It feels like we became one person for a moment."
			"I did the same thing with Nabira the other day." Connor nodded, and closed his eyes again.
			"Who was that man?" Sparky asked.
			"Which one?"
			"The one you stabbed. I felt that memory..."
			Connor sighed. "James Laverty." he finally said, half-spitting the name. "He... he was mine and Amy's foster-carer."
			"What's a foster-carer?
			"They're supposed to be caregivers. A bit like what I am to you. Someone who isn't your parent, but raises you anyway. But he... he was a monster."
			Worse, deeper memories washed into Connor's mind. Flashes of Laverty... and what he did to Amy. He reached his hand back out, and rejoined his mind with Sparky.
			Sparky took in the flashes, then pulled his head back in disgust.
			"Good work." he nodded. "But you were a pup back then?"
			"Yeah, it was before I got my powers." Connor shrugged. "I don't know how, I just... I went berserk. After that, I was taken away by the police. Thankfully, they decided not to press charges, and that's how me and Amy came to live with Vince."
			Connor sighed. He recalled the memories he'd gleaned from Sparky.
			"I saw your memories too, you know. You... You survived all of that."
			Sparky jumped up, and rested his head on Connor's lap. "You did too. Until I met you, I never knew humans could be nice."
			"You've always been so good with people though." Connor replied. "When Amy came back on your first night with us, you were so good with her. And you were just as good with our other friends."
			"I guess... It's because I had you." Sparky mused. "You saved me from that place. So, I trust you. And that means, I trust who you trust."
			Connor smiled warmly. "I trust you too."
			He went to stroke Sparky's head, before realising he was using the wrong arm. He chuckled grimly.
			"We've both been through hell." he began. "And that's not gonna heal any time soon. But we have each other. Before I had you, I was... I was a wreck. I wanted to die, because the pain was too much. But then you came along. And you were the only creature on Earth who could know what I was going through. More than that, you needed me as much as I needed you. So looking after you... helps me."
			"What do you mean?" Sparky tilted his head.
			"I mean, when it was just me, I could let myself fall apart. But with you here, I have to stick around to help you. Not only that, when you're suffering, I've gotta do something. I can justify not helping myself - I can't justify not helping you. And through that, I learned to help myself. Throgh being kind to you, I learned to be kind to myself. Through helping absolve you, I... I found my own absolution."
			Sparky nuzzled his face into Connor's chest.
			"You're right. We're the only things like us. Which means we can get through this pain... together."

			At the same time, Naismith was overlooking the smouldering ruins. Nina approached him.
			"Good news, sir. We were able to shift the wreckage. We've recovered the hand." she said.
			"In what condition?" Naismith asked.
			"Pristine, sir." she replied. "I've already called the FIs to prep for immediate analysis. Though it's missing a lot of bone, they should still be able to extract prints and DNA."
			"Missing bone?" Naismith tilted his head.
			Nina nodded. "I'm no FI, but it looked to me as though he'd cut the flesh around the bone, and then just pulled until the wrist popped off. As a result, there's the flesh from the wrist, but no forearm-bone. Well, either that, or he doesn't have forearm bones." she chuckled.
			Naismith smirked. "The man's a bloody alien, I'll tell ya."
			As he said this, the hand was brought past them in a container. Nina yelped, as did an FI - the hand was *twitching.*
			"Jesus..." Naismith muttered. "What the fuck?"
			"The techs will have a field day, sir." Nina nodded, shuddering.
			"Well then." Naismith smiled. "Let's get to work."

		Trauma-dumping
		______________________________
		SCENE
			It was past midnight now. Connor had been dreading this, but it needed to be done.
			He opened his flat's door.
			Immediately, his eyes flashed red for a second. He saw Amy's heartbeat behind her door.
			She was sat against it, as if barricading herself away.
			Timidly, he approached. He could hear her breathing quicken as he walked, and her heart skip a beat as he knocked.
			"Amy..." he whispered. "It's... it's me. Connor."
			She didn't say anything. She just silently sobbed, covering her mouth so as not to scream.
			He sat down against her door. Even without super-senses, she could feel her brother's presence opposite her.
			Connor sighed. "These... these men, they shot me in the head. They took me away, and they... did something to me. Experimented on me. Tortured me. Made me into... this."
			Her breathing trembled.
			"I wanted to tell you..." he continued, his voice cracking. "I... I was just scared. Scared it might put a target on your back, scared you'd think I was crazy, scared I *was* crazy... and scared that I'd scare you. Like now."
			She sniffled softly, clutching her knees.
			"I know it's a lot... I can't imagine how you are right now, but I..." he began, tears rolling down his face. "I could really use my sister right now."
			She took a deep breath, stood, and opened the door. He rose too.
			She wordlessly pulled him in for an embrace. He held his arms out awkwardly, before wrapping her in them. They both took a moment to breathe.

			Finally, she pulled back, and looked at him, before going pale again.
			"Uh... What the hell?! What happened? W-where the fuck is your hand?!" she stammered, horrified.
			"Oh, shit." Connor sighed, sitting her down.
			"What happened?!" she repeated. Sparky jumped up, and curled into a ball next to her. She absently stroked his fur, grounding herself.
			"I got pinned under some rubble." Connor explained nonchalantly.
			"You... You cut off your own hand?" she asked.
			"...yes." he nodded. "It was either that, or get caught by the police."
			"Can you grow hands back? Is that one of your superpowers?"
			Connor allowed himself a chuckle. "Superpowers?"
			"You *do* know I saw you at the Horse, right? Getting shot in the chest six times and barely flinching?" she cocked an eyebrow.
			"Fair enough." he grinned. "Anyway, I'm not sure. Never lost a limb before. But..." he began, pulling up his sleeve. "It's healed a little. Look at the bone - there was more sticking out ealier. Hell, my wrist-bone seems to be growing back too."
			He pointed at the stump, revealing a fledgling wrist-joint forming above his arm-bone. His skin and flesh was creeping up the bone, covering it neatly. He hadn't looked at it in the light, but now he could see - His bone was dark, as though someone mixed calcium with coal. His brain flashed back to his school chemistry lessons, but he shook his head.
			"Plus, I've grown back teeth before, and I've healed away scars." he shrugged.
			Amy gulped, and held his stump gently.
			"So... you're gonna be okay?" she asked finally.
			"Probably. If not, I'm sure I can get some decent prosthetics from the KGB." he answered nonchalantly.
			"The KGB?" she cocked her eyebrow.
			"Long story. But yeah, the KGB are helping me. Whoever these freaks I'm fighting are, they're clearly connected to fascists - and for all their faults, the KGB *hate* fascism."
			Amy nodded slightly, then allowed herself a chuckle. "Christ, if Vince knew you were working with communists, he'd be jumping for joy."
			Connor laughed. "Just wait 'til we get the IRA on-side."
			She giggled, then went quiet. "So... You're the 'Werewolf' people have been talking about?"
			"I have *no* idea where that nickname comes from." Connor chuckled grimly. Amy allowed herself a laugh.
			"Yeah. It's fucking lame." she snarked, still in shock.

			She paused, hesitant. "You... you mentioned torture?"
			Connor sighed, and nodded. "The Commandant - the guy who phoned earlier. He put me through hell."
			"Why? Why would he do that?"
			"Not sure yet. But either way, he kidnapped me, tortured me, and changed me."
			He took a deep breath, before continuing.
			"It wasn't just physical. I mean, they cut me up, zapped me, put me in an ice bath, waterboarded me, you name it. But the worst was the tricks."
			"Tricks?"
			"One time, he let me think I was escaping. Just as I was about to leave, he shot me, and brought me back in. Not only that, they fucked with my head somehow... the memories are jumbled."
			"So how did you escape? How did you come back home?"
			"I snapped." he shuddered. "The Commandant was gone, and there was some other goon stood with me. I bit his throat out, and... ate him."
			"*Ate him?!*" she gasped.
			"I... it's not how it sounds. I'd been starved, and I was half-feral." he quickly explained.
			"I-I'm not judging you." she quickly corrected. "You did what you had to do, I'm sure of it. Just... a lot to process."
			He nodded, and swallowed, as if forcing the memories back down.
			"Anyway... after that, the whole place got blown up. I was buried then, too - didn't have to cut my hand off, though. Instead, I got burned to a crisp. Managed to dig my way out, and... ended up back here. The rest, I suppose you know."
			She nodded. "And... now, he's dead?"
			"No. This was just a trap. He's... he's still out there." he shook his head. His voice slowly turned to a growl.

			Amy paused, taking it all in.
			"I... Thanks for telling me. And... I get why you didn't."
			He smiled sadly.
			"Does anyone else know?" she asked. "Besides, you know... the *KGB?*"
			"Tommy knows." Connor admitted. "You remember Reece Tomlinson?"
			"Stoker's goon? The one who got his head shot off?" she tilted her head. "He was one of the cunts who came at me in Raj's."
			"I killed him." Connor sighed. "I didn't mean to. He came for me shortly after I escaped, and I hit him in the chin."
			"His head had been blown off with a shotgun!" Amy countered.
			Connor sighed. "I'm *that* strong. When fighting humans, it's like their skin is paper and their bones are glass. It's taken me a hell of a lot of effort to avoid killing them by accident."
			"Humans?" she interjected, head tilted.
			Connor sighed again. "I'm not human anymore. Whatever they did to me... It's safe to say, I'm post-human. As are the people I kill."
			"So those rumours about the Skulls..."
			"All true. The people I'm hunting have this weird drug... it makes people stronger, faster, tougher, you name it. For some reason, I'm tougher than most who take it. Still working that one out."
			Amy shook her head. "I thought I recognised that look on your face."
			"Hm?"
			"When you first came to mine, after you went missing." she explained. "You had a look on your face - like shellshock. You looked the exact same way when... when you killed Laverty."
			Connor tensed up a little. "Yeah, I suppose I did. Guess I was always a killer, then, eh?"
			"No." she said firmly. "You killed him to save me. Same as the other freaks you've taken out - you killed them to save other people."
			Connor took a deep breath, and nodded. "Yeah, I... I suppose. I definitely don't regret killing *him.*"

			"Anything else I need to know? Can you fly or something? Laser eyes? X-ray vision?" she quipped.
			"Super-senses." he nonchalantly shrugged. "Strength, endurance, stamina... you've seen the shapeshifting, too. I've no idea how it all works. Oh, and Sparky can talk."

			"I was never a good listener." Connor snarked. "Now, I was told as a kid to never hit a woman, so maybe this'd be easier if you just surren---"
			At that, she launched a throwing knife at him. He caught it by the handle, and looked up, just as her whip smacked across his face.
			He cartwheeled away to reduce the impact, and stabbed the knife into the ground.
			"That wasn't very nice. I was still monologuing." he laughed, before his costume thickened with anticipation.
			"Sorry. Busy schedule." she smirked. She threw a knife into the air, and hit it with her whip. To Connor's amazement, the whip's edge wrapped around the handle and knotted itself perfectly.
			"Whoa... do it again!" he snarked, before pouncing in.

			Whiplash, true to her name, swung out, the knife at the edge slashing across Connor's chest. At the second strike, he grabbed the rope, only for the knife to swing around and stab into his abdomen. He pulled the whip as hard as he could, and Whiplash launched towards him.
			He sent a haymaker aiming right for her head. As it sailed through the air, her eyes flashed violet, and he felt it move - as if some hidden force was pushing it away. All the momentum was lost, as it went right by the side of her head. Meanwhile, she pulled two knives from her belt, and sank them repeatedly into his torso.
			He kicked her as hard as he could, and actually made her move - slightly. He scurried backwards, gasping for breath.
			"Okay... time out?" he shrugged.
			"You wish." she grinned, striking him with her whip once more. It caught him in the face, cutting across his cheek.
			He quickly darted backwards, and felt his gauntlets morph. He readied his crossbows, and fired.
			As the bolts flew forwards, he made sure to trigger his super-senses. His eyes burned red, and he watched in slow motion as they sailed through the air. Both were on a direct course for her. Even with her enhanced physicals, she couldn't possibly move fast enough to dodge them.
			To his horror, he watched as her eyes shifted, and they suddenly veered off course, flying past her with not a single scratch.
			"How the fuck..." he muttered, before realising.
			His suit rippled, pressurising again. His eyes roared brightly, and then it popped.
			Whiplash grunted as the smoke cloud erupted over the rooftop. She covered her eyes and wiped them. When she reopened, she saw him charging in, bull-rushing towards her. His eyes roared brightly as he ignored strike after strike. In moments, he closed the distance. He grabbed her by the head as hard as he could, and rather than stabbing, he pushed his free hand into her arm. Despite his lack of momentum, it broke past the skin and into the flesh beneath.
			She roared in... no, not pain. Excitement? Surprise? Either way, she spun the whip around, and the knife sank right into his back. Undeterred, he gripped a hold of her arms, and headbutted her as hard as he could.
			Again, he felt a force pushing back. A normal Super-Agent would've been stunned badly by that - she was barely fazed. She headbutted him right back, with far more force, and sent him sprawling backwards.
			He panted for breath, as did she.
			"Oh, my..." she grinned, licking the blood off of her lips. "Now *this* is a fight..."
			"Okay, this is getting weird now." he chuckled, rising. "How the fuck are you doing that?"
			"What? This?" she smirked, before launching her whip at him again. This time, his hand shot out, and he grabbed it. He ripped it towards him, and planted his foot in her torso. She tried, but couldn't keep her grip. He threw it down, and raised his fists. The smoke cloud finally cleared - this was it. Make or break.
