			"Oh... excellent." she growled excitedly, putting up her stance.
			The two super-warriors clashed again, and once more, Connor felt that strange force at his hands. Every strike he made either lost momentum, or glanced away, dealing minimal damage. Meanwhile, he could hardly move to dodge. It was as though the air was thicker for him, and thinner for her. He tried to twist - oh, he tried. Failed, though.
			Finally, a haymaker from her sent him spinning to the ground. Landing on his back, she planted her boot on his neck. He gripped her heel, trying desperately to move it, but felt even the tiny gasps of air he could breathe be pulled from his lungs.
			"That was... very impressive." she panted, grinning sadistically.
			Connor felt his vision blur. The world was going darker, and he fought for every breath.
			"Shh... don't fight it. Embrace it." she whispered.
			"Embrace it." the voice echoed in his skull. "Embrace it..."
			He felt his twin heartbeats quicken, then begin to slow. It was too much...
			Too much...
			No.
			NO!

While the force restricted it, it landed, and his knuckles cracked along with her cheekbone. Then, he twisted her to face away, and wrapped her as tight as he could.
			"This is... no time for a cuddle..." she snarled, gripping her braid. She sank the knife into his chest. Then again. And again.

			It made a tiny difference, as they smashed down into a car. Metal and glass cut into her skin, and she felt her ribcage give way.

For example, I can manipulate trajectories, but I never trained in general telekinesis. For my... line of work... you need a more subtle touch."

Also, if I'm touching someone, I can understand them, no matter what language they speak - and vice versa, too. I can also read people's emotions - and tell if they're lying. I've even... even managed to see into their memories - and them into mine. Like we become one person for a moment."

			"I get it." Connor nodded gently. "But listen - if you do need help, come to the Singing Horse - it's a nightclub in Redbridge. Ask for me - the owner knows me."
			"Why are you doing this?" she asked, her brow furrowing.
			"Doing what? Being kind?"
			"Yes! Why would you do that?!" she hissed.
			"Because... I know what it's like to be tortured." he shrugged. "And to be hunted. And it's my fault you're in this situation. And... well, I'm something of a superhero. It's my *job* to be kind. Besides, it sounds like we're both in the business of killing Super-Agents."
			She paused, looking at him up and down. The monster in the kevlar suit - her target, her prey... it didn't make sense.
			She hesitantly reached out her hand. He paused, but took it, and their consciousnesses shot against each other.
			She saw the Commandant's torment of him. His body twisting and reshaping against his will. He saw... nothing. The horror of nothingness. The pod.
			It was too much. They pulled away, and rubbed their temples in unison.
			She turned away, then turned her head back. She pulled off her domino mask, and gulped.
			"Before they took me..." she began, choking on her words. "My name was Gwen. Gwen Blake."
			Connor hesitated, but his mask rippled and melted away.
			"I'm Connor. Connor Barrett."
			Whiplash - Gwen - bowed her head, and walked away into the night.
			Connor stood there, as she faded into the fog. The kevlar melted back down into his soft red hoodie, and he pulled the cloth closer for warmth. He took a deep breath, and smiled sadly.

			The two breathed out in relief, and left the autopsy room.

You're all I think about..." he put on all his best charms. Bea melted.

			November 2011. Snow on the ground. And for the first time in a decade, Connor had almost forgotten what day it was. Almost.

			This silence carried on for a good while - longer than most 15-year-olds could've managed. Finally, Connor took a deep breath.
			"This is all your fault." he growled.

			"Oh, boo hoo. The weirdo had a rough day." Trey mocked.

			"It's bloody Friday, you idiot." Trey scoffed.

			"Fuck off! I mean the English! None of yous even acknowledge what happened! What yous took from me! *WHO* yous took from me!"
			Connor's anguished scream echoed in the room. It went deathly silent, and Connor tried - and failed - to regain his composure.

			"I wish my grandparents were dead." Trey began. "My mum's side, that is."

			"Right, I'm going to go to bed. I'll see you all in the morning. That door has a dog door on it - though I doubt yours will fit." he chuckled at the thought of Sparky trying to squeeze through the door.
			"Good point - Sparky! Come on!" Connor called for him, and Sparky came in smiling.
			"There's a dog bed in your room, too - though, if you normally let him sleep on the bed with you, you can do that here too. Just don't tell Catherine." William smirked. Connor chuckled and nodded gratefully.

		SCENE
			The next morning, Connor awoke. He yawned - that bed was very soft. Not as soft as Chloe's bed in her apartment, but maybe that was just because he had her with him... he snapped out of it. No time for daydreaming about her.
			He re-made the bed, morphed a fresh set of clothes, and headed downstairs. He smelled bacon. He walked into the kitchen, and saw a young woman in a maid's outfit, cooking. Next to her, a woman in a nurse's uniform sipped a coffee. A network of lined, aged scars crisscrossed around her arm and neck.
			"Oh... Good morning! I don't think we've met. I'm Connor." he said, greeting both.

			"Um--if it's going." he shrugged awkwardly, scratching the back of his had.

			"[I've missed you so much! How have you been?]" she said, in perfect Russian. 
			"[Oh, I've missed you too, dorogaya! I'm fine, how's school?]" Sveta replied, smiling warmly.
			"[Good, good! I'm not learning anything, as usual!]" Chloe smirked.
			Sveta laughed. "[Haha! As it should be.]"
			Connor looked at Chloe, amazed. "I didn't know you spoke Russian!" he said. She smiled.
			"Well, we have Russian family. But mainly, I learned it for Sveta."
			She gestured to Sveta, who nodded and smiled.
			"She is a good girl. Very bright." Sveta said, this time in English. "You are her friend?"
			"Uh, yes, we're friends." Connor said. Chloe smiled, as she put on her glasses.
			"Oh, good morning Olivia!" she beamed.
			"Good morning, Chloe!" she smiled back.
			Chloe turned to Sveta. "[How have things been since I was away?]"
			As she said this, Catherine appeared.
			"Chloe, in case you've forgotten, we speak English in this country." she frowned. Sveta silently scoffed.
			"Wow, sorry I took the effort to learn your parents' language." Chloe rolled her eyes.
			"Maybe if you put more effort into school, you wouldn't be studying in a dump like Drackhill." Catherine scowled.
			Connor, sipping a coffee Olivia made for him, nodded thankfully at her. "Good morning, Mrs. Derrington." he began.
			Catherine ignored him, as Chloe turned to face her.
			"First, Drackhill isn't a bad school - especially not for Biotech. Second, a city isn't bad just because it's poor. I've only just got back home and I've already had it to the back teeth with your classism!"
			"Classism?! I am trying to ensure my children have the best life they can! Sorry if that makes me a bad mother!" Catherine snapped back. Both women were now openly scowling at each other.
			"Chloe..." Connor said, trying to calm her, but she was fired up. Olivia quietly pretended like she needed something from the pantry.
			"No, what made you a bad mother was treating me like dirt and putting Victor on a pedestal our whole lives. Hey, maybe if you'd've actually put some effort in with me, I might not hate this place so much I had to move as far away as possible for uni!"

			With that, William came down the stairs. "Enough!" he snapped. Both women stopped, but continued scowling at each other.

			With that, Catherine's face scrunched - if she were a dog, she'd have snarled there - and she stormed off, heading back upstairs.
			"I'm sorry..." Chloe said, her face red. She turned to face Connor. "Connor, I'm sorry, I shouldn't have been like that in front of you." 
			Connor smiled gently. "It's okay. Hey, it's okay." Chloe moved in and hugged him. He returned it.
			William sighed. "I'm sorry, Connor. Catherine has been so rude to you."
			Connor shrugged. "It's okay. Honestly, that bed was so comfy - it's a fair trade." he smirked, eliciting a chuckle from William and Chloe.
			"Are you staying for breakfast?" William asked.
			"I'd love to." Connor nodded. William and Chloe smiled. Olivia finished making breakfast, as Sveta brought Oliver in on a wheelchair.
			Chloe hugged him. "Hi, grandad!" she smiled.
			"Hello, dear! You're looking very well!" he said loudly. His voice was hoarse, and his eyes were clouded by cataracts.
			Chloe turned. "Connor, this is my grandad, Oliver." she smiled.
			Connor put his hand out. "Hello, Oliver! How are you?"
			"Hello there, young man!" Oliver said, taking Connor's hand. "You're growing up so fast. How is school going?"
			Connor tilted his head slightly, and William rubbed the bridge of his nose. Chloe leaned in.
			"Just go along with it." she whispered.
			Connor nodded. "School's going well!" he said, putting on a posher voice. Chloe chuckled quietly at his impression.
			Once finished, Connor walked to his car with Sparky. As he approached his car, Chloe followed him. Now having a moment to themselves, she blushed.
			"I'm sorry about earlier... I just, I'm fed up with her. She acts like she's the mother from heaven and I'm the daughter from hell."
			Connor smiled softly. "It's okay. Really, it is. Besides, like I said, my uncle's in prison. It's not like I can sit in judgement on other people's family dynamics."
			Chloe chuckled. "Well, at least your uncle sounds alright. Hey, speaking of... Last night, you said there's the law, and then there's right and wrong. I... I didn't mean to imply that I was judging you and your uncle." she said, looking down shyly.
			"Oh? I didn't even think of that - it's okay." Connor smiled. Chloe looked relieved.
			"That's good." she smiled. "I was worried that it might come off as some... I don't know, like I was trying to insult you in the subtext? Which I wasn't, to be clear." she stammered.
			"Oh, god, don't do that - you wanna insult me, your best bet is just saying it openly. You know me and subtext." Connor chuckled. Chloe smirked.
			"Hah, forgot about that. I'll bear that in mind." she said. "To be honest, it's refreshing."
			"Oh?"
			"Well... I don't have to worry about subtext with you. I know that when you say something, there's no hidden meaning. And I don't have to worry about how you'll take something I say, either." she explained.
			"I guess being autistic as all hell has some advantages." Connor quipped.
			Both laughed at that, and she bade him farewell with a hug.

	EPISODE - Year's End
		______________________________
		SCENE
			The sky seemed almost determined to make this morning as miserable as possible. Slushy, cold sleet pelted down into the valley. Despite this, it failed to ruin the Barrett's morning.
			After all, it was Christmas.
			Connor, Amy, and Sparky stood outside the prison. A buzzer went off, and Vince came out. 
			Amy ran over to embrace him.
			"Vince! Oh, I've missed you..." she said.
			"Oh, I have missed you so much, sweetheart." Vince replied, returning the embrace. He released her, and pulled Connor in for a bear hug.
			"Good to see you again, lad." he said.
			Connor returned the embrace, and replied "Missed you." while smiling.
			"And who's this?!" Vince said, facing Sparky, his face full of glee. "Good boy! Very well behaved, waiting to say hi! Come on!"
			With that, Sparky jumped up and began to lick Vince's face.
			"Hello! Hi! I'm Sparky! You're part of Connor's pack, which means we're family! Hello!"
			"Hah! Well, hello to you too! What a chatty boy!" Vince said, hearing only barks and yaps.
			With that, the group headed back to Riverside for Christmas dinner.
			"So... welcome to our new place." Connor gestured. "Work on the motel finished just ahead of schedule - so we finally have bedrooms again."
			Vince grinned. "This is incredible. You've both come so far."
			"Yeah. We've gone from living it large in a nice flat to squatting in a fuckin' garage." Amy snarked. The family laughed heartily, before sitting down for food.
			Vince ate well, enjoying the break from prison slop.
			"This is amazing! Who made this?" he asked between mouthfuls.
			"Uh, well..." Amy began shyly. "The shop made it. Pre-stuffed turkey. I just put it in the oven."
			"Hah! Wonders of modern society, eh? Good lass." Vince said, beaming with pride. Amy smiled happily.
			"The garden's lovely, too." Vince smiled. "Bet the wee man loves it. For a wolfdog, he's so well behaved - I'm surprised he hasn't torn this place to shreds."
			"I get plenty of excercise!" Sparky yapped happily, having greedily devoured his own bowl. He was now shamelessly begging for more food.
			"Amy..." he began, targeting the weakest link. "I'm so hungry... Connor never feeds me..."
			His pupils had almost engulfed his brilliant yellow irises.
			Amy chuckled. Connor gave her a subtle nod.
			"Go on, then, buddy. Only one, okay?" she said, giving him a sausage that was practically inhaled. She hesitated, giggled, and gave him another.
			It was never really 'only one' with him.
			Once the eating was done, Amy played a song on her guitar to everyone.
			"Wow." Vince said at last, almost crying. "I remember when you first played guitar, when you were wee."
			"Yeah, it was terrible." Connor grinned. "And look at you now."
			"Fuck you." she grinned. She may well have been the only person on Earth who could say that with such warmth.
			"So?" Vince piped up. "Any other news with yous?"
			"Oh, well, I've got a new job at a dog daycare." Amy began.
			"That's amazing." Vince beamed.
			"If she needs any tips on how we think, just let me know." Sparky grinned while nursing his full belly. Connor chuckled.

			Connor stood outside with Sparky, as he did his business on the grass.
			"Hey, bud." he began.
			"Hello!" Sparky replied, smiling. "That food was really nice! Can we have Christmas every year?"
			"Haha! Yeah, don't worry - Christmas is a yearly thing." Connor replied.
			"Yay! I can't wait until next year!" Sparky yapped, excited.
			"Haha, good... Hey, there's something I want to do, but I won't do it if you don't want to."
			"What's that?" Sparky asked, tilting his head.
			"...I'm going to tell Vince about us. I mean, about what we really are."
			"Okay!" Sparky said, as nonchalantly as a talking wolf could.
			"That's it? You're not... scared?" Connor asked, surprised.
			"He's part of our pack, isn't he? He'll be happy to learn more about us, then."
			"Hah, I guess you're right..." Connor replied, deep in thought. He headed back inside.

			"Um... Vince?" he began, nervously.
			"Everything okay, lad?" Vince asked.
			"I... I need to show you something."
			"What is it?" he tilted his head.
			"So... I don't suppose you've heard about this mutant vigilante - they call him the Werewolf?" Connor asked timidly.
			"Where are you going with this?"
			Amy gave Connor a knowing nod of tacit approval.
			Connor didn't answer. Instead, he activated his morphing powers. His clothes turned black and melted, covering his body completely. The biomass hardened, forming itself into his kevlar bodysuit - the costume now famously associated with the Werewolf. Vince turned pale. Connor un-morphed the mask, so his head became exposed. He sighed.
			"I'm sorry, I wanted to tell you sooner..."
			"Connor... Connor, my sweet lad... Who did this to you?" Vince asked, tears forming in his eyes.
			"I don't know yet." Connor replied, choking back tears. "But I'm going to find out."
			"Did you know?" he asked Amy.
			"Yeah." she admitted. "I found out last month."
			"How?"
			"I, uh... accidentally shapeshifted in front of her." Connor explained nonchalantly. "Um... long story."
			"Who else knows?" Vince stammered.
			"Tommy. Trey found out a couple of nights ago. And I have a contact in the KGB who knows my real name, too."
			Vince leant against a wall, deep in consideration.
			"So..." he began. "You're the Werewolf? The one that killed Hughes?"
			"I..." Connor looked down, ashamed. "Yes."
			Vince paused for a moment, deep in thought. Then, he looked Connor in the eye.
			"Connor, my boy..." he said, tears now openly streaming down his face - but tears of pride. "You did good. You did very, *very* good."
			"I killed a man! Not just that, but I've been lying to everyone I care about! How can you be okay with this?!" Connor asked, crying now, practically begging to be condemned by his loved ones - begging for them to feel about him the way he felt about himself. 
			But Vince denied this with a simple embrace.
			"You didn't kill a man." he whispered. "You saved hundreds of young kids who were being trafficked by a monster. There are children who haven't been snatched from their mothers because of what you did. How could I ever judge you for that?"
			Connor sighed deeply.
			"Connor..." Vince smiled warmly. "I won't tell a soul. Your secret is safe, lad. Just... Be safe. And find the bastards that did this to you. Don't let them do it to anyone else."
			"I won't. Thank you..." Connor replied, smiling.
			Sparky barked. "See! I told you he'd understand!"
			"Oh yeah, Sparky can talk." Amy added.
			"WHAT?!" Vince gasped.
			The kids laughed giddily, and sat back down.

			Another hour passed, and Vince hugged his children, before going back to prison. Once he left, Amy and Connor sat down in the kitchen, missing him already. Sparky nuzzled between them.
			"That went well." Amy smiled.
			"Yeah." Connor nodded. "I just... I'm sick of lying."
			"I know..." she sighed. "But you can't tell people. Telling Vince was okay, but this needs to stay secret."
			"Pretty much everyone knows. It's just Chloe and Bea." he shrugged.
			"Yeah, but... not yet, okay?"
			"I know, I know..." Connor leant back.
			"Anyway... How are things going?" she asked.
			"We found out the name of the cabal we're fighting." he shrugged.
			"Who are they?"
			"They're called the Optimates." he began. "A conspiracy of the ruling class. Corporate fascists."
			"Holy shit." Amy turned pale. "And they're the ones making superhumans?"
			"Yeah." Connor nodded. "Some kind of ubermensch bullshit, only it somehow worked."
			"Doesn't make any sense." Amy shook her head. "Fascists never read to me as very clever or logical. There was a documentary I saw the other night about Mengele - he wasn't a mad scientist, he was just mad."
			"They probably stole whatever it is they know. Or they have ties to a laboratory that *is* staffed with clever people."
			"You say that like you know something..." Amy tilted her head.
			"Yeah... it gets worse."
			"How can it get worse than fascist super-soldiers?" she groaned.
			His face turned serious. "Chloe."
			"She knows?"
			"No. But she's working at that big genetics company in Belson, right? And they've got her working on the Werewolf case, studying the various superhuman DNA they've found. And the company she works for... They're connected to the Optimates." Connor said, his expression grim.
			Amy's face turned pale. "Oh my god... but why? I mean, she's only a uni placement student - why would they have her working such an important case?"
			"That's what I wondered when I found out. I mean, she's brilliant in biotechnology, but still... We think they put her there as a human shield." Connor replied, his voice cold.
			"What do you mean?" Amy asked.
			"Well, I have a tendency to smash the places connected to them. If she's there, there's no way I'm starting a fight there. Whatever it is they're doing at Vitalis, they need me to stay out of it. And I can't look into it without putting her at risk. I can't even tell her without putting her at risk."
			"That, or they're using her as bait." Amy added, her face betraying fear. "If she's involved, you're going to be focused on Vitalis. Maybe something's going to happen there, and they can hold her ransom through that."
			Connor slumped into his chair, pale as a ghost. "Whatever the reason is, it cannot be a good one. And it's all because of me..."
			"No." Amy interrupted. "It's because of who-the-fuck these people are. Do *not* cut them any slack here. I know you have feelings for Chloe, deny it all you like. But she's my friend too. And I will not let these bastards hurt her. Which means..." Amy paused for breath. "It means you need to find out what's going on. They've put her in harms way to stop you from learning something, right? So, learn it. The most dangerous place for Chloe right now is at arm's reach. It is not safe to let them continue. So, don't let them." she said authoritatively.
			Connor sighed, a mix of relief and fear. "I won't." he vowed.
			"But what I said before still stands. Do not tell her, or anyone else." she said firmly. "This day and age, the walls don't just have eyes - they have ears and noses too. All it takes is for one person you've told to slip up - not even betraying you, just making one mistake at the wrong moment - for this whole thing to collapse. As long as these bastards are out there, this has to remain under wraps."
			"I won't tell anyone else." Connor nodded, accepting the situation as it was.

			He hesitated, but cleared his throat.
			"I, uh... I wanna show you both something."
			Amy tilted her head as he stood.
			He logged into the computer. "I, uh... I did some digging. About your mum. I found this."
			He brought up a photograph of two people - a young woman, and an older man.
			"Who are they?" she asked.
			"Your mum, and her dad." he said softly.
			She sat down, looking closer. Without thinking, her hand reached out, gently burushing her mother's face.
			"I... I've never seen a photo of her before."
			"Dr. Zhao Mei. She graduated medical school a few years before you were born." Connor explained. "I couldn't find any information on who your father was, but..."
			"But?"
			Connor hesitated. "There's, um... there's something you need to know about your grandad."
			He pressed a few buttons, pulling up a profile.
			"Dr. Zhao Liang. Biochemist from the PRC. He and your mum moved here after his wife - your nan - passed away. And the weird thing is, he went off-grid completely after you were born. But it gets worse - not only do I kind of recognise him, but the name - Dr. Zhao - I heard it before. When I was being tortured."
			"Are you kidding me?!" Amy gasped. "You knew someone in my family was involved?"
			"Amy, 2% of everyone in China has the surname Zhao. You're not connected to all of them."
			She sighed. "Sorry, just... this is a lot to process."
			"If it helps, I don't think he was invovled willingly." Connor smiled softly. "But he vanished right after your birth. I don't know anything yet... but I have a hunch he was involved in whatever happened when we were born. And worse, that implies the Optimates might've been involved too."
			Amy looked down, her skin paler than before. She tabbed back over to the photo.
			"They're both so... they look happy, at least."
			"Whoever Dr. Zhao is... we can assume he was a good father." Connor nodded. "I'll find him. And you can ask him everything you wanna know."
			She paused. Then she turned, and embraced her brother.
			"Thank you... really. This means a lot."
			"Don't mention it." Connor smiled warmly.
			She stretched out, yawning. "I'd better get to bed, I've got work tomorrow."
			"One more thing - I found a few more photos of her. I'll send them over to you - let you go over them in private."
			She squeezed him tight. It took a while for her to let go.
			"See you later, sis." he nodded.
			She smiled, slightly teary-eyed. "Yeah. See you later."

		Barrett Family Christmas
		______________________________
		SCENE
			That same day, Trey was having dinner at his grandparents' house. Trey's uncle and auntie, as well as his two cousins, were present too, though they kept their distance from him. The house was adorned with crucifixes, Union Jacks, and Jamaican kicknacks - a typical Windrush generation house. While eating, Trey spoke up.
			"Nana, this is amazing - the turkey is so succulent!" he said cheerfully.
			His grandmother smiled. "Glad you like it, my boy." she replied in a heavy Jamaican accent.
			His grandfather chuckled. "The turkey is good, but the pigs-in-blankets? Oh my! You can thank our Patricia for that." he cheered, looking lovingly at his wife.
			"You just lucky they all here - if it were me and you, Jamal, I'd serve ya pasta and rice!" she said, eliciting laughter across the table.
			Trey's uncle piped up. "So, Trey. How's life been?"
			"Good, thank you." Trey replied tensely. "Work has been hectic, but at least the pay's gone up."
			"And socially?" his uncle continued. "Any new girlfriends?"
			"No. I went on a date with a boy the other week though." Trey replied, stressing the word "Boy."
			His auntie dropped her fork and gasped. "Not at the dinner table."
			"Indeed." his uncle scowled. "We don't want to hear about your--"
			"Andrew." Patricia said sternly. "You asked our Trey about girlfriends. If he said he'd been on a date with a girl, you wouldn't be moanin' and whinin'. All you should care about is that your nephew is happy."
			"I--" Andrew began, but stopped himself. He continued his food.
			Jamal chimed in. "Wicked boy. Don't be tellin' people we raised ya like that! Should be you with the pasta and the rice." With that, Trey laughed, causing his grandparents to chuckle. Phil beamed with pride at his son, and then turned to Trey's older cousin.
			"So, Jamie! How about you? Any new boyfriends?" he asked provocatively.
			Jamie caught the hint and smirked. "Oh yeah, loads. Total battyboy, me."
			Trey erupted into laughter. "I never should have taught you that word!"
			With that, his grandparents laughed too.
			"Oh, see! You tellin' everybody I told Jamie to say battyboy. The truth is comin' out in spades! Pennies dropping left, right, and centre!" Jamal grinned at Patricia, who chuckled delightfully.
			"Just because you're not guilty here, doesn't mean you're not guilty there, you wicked rogue." she retorted.
			Andrew was openly scowling at Trey and Phil, but chose not to cause a scene. The family finished dinner and sat down.

			"...and so she says to me, "Don't look at me with that tone of voice! It smells a funny colour!"" Jamal finished an anecdote with, causing an eruption of laughter across the room.
			"Right, we'd best be off soon." Phil said, checking his phone.
			"So soon?" Patricia asked, saddened.
			"Sorry, mama - we've got to go see Kerry's folks." Phil explained, his voice breaking ever-so-slightly at the mention of his late wife.
			Patricia's expression changed to one of understanding. "Of course, my boy. We'll see you soon." She stood up and hugged Trey. "Bye, my little angel."
			"See you soon, nana. Love you." Trey replied, hugging back. 
			"Love you too, me boy. God bless." she replied, smiling.
			Jamal stood up.
			"Be safe, my boys. Merry Christmas." Jamal said to both, hugging Trey, and then hugging Phil, who responded in kind.
			"See you." Andrew said to both, not standing up. Jamal and Patricia scoffed. Jamie and Trey's younger cousin stood up and hugged both goodbye. Trey's aunt stood and hugged both. She whispered an apology for her earlier behaviour in Trey's ear, which he gratefully accepted.
			
			The two arrived at Kerry's parents' house. Trey and Phil sat in the car for a moment, before taking an intake of breath. Phil had gripped the steering wheel hard enough to show the whites of his knuckles. Trey had accidentally cut his hand from scratching it in nervousness. They inhaled, then exhaled, in unison. They got out the car and exchanged supportive glances at each other. They knocked on the door.
			Kerry's father, George, answered the door. Upon seeing the two, he became visibly disappointed. "Fine. Come in." he said through gritted teeth. The two entered.
			The house was almost hypnotically minimalist. Unlike Phil's parents, Kerry's were born in the UK, and so spoke with English accents. Kerry's mother, Gloria, came in and hugged both.
			"Merry Christmas! How has your day been?" she asked. George rolled his eyes at this.
			"It's been good, nan. How has yours been?" Trey replied, smiling sadly. She was visibly drunk.
			"Good! Neither of us wanted to cook, so we had a Chinese instead." she replied, slurring slightly.
			George came in. Phil revealed the presents they brought. Gloria excitedly opened hers - first, she opened Phil's present.
			"Ah! I've been looking everywhere for this!" she said, holding the gift - a device which converted tapes into digital files - with glee.
			"Well, they don't sell them in shops anymore - I got that one online." Phil smiled.
			"Ah, I never got on with online shopping." Gloria said, cheerfully. She opened Trey's gift next.
			"Oh wow! Thank you so much sweetheart!" she said, holding the gift - a blanket hoodie with hand-and-foot warmers - high in the air.
			"Glad you like it, nan! I know you get cold at night sometimes, what with your circulation... I thought it might help you." Trey said shyly.
			"Such a sweet boy. I think I've got your presents here somewhere... Ah!" she handed both their presents.
			"Oh... a £20 gift voucher to ASDA. That's... Thank you so much!" Trey said, trying his hardest to be appreciative.
			"Ah... socks! Can never have enough of those!" Phil put on a smile. Trey looked over at George, who had not sat down yet - despite his bad leg.
			He refused to show any hospitality. He also had not acknowledged the presents brought for him.
			"Uh, grandad..." Trey began. George scowled at being called that. "These presents are for you... Merry Christmas. I hope you like them."
			George scoffed.
			"Is it your mother, returned to life?" he asked. Trey, Phil, and Gloria all looked down. "No? Didn't think so. Then I don't want it." he snarled.
			"George, please... Trey is all that we have left of Kerry." Gloria began, but she buttoned it once George continued.
			"Oh? And why is that? Oh that's right, because she *DIED* giving birth to him! And who's fault is that?" George growled, almost ferally.
			Gloria looked down in fear, shaking slightly at George's outburst.
			"Why are you defending him? Eh? You'd rather stick up for your daughter's killer than you would your daughter?!" he asked, looming over her. She cowered away from him. 
			"Stop blaming my dad for what happened!" Trey snapped.
			"Oh, don't worry - I blame you plenty." George snarled back.
			"Enough!" Phil snapped. "We came here hoping to bridge the gap. I would never dream of keeping your only grandson away from you. But I can tell when we're not wanted. So, thank you for the gifts, Gloria, merry Christmas to you. Good night." Phil said. Both Trey and Phil left.
			George shouted out as they got in the car.
			"A couple of poncey gifts won't bring her back! You killed my daughter, Morgan! Both of you!" he screamed, throwing his gifts at their car. Trey cried silently while his dad drove them home. They entered their house, and started to openly cry with each other.

		Morgan Family Christmas
		______________________________
		SCENE
			The aftermath of Christmas dinner at the Jefferson household was peaceful, if a little sluggish. The room practically oozed warmth - the scent of cinnamon and roast goose still clung to the air. Bea lay sprawled across a reclining sofa, her stomach full, her eyelids heavy. Her year-younger sister, Tea, was fast asleep across the room, wrapped in a throw blanket. Their dad had retired upstairs for a nap, and their mum had disappeared into the bath nearly an hour ago, likely dozing there too.

			Her phone buzzed softly on the side table. She blinked slowly, and reached for it.
			"Merry Christmas, gorgeous." Charlie had written. "I hope your day's been magical. I've been thinking about you all day. I got you a little something... was wondering if I could see you? Just for a bit. If not, that's okay. I get it."
			She smiled, cheeks warming. She tapped out a reply.
			"Merry Christmas! It's been lovely – my family are all in food comas lol. Hope yours has been good too?"
			He replied almost instantly.
			"It's been fine. Quiet. Just wish I had someone around who really gets me, you know? Everyone's so wrapped up in their own little worlds. It would be lovely if you wanted to meet up?"
			Something about the phrasing made Bea pause. She bit her lip, then typed:
			"Where would you want to meet?"
			"The town square? Or... you could come to mine? It's warm. I've got mulled wine and an actual fireplace lol." he sent.
			Her fingers hovered, hesitant.
			"I can meet at the park for a bit! I can't stay too long though – everyone's asleep but I'll need to be back soon."
			"Sure." he replied abruptly.
			She stood up quietly and grabbed her coat.
			"Where are you off to?" Tea murmured from beneath the blanket, revealing herself. She was almost identical to Bea in terms of facial structure. However, where Bea's skin was a constellation of vitiligo, Tea's was a solid sheet of light-brown. Where Bea's eyes contrasted through heterochromia, Tea's were both a shimmering hazel.
			In most dynamics, the 'normal' sister would be the suave, confident one; while the 'abnormal' would be shy and socially deprived. The key word there was 'most.'
			Tea's clothes were almost impressively plain. A grey hoodie over light blue jeans - in this case, unbuttoned at the top to accommodate Christmas dinner. Her hair was as curly as Bea's, but rather than the bright and loud red-dyed afro bob that Bea had opted for, her thick curls had been bunched into a low ponytail, with a few strands dangling in front of her face. All in all, neither sister could be put into a label - fittingly, neither would desire to be.
			"Just a walk." Bea whispered. "I'll be back soon."
			The streets were cold and slick. The sky was darkening, the stars blurry behind thin clouds. Bea pulled her coat tighter as she reached the park. 
			Charlie stood waiting, hands in his coat pockets, eyes on the ground.
			He looked up and smiled as she approached. "Hey."
			"Hey!" she replied, breath puffing in the cold.
			"I didn't think you'd come." he began. His voice was low. "I thought maybe you'd changed your mind."
			"No, I just didn't want to stay long. Everyone's still up, mostly."
			He pulled a small wrapped box from his coat and handed it to her.
			Bea opened it carefully. Inside was a delicate silver bracelet.
			She stared at it. "Charlie... this is beautiful."
			He smiled.
			She looked down at the bracelet again. "Thank you. Really."
			He reached forward, brushing her hair behind her ear. "You don't have to say anything. Just being here... it means more than you know."
			She nodded, pushing her face into his hand.
			"I wanted to give you something that reminded you how different you are. How real." he said. "Not like... the people around you."
			She shifted. "Charlie..."
			"I mean, it's nice they're there," he said, too quickly. "But they don't see you. Not like I do. You said yourself you feel like the extra in your own friend group sometimes."
			"I didn't mean it like that," she said, suddenly uncomfortable.
			He studied her for a moment, then reached for her hands. "Come back to mine?"
			She blinked. "What?"
			"Just for a bit." he said quickly. "I've got this bottle of wine I've been saving, and I made mince pies. I thought... maybe we could just have a moment. Something that's ours."
			"I can't, sorry. I should probably head back soon," she said, almost apologetically.
			His expression shifted. The smile disappeared. "Right."
			She frowned. "I'm sorry, I just - "
			"It's fine," he said sharply, pulling his hands away. "It's totally fine. I just thought maybe you'd want to spend time with me. Guess I misread things."
			"Charlie, I--"
			"No, it's okay. Seriously. Don't worry about it." His tone was brittle. "Enjoy your perfect little family night."
			"That's not fair," Bea said, a tremble in her voice.
			He turned away, jaw tight. "You know what? Just forget I asked. I shouldn't have. This was stupid."
			There was a beat of silence, and then, as suddenly as he had snapped, he softened.
			"I'm sorry," he said, running a hand through his hair. "God, I'm such an idiot. You didn't deserve that. I just... I missed you so much today. I guess I let it get to me."
			Bea stood frozen.
			"I'm sorry, Bea. I just thought... I thought we had something. And I thought maybe today, of all days, I'd matter enough to you to get a little of your time. But it's okay. Really."
			He offered a weak smile, eyes sad. "Go home. They'll miss you."
			Bea gulped, a lump in her throat. "Of course you matter to me. It's just... it's Christmas, you know? We see each other every day at uni."
			"You don't have to explain." he said, backing away.
			She didn't reply. She couldn't. Her feet felt stuck to the pavement.
			"Merry Christmas, Bea." he whispered.
			And then he was gone, his footsteps echoing off the wet stones, leaving her standing alone with the bracelet still in her hands.
			She sighed deeply.

You don't have to decide anything now - I advise you to seek out family and friends, and seek comfort from that." she said kindly.
			"I... thank you, doctor. I... I'll..." he sobbed. "I'll come to the hospital tomorrow morning."
			"Thank you, Mr. Naismith. Please take your time, and look after yourself. Once again, I'm very sorry for your loss."
			With that, Naismith put down the phone, and found himself in a room with an older woman, with a notepad and pen.
			"So, Henry... how are you feeling?" she asked.
			"Fine." Naismith replied bluntly.
			The woman noted something down. "And how has work been going?"
			"Fine." Naismith replied again. The woman again made a note.
			"Have you been meditating like we practiced?" she asked softly.
			"No." he replied in the same tone.
			"That's okay. It doesn't work for everyone. We all process grief in different ways."
			"I'm fine." Naismith said firmly. The woman shook her head.
			"Henry, it's okay to feel anything. Emotions are always valid." she said calmly.
			Naismith's expression hardened. "I said I'm fine. Is it that hard to believe?" he snapped.
			"Henry, your fiancee died in a tragic accident. It's only natural to want to... to bury these emotions. But if you don't accept them, we cannot deal with them." she sighed, with an almost motherly concern about her.
			Naismith's expression became even more grim. "Stop it."
			"Henry..." she began, but he cut her off by shouting.
			"I said stop it!" he barked. She crossed her legs and frowned.
			"I'm fine. I am always fine. And I'm sick of people pestering me! Go to therapy, this - take some time off, that. I've had enough. Do you hear me? Enough! An innocent man has been locked away, by a bunch of racist twats - purely because I *tried* to process these emotions. No more. No more!" he stormed out of the room, slamming the door. With that, he jolted awake.
			Naismith - the same, older, haggard Naismith - curled into a ball and sobbed. He headed into the kitchen to made a coffee, and while searching for his cigarettes, put his hand on his pistol. He pulled it out, and stared at it. He sat on the ground, still staring. He loaded the chamber, cocked it, and pushed it into his temple.
			"One second. That's all it'll take. One tiny little push, and *poof* - all your troubles gone. All your pain and sadness painting the walls of this rotten old house." he mumbled to himself.
			He steeled himself. He took a sharp intake of breath. He closed his eyes tightly.
			"Okay, Naismith. This time, you're really going to do it. Okay. One, Two..."
			"WOOF!"
			Naismith put down the gun, to see Max staring at him, whimpering. He smiled. He dropped the gun, and broke down in tears.
			"You're right. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Max... I'm so sorry." he sobbed. Max cuddled into him and licked his tears away. Naismith stood, picked up his gun. Max whimpered, but Naismith uncocked it, took out the magazine, and emptied the chamber. The ease at which he did this even when drunk was indicative of his skill at arms.
			"It's okay, buddy." Naismith smiled at Max. "I'm not going anywhere. We still have work to do."

Like, I mean, it's not like..." Connor trailed off, stumbling on his words. Trey laughed warmly, and pulled Connor in for an embrace.

			Chloe was in the lab, along with her supervisor. She was delivering a presentation to Gregory Morland, the CEO.

			"And what does it do?" Morland asked, intrigued.
			"Well, it... It amplifies their physical abilities - Paradrenaline binds more effectively to the adrenergic receptors in the body, particularly the alpha-1 and beta-2 receptors, responsible for increasing heart rate, blood flow, and muscle contraction. The result is a massive enhancement of physical capabilities: regenerative healing, increased reflexes, and a dramatic rise in strength. But--" she paused, "There are side effects."
			Morland leant forward, his gaze intense. "What kind of side effects?"
			"Well..." Chloe cleared her throat. "At low doses, subjects begin to experience neurological symptoms, primarily intense migraines and frequent nosebleeds. These occur due to an overstimulation of the sympathetic nervous system, which causes vasodilation in the brain, increasing pressure and causing the blood vessels to rupture."
			Morland raised an eyebrow but said nothing, so Chloe continued, tapping the screen to show the next slide.
			"At moderate doses, we start seeing seizures. The neurons in the brain become hyper-excitable due to an imbalance in the sodium and potassium ion channels. It's like a short circuit in the nervous system. The more the subject's body is exposed to Paradrenaline, the more severe the disruption becomes."
			Morland winced, his lips curling into a slight smile. "And at high doses?"
			Chloe's voice lowered, growing more serious. "At high doses, the symptoms are catastrophic. Strokes, aneurysms, and cerebral haemorrhages. The vasculature in the brain becomes too fragile, and the heart rate increases to dangerous levels, putting immense strain on the circulatory system."
			Morland watched her intently, considering her words. "But the superhumans, they survive these doses?"
			"Yes." she nodded. "We believe it's due to their enhanced anatomy. Their bodies seem to compensate for the damage. Their regenerative abilities kick in faster than normal, allowing them to recover from the worst effects. But it's still a temporary fix - they can only withstand so much before the damage becomes incapacitating."

			Grozny, Chechen ASSR. 18th of February, 2009.

			The evacuation would have been doomed - were it not for the 9th Motor Rifle Division's timely arrival.
			This was going to be the Battle of Grozny.

			The Division's commander, Major Iosef Tarkovsky - an older man, with a nervous disposition - was surveying some maps, alongside his aides.
			"[It's a mess out there.]" Tarkovsky noted dryly.
			"[Yes, sir.]" an aide nodded. "[Our current strategy is to have Makharadze and Lebedev reinfoce Ahmadov - the de-facto leader of the Loyalist forces. From there, general Trepov will come in from the north, and close in on the insurgents. Once they are put to rout, we will complete the evacuation.]"
			"[Is there any hope of us taking the city?]" Tarkovsky asked wearily.
			"[I'm afraid not, sir. Even if Zamaldayev died here, the city is effectively lost to us. Our only hope is to cross back over the mountains, and pray Moscow hasn't fallen when we get there.]"
			"[So be it.]" Tarkovsky sighed. "[Begin the operation.]"

			An hour had passed. In Lebedev's brigade, the fighting was intense. Separatist forces anticipated the maneuver, and intercepted before Lebedev could reach the convoy.

			"[You'll be okay, dorogaya.]" she said softly, trying to calm him.

She looked over at the young man, whose wound was torn open by the blast. He was dead.

			"I'm FBI. My expertise extends to "Some of the drugs we caught the CIA selling originated here.""

			"Buena caza, mi amigo." he grinned. Connor smirked, and drove onwards.

			Over in Belson, Chloe began looking over the lab rats they'd been applying serum to.
			"By the way, Jones..." she began, her brow furrowed. "Where are we getting all this from?"
			"Downstairs - that's all I know." Jones shrugged. "Anyway, findings?"
			"Applying it to adults has had a number of effects. Major increases in musclemass, bone density, endurance... and some small cognitive improvements."
			"Any drawbacks?"
			"Increased aggression, and signs of pain - courtesy of the paradrenaline, no doubt. Also, they become completely sterile. Their germ cells have completely random numbers of chromosomes, or sometimes none at all. Even stranger, the males appear to have a tiny number of inert egg cells developing in their testes, while the females have inert sperm cells in their ovaries. Likely, the mutations have confused their stem cells. That fits with my theory that their mutations are imperfect because their brain can't direct their generative cells properly."
			Jones nodded, stroking his chin. "What about the tests on pregnant rats?"
			Chloe shuddered slightly. "Injecting pregnant rats directly led to terminations of their pregnancies. Accepting the mutations makes you unable to bear children at all, it seems. As for in-utero exposure to the fetuses directly... Most of them simply spontanaeosly abort. A large number of the mother rats suffer severe aneurysms, too. It looks like serum-injected fetuses produce massive amounts of paradrenaline, which gets into the mother's system and causes the haemorrhaging. A couple of births have happened so far - all stillbirths... except for one."
			She showed him a tiny rat in an incubator. Despite all the other rats being albino as was common for lab-rats, including its parents - this one had healthy melanin levels.
			"Her mother died during birth, same as most. But she's the only one that survived in-utero exposure." she explained. "Rat pregnancies don't take long, and they give birth in litters - meaning we could produce several in a short amount of time. Still, there have been over 200 in-utero exposures, and she's the only one who survived."
			"Amazing..." Jones gasped. "Have you tested its DNA yet?"
			Chloe winced slightly at the use of 'It.' "No, not yet. She's still so fragile, I... I don't want to start taking samples until she gets a little bigger."
			"I understand..." Jones nodded. "But this has to be done. I'll take the sample - if anything goes wrong, it's my fault alone, okay?"
			Chloe sighed, but nodded silently, and left. Jones stuck a big needle into the tiny rat, and drew some blood into a vial.

			Outside Murillo's compound, Connor stood menacingly. Two guards stood outside the front gate.
			"Hey!" one guard barked. "Que crees que estas haciendo aqui?!"
			The two guards at the gate were professionals, armed with sleek rifles, not the patched-together gear of street thugs.

			This wasn't a normal gang. This was a private army.
			Behind Connor's back, his costume morphed. A crossbow formed around his wrist, and loaded itself with a ball. Connor rose this, and fired right into the guard's head.
			The guard's eyes rolled back, and he collapsed to the ground, out cold. The other rushed to draw his gun, but the crossbow reloaded and redrew itself without delay. It fired, taking that one down too. He morphed up his full suit, and re-created the ballistic shield from the bridge incident, before kicking the gate down.
			"MATALO!" a guard roared, as a hail of bullets came Connor's way. He ducked behind his shield, and thought for a second, before grinning. He morphed his crossbow throught the sheild - like a Roman ballista - and began shooting. He swapped his ammo out for makeshift Bolas - tangling the men onto the ground, gift-wrapped for the Federales.
			Women, drug dealers, and other civilians rushed out the gateway, as Connor continued through. Each shot of the bow sent another gunman down to the ground. Finally, the room went quiet, save the grunts and struggles of half-conscious gunmen.
			If the urge had a voice, it'd whine at the lack of slaughter. Connor took a breath, chuckling.
			He looked down, and realised his costume had gone thin - very thin. He used up most of its material making the Bolas, and would need time to regrow. Time he didn't have.
			He shrugged, and un-morphed the bow and shield, pushing it back under his skin to help him recover. He headed down to the basement.
			There, Murillo sat, holding his hands together. Not praying, but waiting. Two bodyguards opened fire, but Connor was a blur - taking both down in moments.

			"FBI's, actually." Connor chuckled. "Right, we can do this quick if you like - or you can monologue for bit, it's your choice."
			Murillo chuckled mirthlessly. "All this time, I kept wondering - will they send a man, or a missile? Looks like they sent both."
			His face turned to a scowl. "Your Optimate paymasters must be very proud."
			"I'm not with the Optimates." Connor growled. "I'm here because you're doing the same as them. And I'm the man - or the missile - who stops that."
			Murillo grinned. "That's life. It's evolution. Survival of the fittest. Now, Paladin's got it all wrong - they think being a gringo makes you superior. It doesn't. Only three things do - ruthless determination, stepping on every poor bastard beneath you... and this." he said, revealing a syringe of serum.
			"You're both wrong. Look at me - I'm supposed to be a super-weapon, and instead I protect people." Connor replied in cold defiance.
			"And who are you protecting right now? You're here to kill me!"
			"I'm protecting every poor bastard getting stepped on." Connor snarled back.
			Murillo sighed. "In this world, it's eat or be eaten. All that power, and you still don't get it."
			"I don't." said Connor, rising. "I don't understand why anyone would hurt other people like this. What is it? Simple greed? Lust for power? Spite?"
			"Spite." Murillo chuckled. "You know, I was an asset of the gringos - in the 2000s. You wanna watch them. They're manipulative, and conniving."

			"That's not what they told you?" Murillo chuckled. "No kidding. They tell lies as easily as breathe. You're on the wrong side, kid."

			"Join me." Murillo grinned devilishly. "I know my place in the food chain, and it's under you, and Paladin. But together... maybe we could take them down."
			Connor sheathed his blade. "Alright, I won't kill you."
			"Good... good..."
			"Don't get comfy. You're coming with me."

Anyway, skipping ahead a bit, following the October Revolution, Chechnya along with the rest of the Caucasus was re-integrated as part of the Greater Caucasian SFSR, which included Transcaucasia - places like Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan - and Ciscaucasia, where you'll find Ossetia, Dagestan, and relevant for us - Chechnya. And its current de-facto leader - Vadim Zamaldayev."

The impact was heavy, but his healing factor kicked in almost instantly, the wounds knitting back together. 			Chloe looked over, realising where she was. The alleyway Connor landed. The same alleyway he and Sparky saved her from all those months ago. There, she saw Banner - or what was left of him. He landed right on his head, and a pile of red mush was all that remained above his neck.
			But Connor... Connor landed back-first on a dumpster. He was bent backwards in a sickening, unnatural way - his back was snapped clean in half. Chloe fell down to her knees again.
			"Oh... Oh god..." she shuddered.
			"Listen." Gwen said firmly, grabbing her shoulders. "You know more than anyone else about his biology. Can we fix him?"
			"I--I--" she stuttered. She pulled his body from the dumpster, laying him down flat. He didn't breathe.
			"Connor... Connor, wake up. Come on, wake up. Please wake up... Hey, remember this alleyway? You saved me here, and you just saved me again. Come on... Come on, get up! That's an order!" she pleaded. She slammed his chest with her fist, causing a cracking noise from his spine.
			Whiplash tilted her head.
			"Come on, get up... Hey, if you get up, I'll... I'll forgive you, okay? I won't be mad, not even a little. Just... please wake up. You've survived so much, you can survive this! Please!" she sobbed. "Please..." she begged, as she hit his chest again. Another cracking noise.
			"Hit him again!" she nodded, stretching her hands out. "I'll redirect the force - if we can shift his spine back into place, he might be okay."
			Chloe cocked an eyebrow, but nodded, and hit him. And again. And again.
			With that...
			"GAAGGH!" Connor gasped, his eyes shooting open.
			"Connor?!" she looked up.
			"Agh... AAAGH!" he screamed in agony. He rolled onto his front and clutched his back.
			"Connor... Connor, what... What do I do?" she asked, tears streaming down her cheek.
			"Agh... Ah... I... Help..." he spluttered out, trying to stand. Chloe helped him up. He shouted in pain as he rose, but found his footing.
			"Connor, you... You're alive..." she whispered, in shock.
			With that, the police exited the building. "Area secure, sir!" Nina barked. "All hostages save one have been located."
			"I..." Chloe began. "You'd better go. If they find you..."
			"Chloe, I..." Connor started, but she raised her hand, silencing him.
			"We'll talk about this later, okay? I... I'll see you later." she said, and hugged him. Though his back was in agony, he hugged her too.
			"We'll glide back - the streets are locked down." Gwen nodded. "I'll keep you airborne, don't worry."
			"The cops will wanna question you." he choked, turning to Chloe. "When they're done, get them to drop you off at the repair shop. I'll explain everything, I promise."
			She nodded hesitantly, and he hobbled off into the distance. Gwen drew her glider, and an updraft took them into the sky.

		Telling the Truth

		SCENE
			Bullets flew overhead, ricocheting off the walls and the metal framework of the station as TO-24 took cover behind a crumbling pillar.

The force of the blow was enough to lift him off his feet.

		The Judge Awakens
		______________________________
		SCENE
			That night, Connor was sprinting, leaping from rooftop to rooftop in a patrol. While running, he heard a scream. He sprinted straight towards the source.
			There, he saw a monster grabbing a man in Skull leathers. The monster let the man go, and turned to face Connor.
			It was a freak that would make Nosferatu look pretty. Its skin was grey, and its eyes a dark blood-red, blending iris, pupil, and sclera. Its face was only vaguely human - its eyes too far apart, its nose at once too pointy and too flat, its jaw stuttered and spiked. All in all, it could only be described by negation - "Face not-quite-human," "Teeth not-quite-canine," "Frame not-quite-apelike."
			"This is Vanguard. Contact." he whispered in shock.
			The creature turned slowly, its face twisted into a grotesque grin.
			"Greetings, youngblood." it growled, lips curling. "Are you ready for your judgment?"
			Connor raised an eyebrow, taking a step forward. His usual cocky smirk formed. "Who the fuck are you?"
			"I am the Judge." the creature replied, showing its teeth, the grin stretching impossibly wide. "And I am your end, youngblood."
			Connor's smirk deepened. "Oh? Well, if you'll let me be the 'judge' for a second - I find you guilty of being fuck-ugly."
			The Judge's grin faltered for a moment, but then it returned, colder than before. "Such insolence, to curse and demean your natural ruler. The Lord has demanded your death."
			"'The Lord'? You mean the Commandant?" Connor asked, eyebrow raised.
			"Do not dare blaspheme in such ways." the Judge snarled, his voice venomous. "To compare the Lord to the Commandant is to compare a star to a single ember."
			Connor tilted his head, genuinely curious now. "Who are you? What, a preacher?"
			The Judge's eyes narrowed, a cold flicker passing through them. "No. You are mistaken. I do not come to bring the Word to the ears of mankind. I am the Judge. And I find you... guilty."
			His voice hardened, and his grip tightened on his weapons.
			Connor pressed, determined to understand. "Why are you doing this?"
			"You have failed this city." the Judge snarled. "You claim to protect the innocent, let you allow miscreants and parasites to draw breath. You are unwilling to mete out true justice upon this land!"
			"I stop monsters." Connor growled, rolling his shoulders. "And you're putting yourself in that category."
			The Judge's eyes flared. "Be silent." he snapped. "Your failures, your heresy, ends tonight. Either prostrate yourself before me and accept your place, or die at my feet. The choice is yours, youngblood."
			Connor stared at him, his expression hardening. "Have it your way." he muttered, his eyes flashing. He morphed his blades, their gleaming edges catching the light. "Let's dance."
			The Judge's grin widened. "I hereby sentence you to death." he said grimly. "May the Lord burn your soul for eternity."
			The dark urge chanted encouragingly.
			Without another word, they charged.

			The sound of their blades clashing rang out in the alley as the two monsters collided. The first thing Connor noticed was the Judge's strength - far greater than he expected. The creature moved with unnatural speed, his strikes heavy and relentless. Connor was forced to backpedal, his blades deflecting each blow.
			The Judge struck again, and this time, Connor's parry was too slow. The Judge's blade cut deep into Connor's thigh. Blood poured from the wound.
			Connor swung his blade with a growl, his edge slicing across the Judge's thigh. The creature howled in pain, stumbling back slightly, but the grin never left its face.
			The Judge's next move was swift - he brought his blade down toward Connor's head. Connor reacted instinctively, diving backward, barely avoiding the blow. He threw a knife, but the creature was too fast, parrying the blade with one of its own. The two made eye contact - two predators circling each other, their blades hungry for blood.
			"About time for a challenge." Connor thought, the adrenaline surging through him. His fear was buried deep, hidden beneath the hunger for battle.
			The Judge didn't waste time. He plunged his blade into the ground, sending a shockwave of energy through the earth. The pavement cracked, and gravel flew into the air. With a growl, the Judge charged forward, sweeping his blade up. The gravel cut into Connor's eyes, blinding him momentarily.
			Connor staggered back, wiping the dirt from his eyes, but the Judge was already on him. The second flurry of strikes came fast, and one of them finally landed - cutting across Connor's abdomen. The pain was immediate, sharp, and deep. Blood poured from the wound, but Connor forced himself to focus.
			With a roar, he swung his longblade, the strike strong enough to send a shockwave through the Judge's defenses. The creature blocked the attack, but Connor grinned. It was a feint. He thrusted his shortblade forward, burying it deep into the Judge's abdomen.
			But the Judge didn't falter. His grin only grew wider as he grabbed Connor's blade and pushed it out, his other hand moving faster than Connor could react. In a single fluid motion, the Judge morphed his blades into a spear, thrusting it toward Connor. The weapon drove into his abdomen with brutal force.
			Connor grabbed the spear, pulling himself toward the Judge with a snarl. He morphed blades from his wrists, slashing at the Judge's face. The strike connected, cutting deep, but the Judge simply grinned. He twisted the spear, and Connor felt the blade tear through his insides, sending shockwaves of agony through his body.
			For the first time since starting his quest, real, primal fear crept into Connor's hearts. The blood loss, the agony, the damage...
			Thoughts flooded his mind. His friends. His pack. He couldn't die here. Not like this.
			The Judge morphed his spear back into twin blades, spinning them in the air like a tornado of death. Connor tried to stand his ground, but his legs betrayed him. He was on the edge of collapse.
			Then, with a deafening howl, Connor's eyes flashed red. Rage. The bloodlust took over, drowning out the pain, drowning out the fear. His body surged with raw power, and his vision turned crimson.
			The Judge wiped blood from his mouth, his grin widening. "Now... Now it's a fight." he muttered, his own eyes flashing red with a sudden, dangerous fury. He un-morphed his blades, drawing wristblades in their place.
			The two monsters collided again. Their wristblades clashed in a shower of gore, neither one attempting to block - only strike. Blood splattered across the alley as their bodies were torn. For a moment, the Judge stumbled, his left hand pressing against the stab wound Connor inflicted earlier. But his grin only grew fiercer, and his eyes glowed red.
			For a split second, Connor's mind cleared. "He can Rage too?" The thought barely registered before his feral instincts took over once more. The two continued to clash, a blur of violence and blood.
			The Judge hit harder than anyone Connor had faced before. Each strike felt like it could shatter bone, and Connor was barely able to stay on his feet. But he fought through the pain, launching a haymaker that connected with the Judge's ribcage. He felt something crack beneath his fist.
			For a moment, the Judge faltered, his breath ragged. He straightened, his body obeying his will with terrifying precision.
			Connor scowled, his chest heaving.
			Normally, the acid spit was a good attack. Enemies never expected it, and had no means of preventing it.
			Against one of your own kind, though? One wise to the trick?
			Suicide.
			The Judge swiped, his blade slashing across Connor's throat with terrifying precision. The acid spilled out of the impromptu tracheotomy, hissing as it burned down his chest. Before he could react, the Judge grabbed his tongue, yanking it out with a sickening pull.
			Then, in one fluid motion, the Judge re-morphed his spear, driving it through Connor's chest.
			Connor howled, the sound tearing from his chest as the spear twisted, shredding his lungs. Blood poured from him in torrents as the Judge raised the spear into the air, a triumphant roar echoing in the alley. His left heart was completely punched out, and his right was horribly mangled to the point of unusability.
			With a brutal, final motion, the Judge drove the spear into the ground, impaling Connor like a trophy.
			Connor's limp body slumped down, blood pooling around him. The Judge stood over him, his eyes returning to their cold, fanatical calm. He chuckled, the sound dark and victorious. He placed a hand on Connor's chin, almost gently.
			"You fought well, youngblood. Though you squander the gifts of the Great One... you fought well."
			Connor tried to speak, to roar, to spit. Something.
			"Shh..." the Judge replied, again with a horrifyingly gentle tone. "Don't be ashamed. You did your best. Nothing that happens after today is your fault."
			Again, another death-rattle came out of Connor's bloody mouth.
			"Hush, now, youngblood." the Judge smiled - not savagely, but warmly. "Go in peace."

			With that, the Judge rose, bowed, and left.
			Connor's limp, apparently lifeless body slid down the spear, making a sickening *squelch* as it hit the ground.
			Must hold on. Must hold on.
			Every cell in Connor's body screamed. Every nerve ending begged him to just let them die.
			Must hold on. Must hold on.
			Lungs ruined. No oxygen. Only a torn half-heart for circulation.
			Must hold on. Must hold on.
			Bleeding from every organ. Brain... shutting down...
			Must... hold on...
			Hold... On...

	EPISODE - Broken Hearts and Bones

		SCENE
			It was early hours of the 10th of October, 1996. 03:27 AM.

			The moon was a waning crescent - nearly new.

			No matter how much he wants to.

			Vince's car swerved into the hospital car park, narrowly missing a bollard. Without bothering to straighten into the lines, he burst out of his door, and sprinted like a blur over to the passenger side. He swung the door open, nearly taking it off its hinges, and pulled his sister Laura from the seat.

			"Vince..." she whispered through ragged breaths.
			"Shh..." he replied, carrying her to the hospital entrance. "You'll be alright..."
			He made it to the door, kicked it open, and screamed for help.

			Just over an hour had passed.
			Specifically, it was now 04:42 AM. The clouds had begun to draw in, and the rain was becoming a little stronger. The moon peeked out through the clouds, as though it was too scared to watch.
			Vince anxiously paced the hospital corridors, as Laura's screams echoed in his skull. A nurse approached him, her face pale.
			"M-mister Barrett?" she asked.
			"Is she okay?" he hurriedly answered, rushing over.
			"We... Laura appears to be suffering from systemic organ failure, and extreme hyperthermia - a condition we've been calling hypermetabolic shock."
			"What?" he asked, white as a sheet. "Wh-what does that mean?"
			"In simple terms, her metabolism has spiked to unprecedented levels. She can't take in enough oxygen to keep up with the burn, causing a dangerous buildup of lactic acid across her body. Worse, she's experiencing a massive rise in body temperature - her core temp is currently 41.3°C, and rising still. Her blood pressure has also grown, causing clots to form in the lungs, andd near the brain, causing a cerebral infarction - a stroke."
			"Oh, God..." Vince whispered in shock. "What... what about the baby?"
			"From the tests we've run, the baby isn't suffering from any of these conditions." the nurse began unsurely. "But as long as he's inside her womb, he's being exposed to the severe temperatures, and her blood chemistry is becoming dangerously acidic."
			"...'he?'" Vince gasped.
			A boy. A baby boy.
			She'd kept the gender secret, even from herself.
			She should be the one to know this. Not him.
			Not him.
			"Mr. Barrett?" the nurse cut in, shaking him from the fog of pain.
			"Is... is there anything you can do?" h finally whispered.
			"At the moment, we have two options." she began. "We can provide her with medication to help bring down her body temperature and blood pressure, giving us time to treat the underlying hypermetabolsim. However, this medication... it's never been used in a live birth before. At the doses we're using, it would most likely cross the placenta... and be toxic to the baby."
			Vince ran his hands through his hair.
			"Our other option... would be to perform a C-section right away, and try to save the baby. But the additional blood loss, and the time it would take... Laura would most likely die."
			Vince agonised over the choice for less than a second. It felt like hours.
			"Save her." he nodded, closing his eyes.
			"Are you sure?" the nurse asked.
			"I'm sure. Save her. Please..." he begged.
			The nurse nodded, and left.
			He leaned against a wall, and hit it with the back of his head.
			She would damn him for his choice. Hate him for it.
			So be it. She'd be alive to do those things, at least.

			27 minutes passed. Vince rose swiftly as the nurse returned.
			"I..." she began, struggling to find the words. "I'm so sorry, Mr. Barrett."
			"No..." he whispered, burying his face in his hands.
			"We did everything we could, but... Laura didn't make it."
			The words echoed in his brain.
			Years went by in a single breath.
			"Can I... Can I see her, please?" he finally asked.
			"Of course." the nurse nodded, ushering him into her room.
			He sat by her side, and squeezed her hand. She was pale and still.
			Vince had always assumed that people would look peaceful in death. But she didn't. Her face was still slightly contorted from the pain. Her skin was pale, cold, and damp to the touch - a disturbing contrast to the searing red hours before.
			Small pools of thick fluid remained dotted around her skin, as though she'd sweated them out. A pinkish foam remained near her lips.
			Vince wept. He howled in pain and sorrow.
			He rested his hand on her abdomen, and...
			He felt movement.
			Kicking. Punching. Flailing, perhaps.
			Dead. Supposed to be dead.
			Alive. Alive?
			Alive.
			"NURSE!" he screamed.

			13 minutes had passed, and the nurse arrived - carrying a newborn baby.
			Vince took him into his arms. He looked into the little one's eyes. Icy, steel grey. Pale skin.
			He had his mother's brow. A tiny, reddish-blonde fuzz sat atop his scalp.
			"I know this has been a lot to take in..." the nurse began.
			"I thought he'd've died..." Vince whispered, still in shock.
			"He's very strong." the nurse smiled proudly. "Did you... did you have any idea what name you'd like to use?"
			Vince paused for a moment.
			"She said... if it were a boy, she'd call him Connor."
			"Connor." the nurse smiled. "It suits him."
			She wrote down, placed down a milk bottle, and nodded. "I'll give you both some time. If you need us, ring the bell."
			"Thank you..." Vince nodded back, his voice hoarse.
			He held Connor, and gently stroked his head.
			"Hey, my lad..." he whispered softly. Connor gurgled slightly, half-asleep. Vince passed the milk bottle up to his mouth.
			Connor turned his head, as though trying to avoid it.
			"Hey, buddy... come on, you need it." he whispered again.
			Connor still rejected it, his face scrunching.
			"Hey... I'm sorry..." he sobbed softly. "I know, it should be her..."
			Tears streamed down Vince's face, dropping onto Connor's.
			"Sorry, mate..." he whispered, wiping Connor's face. Connor reached up, his eyes clenched shut, and grabbed Vince's beard, before yanking.
			"Ow!" Vince exclaimed in surprise, before chuckling. "You're a feisty one, eh?"
			Connor, being a baby, didn't reply - but Vince could've sworn he was grinning.
			He pulled him closer, leaning back so Connor could rest on his chest.
			"Shh, shh..." he whispered as he rocked him slowly. He offered the milk bottle once more, and this time, Connor took it.
			"Good lad..." he smiled warmly.

		Getting Connor to A&E
		______________________________
		SCENE
			Chloe and Ivan sat in the car together, driving to the hospital. Chloe was frantically going through her research notes on her laptop while Ivan drove.

I'm comparing that to the data we found on the clones in the facility. It looks like, when Connor's cells are deprived of oxygen, they enter a dormant state - and also, they can use anaerobic respiration to keep working where needed, but it's slower, and the lactic acid buildup can eventually kill them. According to this, when one clone's lungs became unviable from the cancers, it still continued to be active for 5 days until it finally died." she explained.

They use a backup system to keep things running, but it's inefficient. The downside is that it leads to a buildup of toxins that can eventually kill the cells.]" she said nonchalantly.

Thankfully, the lower pair were in workable condition - the upper pair, however, were like shredded balloons. Another set of stitches covered his windpipes.

		Connor's recovery

		SCENE

Your body kept almost rinsing your head with it - thank god it did, or you'd have had a seizure, or a stroke. In fact, I think this substance is what put you in the healing coma."

			"EEGs showed you were in severe pain - so we tried giving you anaesthetics, but your body just metabolised them instantly. It's all a part of this intracellular communication you seem to have - your body recognises when a substance has foreign origins, and immediately moves to neutralise, expel, or digest it. But..."

So I cooked up a high enough dose, and that seemed to calm you down a notch. Slight problem though - it's brought your paradrenaline way down. I'd need to synthesise more if you wanted to use your Rage."

			"Yes - in a couple hours, I could make a full dose."

			"Yeah, absolutely. I'll crack on now." Chloe said, brushing away her tears and squaring her shoulders.
			Connor rose, a soft smile breaking through the pain on his face. He pulled Chloe into a hug, holding her tightly. She returned the embrace, not wanting it to end.
			She swallowed hard, resting her forehead against his. "Rest while you can. I'll handle this."
			Connor nodded, stepping back. As he laid back down, Chloe sat at her makeshift lab station, her hands trembling for only a moment before she steadied them. She glanced back at him, then down at her notes. Her jaw set with quiet determination.

		Connor wakes up
		______________________________
		SCENE
			The Riverside Squad stood on a junction in the night-time, ready for war.
			Ivan adjusted Isabella's scope, and checked her ammunition. Gwen's eyes flexed violet as she made a dust devil at the ground, readying her powers. Amy's gauntlets crackled as she drew the Pulsar and the Vibroblade, holding them like a pirate holds a flintlock and cutlass.
			Connor and Sparky, meanwhile, felt their costumes ripple and morph with fury. Connor reached to his belt, checking the two metal syringes attached.
			Then, a black car pulled up to the group. They readied their weapons, as Naismith stepped out.

His mask was fully torn off.

			He looked down.
			No.
			Can't be.
			Another trick.
			Or he was going mad.
			"Help me..." Junior begged again.
			Connor sank to his knees.

Buildings had been shattered, hundreds of bodies strewn across, and enough blood to feed a vampire for years. The snow was falling a little heavier now - white flurries melting as they sank into hot pools of gore.

			"Dig a trench, Dr. Zhao. And make it a deep one. I suspect, after today... things are going to get a whole lot worse."

"When I was in your shoes, I hit a man in the chin, and the cops thought I'd used a shotgun. *That's* what you are now. I send you after some Skulls, you'll end up killing them. I send you after Super-Agents, they'll make a chewtoy out of you."

			"I'll go get Vince and Phil." Bea nodded. "See you out there!"
			Amy waved her off, and headed outside with Shannon.

			The Kestrel's engines slowly stopped roaring as she landed in the Riverside car park. The pilot made sure to land her in the lines of a parking bay, grinning as the landing pods folded out.
			The back door swung downwards, and the humans of Riverside looked up as the squad stepped out.
			"Hey!" Amy smiled, hugging Connor.
			"Whoa, hey!" he grinned. "Where's Amy, and what have you done with her?"
			"Shut up, fuckface."
			"*There* she is!"
			"Good to see you, lad." Vince beamed.
			"Hey, dad!" Trey cheered, hugging Phil.
			"Hey, my boy..." Phil embraced him.
			"Hi guys! How was the city while we were away?" asked Sparky.
			"Not bad, bud!" Shannon smiled. "Amy did good."
			Bea and Chloe didn't speak - they just hugged, melting into it.
			"Wait a sec..." Amy looked up, as Ivan, Bevan, and the final passenger disembarked.
			The Judge rolled their shoulders, taking a deep breath of air.
			Amy ripped the Pulsar from her belt, and fired.
			"Amy, no!" Connor barked. Too late.
			The Judge's eyes blazed crimson. They snarled, but placed their hands on their face, and took a calming breath.
			"Youngblood. Good reflexes, I'll admit." they grinned.
			"What the *FUCK* is he doing here?!" Amy growled.
			"Uh--they. They're on our side now." Trey quickly added.
			"...WHAT?!"
			"Let's talk inside." Connor beckoned. "Amy?"
			She held the Pulsar, still aimed at their chest - but relented, and headed in.
			Connor approached the Judge.
			"That one fears me." they somberly noted.
			"Can you blame her? You punched a hole through her brother's chest, and sicced a bunch of Super-Agents on her."
			They looked away. "They have a warrior's heart, to attack me like that."
			"Yeah... she really does." Connor nodded. "Anyway... you'll be staying here. At least one of us will be watching you at all times. Remember my terms."
			"I did not save your life just to end it later, youngblood." they cocked an eyebrow. "You will find no quarrel with me."
			"Good."

			"...so, the Judge is what, our secret alien dad?!" Amy tilted her head.
			"That's... well, it's a bit more complicated, but kinda?" Chloe shrugged. "Their blood was used as the first super-serum on Earth. I suspect it was implanted in-vivo to you three."
			"So they're the one that killed my Kerry..." Phil growled.
			"The Optimates killed her, dad." Trey said softly. "And now the Judge wants to kill them."
			"For now, we make sure at least one of us is with them." Chloe sighed. "From what I can tell though, they're an alien of their word."
			Vince stroked his beard.

			It was late, now. The Judge had been given a motel room to crash in - one with very obvious cameras, and remote-controlled gas canisters. They scoffed, but took their place.
			They began making a sign with their hands - a prayer - before cursing and taking a seat. They ran their hands over their scalp.
			"False one... false one..." they whispered, shaking back and forth.
			"Oi." a voice called out. They looked up.
			"You resemble Connorbarrett." they nodded. "Are you of their genestock?"
			"If that's how aliens ask 'are you family,' then yes." Vince growled, stepping forward.
			"What do you want, human?" they tilted their head.
			"My nephew... he's a good boy. He's got a big heart. The one you stabbed him in." he began, with the devil in his eye. "You hurt him. Badly. Now he may be willing to let that slide, but I'm not."
			"Oh? What do you intend to do?"
			Vince's lip curled. "If you hurt him again... if you dare to touch a hair on his head... I'll kill you. I don't care what planet you're from, or how strong you are. *I will kill you.*"
			The Judge's brow furrowed at the insult. They scanned him up and down, before bowing their head in respect.
			"I believe you."
			Vince nodded firmly, and left. The Judge leaned back, and closed their eyes, deep in thought.
