			"RAAAGH!" Connor roared, his fist crashing through the air and landing squarely in Trey's chest.
			Trey let out a wheeze, before sending a stab to Connor's gut. He pulled back, but just barely, and the skin broke.
			Trey grinned, and pressed his attack. He sent a spinning kick that smacked aside Connor's head, dazing him - before a backflip that kicked him upside the chin.
			Connor snarled, and charged forwards. He wrapped Trey in a bear hug, and squeezed tightly.
			As Trey's bones cracked, he let out a savage growl. He was dazed, but not done. With an explosion of force, he broke free.
			He spinned, kicking Connor in the backside and rising. The two clenched their fists, and struck - both hands crashing into each other. They felt their bones finally break, and stumbled forward, their heads knocking into each other. Their crimson eyes met, and both leaned back, before a headbutt so strong it shook the air around them. Finally, they both collapsed, bloodied and broken.
			"Pathetic." the Judge sneered, arms folded. "*These* are the heroes of Earth?"
			"Hey, fuck you." Connor panted, staggering to his knees. "We lasted ten minutes - that's more than you did."
			"Very funny, youngblood." they tutted. "At least the Wolf shows promise."
			Sparky stumbled into view, before falling to the ground. "Yeah... the Judge doesn't pull their punches in training."
			"Nor should I. The purpose of training is to harden your body and strengthen your soul."
			"Jesus..." Trey chuckled. "And I thought *your* training regimen was a lot."

			Chloe peered through the microscope, looking at the Judge's tissue samples.
			"Anything I can do to help?" asked Bea.
			She smiled. "I'm okay. Just trying to figure out how their biology works."
			"Anything interesting?"
			Chloe chuckled. "A lot. I've found plenty of analogues for terrestrial proteins - overall, Golgothan DNA seems to follow the same rules as humans. There are a few differences though - for example, Golgothans have hyperactive scar tissue. Berserkers can heal scars, but regular Golgothans must be covered in them by the time they get old. Which isn't long, as their telomeres are on the shorter side - again, being a Berserker means that's not a problem, but based on my estimations, a Golgothan probably doesn't live much longer than 50 years."
			Bea nodded her head, intrigued. "That must be pretty lonely, then. Being the only long-lived person in your entire society."
			Chloe paused. "That explains a lot about the Judge, actually. It definitely explains why they were so willing to throw their lot in with us."
			At that, Amy came in, wearing a patient's gown.
			"All done?" Chloe asked.
			"Ugh..." she groaned. "I've never had a CT scan before, and I don't intend to have another."
			"There'll be one more, once we've got your powers working." Chloe smiled. "I'm gonna pick the Judge's brains later on how all *that* works."
			Amy sighed softly.
			"What's wrong?" Bea asked.
			"N-nothing."
			"Amy..." she pressed.
			She sighed again, sitting down.
			"You don't want them?" Chloe tilted her head.
			"It's not that. It's... the Judge. How after everything they did, we're all supposed to just let them into our lives now."
			Chloe gave a sympathetic smile. "I know. I'll admit, I'm not too happy having them around. But... Connor's right. We need all the help we can get. And they've kept to their word - if they wanted to attack, they could've."
			"I know." Amy leaned back. "But I still hate them."
			Bea gently brushed her arm. At that, the Berserkers came back in.
			"Hey, guys." Connor groaned, stretching.
			"Jesus." Bea shuddered, catching their bruises. "What happened?"
			"Training." Trey nodded. "The Judge says that we get stronger over time if we get hurt, so we stopped pulling our punches."
			"I hope we get stronger soon." Sparky chuckled, flopping onto the floor.
			"The results will take time." the Judge nodded. "Go and rest. You will feel better in the morning."
			"Can't. There's patrols that need doing." Connor began.
			"Then I shall watch your city." the Judge bowed his head. "Do not fear, I shall honour your terms."
			"You're not gonna let that thing *actually* go on patrol, right?" Amy scowled. "They killed people! Strung them up by their guts!"
			"Amy's right." Connor nodded. "I don't want you patrolling unsupervised until I can be sure you're not gonna go too far."
			The Judge's face contorted slightly, but they relented, and turned to Amy. "Perhaps, then, I can be supervised by you?"
			Amy scoffed. "You might've pulled the wool over Connor's eyes, but there's no way in hell I'm trusting you."
			"Amy..." Connor said softly.
			"No." she snapped. "You're the leader or whatever, so you can do what you want. But I'm *not* going *anywhere* with them."
			The Judge hesitated, but then had an idea. "You are aware of our vulnerability to certain noises, yes?"
			Amy tilted her head, as they grabbed an earpiece.
			"Have your Fabricator modify this device such that it can deliver those frequencies. If you disapprove of my actions, activate it. I will be incapacitated and at your mercy - and electricity is another thing we are weak to. Use your shock-pistol to further stun me, and claim my head with your blade."
			"You'd... willingly make yourself vulnerable like that?" Connor cocked an eyebrow.
			"I am... unused to human customs. But I can tell that your trust is earned." they bowed their head again.
			Amy hesitated. "You so much as look at me funny, and I'm mounting your head on a wall."
			"Understood. Jazh korahl i'Rezuul."
			"I serve at your command." Connor muttered in translation. "Up to you, sis."
			She looked the alien up and down, and sighed.
			"Fine."
